Declan shifted in his seat, still trying to wrap his head around it. Living with Kyle Barnes. Having breakfast across the table from the guy who used to light it up in the league. It was a lot to take in.
Kyle let out a soft chuckle, picking up on the hesitation in Declan’s eyes. “It’s a lot to process, huh?”
Declan didn’t answer, but the look on his face said enough. He watched Kyle carefully, the weight of it all pressing in.
Kyle leaned back in his chair, settling into a more relaxed posture, but his eyes stayed sharp and knowing. “I’ve been where you’re sitting. New town. New team. Big pressure. It can mess with your head if you let it.”
tgt_seg:
德克兰在座位上挪动，仍然试图理解这一切。与凯尔·巴恩斯同住。与在联盟里经常给他点烟的那个人一起吃早餐。这太难以接受了。
凯尔轻轻地笑了笑，注意到德克兰眼神中的犹豫。“这太难以理解了，对吧？”
德克兰没有回答，但他的表情已经说明了一切。他紧紧地盯着凯尔，这一切的重量压在他身上。
凯尔靠在椅子上，放松了姿势，但他的眼神依然犀利而明了。“我也经历过你现在的处境。新城镇。新球队。压力很大。如果你让它影响你，它会搞乱你的思绪。”

src_seg:
Declan’s mind flickered through every worry he’d been carrying since stepping off that bus. Was Kyle reading him that easily? It felt like he was peeling back layers without even trying. That low, familiar buzz of uncertainty crept up again, and somehow, Kyle seemed to catch it without a word.
“I know it’s not easy, kid.” Kyle gave a small, almost fatherly sigh. His voice was lower now; gentle, but steady. “But here’s the thing. If you stay with us, you’re not just crashing at a billet house. I’m offering you space to breathe. A place to land when everything else feels like it’s spinning.”
tgt_seg:
德克兰的脑子里闪过他从那辆公交车上下来后一直担忧的每一个问题。凯尔读懂了他吗？感觉他像剥洋葱一样毫不费力地剥开了他的层层防御。那低沉、熟悉的不确定感又一次悄然爬上心头，凯尔似乎不用说一句话就已经捕捉到了。
“我知道这不容易，孩子。”凯尔轻轻叹了口气，声音低了下来，温柔而坚定。“但你要明白，如果你留下来，你不是在一个简陋的旅店里住宿。我在这里给你一个呼吸的空间。一个让你在一切都像在旋转的时候都能找到落脚的地方。”

src_seg:
Declan felt his throat tighten. Like the room had gone still for a second.
“Hockey’s a hell of a ride,” Kyle went on, “and yeah, I’ll push you. But I’ll have your back every step of the way. This isn’t just about stats or ice time, it’s about becoming the kind of player, the kind of person, who can handle the long haul. And I’ve been through the trenches. I know what that takes.”
He folded his arms casually, the edge in his voice softening into something more inviting. “It’s a big decision, I get that. So here’s what I’m thinking, you crash with us tonight. No pressure. See the house, meet Nicole and Ryan. Feel it out. Then tomorrow, if it feels right, we’ll talk.”
tgt_seg:
Declan 感到喉咙紧张。就像房间在短暂的一瞬间静止了。
“冰球真是太刺激了，” Kyle 继续说，“当然，我会给你加油。但我会一直支持你。这不仅仅是关于数据或上场时间，而是关于成为一个能够坚持下来的球员，成为一个能够坚持下来的人。我经历过战火纷飞的岁月。我知道这需要什么。”
他随意地把胳膊搭在胸前，声音的锋芒被软化成更具邀请性的语气。“这是一个大决定，我明白。所以我想，你今晚和我们一起去吧。不用担心压力。看看房子，见见 Nicole 和 Ryan。试试看。然后明天，如果感觉合适，我们再谈。”

src_seg:
Declan didn’t even realize he was nodding until the motion was halfway done.
Something about the way Kyle spoke; calm, direct, like he actually got it. It cut through the usual static in Declan’s brain. He didn’t know what was happening, not really. Just that, for some reason, this guy already had a kind of hold on him. Not in a forced way. Just…steady. Solid. Like someone who meant what he said and wouldn’t flake the second things got hard.
No adult had ever made him feel that before. Not a teacher. Not a coach. Not even his own dad.
tgt_seg:
德克兰甚至没有意识到自己在点头，直到动作已经完成了一半。
凯尔说话的方式让德克兰有些不知所措；平静、直接，仿佛他真的明白了。这打破了德克兰脑海中通常的杂乱。他不知道发生了什么，真的不知道。只是，出于某种原因，这家伙已经在某种程度上控制了他。不是强制性的方式。只是……稳稳的。坚定的。就像一个说话算话的人，不会在事情变得艰难时就放弃。
从来没有成年人让他感到过这种感觉。不是老师。不是教练。甚至连他自己的爸爸也没有。

src_seg:
So yeah, maybe he wasn’t sure about any of this, but his head kept nodding anyway.
“Okay,” he said finally. “I’ll give it a shot.”
Luc and Kyle exchanged a quick smile, something quiet and satisfied passing between them.
"Great!" Luc said, his enthusiasm palpable. He leaned forward, a spark in his eyes. "Any questions or anything on your mind before you head out to practice?"
Declan paused, the question hanging in the air for a moment. He glanced between Luc and Kyle, then shook his head. "I think I’m good for now."
"Alright, go ahead and get settled in," Luc said, standing up and motioning toward the hallway. "Locker room's down the hall to the right. Your name’s on one of the stalls, and your gear's already waiting for you."
tgt_seg:
所以，也许他对这一切都不太确定，但他的头还是点了点。
“好吧，”他终于说。“我试试看。”
卢克和凯尔交换了一下眼神，眼神中充满了安静的满足感。
“太好了！”卢克说，他的热情溢于言表。他向前倾了倾身子，眼中闪烁着光芒。“有什么问题或什么在你心里吗，你要出去练习之前？”
德克兰停顿了一下，问题悬挂在空中片刻。他看了看卢克和凯尔，然后摇了摇头。“我觉得我现在就行了。”
“好吧，那就去安顿一下吧，”卢克站起来，向走廊方向示意。“更衣室就在右边的走廊。你的名字在一个隔间上，你的装备已经在那里等着你了。”

src_seg:
Declan rose to his feet, clutching the duffel a little tighter.
Luc gave him a nod. “Practice starts in twenty. Coach Reynolds will meet you on the ice.”
Kyle stood too, that same calm energy still radiating off him. “I’ll see you after. Nicole’s making chicken parm tonight. Hope you’re hungry.”
Declan gave a half-smile without meaning to. “Yeah. Sounds good.”
And with that, he turned and headed for the hallway, trying not to overthink the million things racing through his head.
Practice flew by in a blur of crisp passes, sharp turns, and the unmistakable rush that only came when his skates hit fresh ice. Declan didn’t need time to adjust to that, his instincts kicked in from the first drill. It wasn’t long before heads were turning and quiet nods of approval passed between coaches.
tgt_seg:
德克兰站起来，紧紧抓住行李袋。
卢克向他点了点头。“训练在 20 点开始。教练雷诺兹会在冰上见你。”
凯尔也站起来，依然散发着平静的能量。“我在后面见你。妮可今晚做鸡肉帕玛森。希望你饿了。”
德克兰半笑着，没有想到。“是的。听起来不错。”
说完，他转身走向走廊，试图不去想脑子里飞速奔跑的无数事情。
训练在清晰的传球、急转弯和只有在冰刀触碰新冰时才有的那种不可思议的冲击中飞快地过去了。德克兰不需要时间来适应这种感觉，他的本能在第一项练习时就发挥了作用。不久，教练们的头转向了他，传来了低声的点头。

src_seg:
It felt good. Easy. Like slipping into something that had always fit.
The locker room buzzed with post-practice energy; snapping tape, the thud of gear hitting benches, and a steady stream of chirps flying from stall to stall.
“Not bad for the new guy,” one of the defensemen called, grinning as he peeled off his jersey. 
Declan smirked as he unstrapped his pads. “Figured I’d show up, impress a little, then humble you tomorrow.”
A few guys let out loud “Oooohs,” one of them chucking a rolled-up sock at him.
As he dodged the sock, Declan caught Ryan watching him from across the room. Not in a hostile way, just…quietly. Studying. Like he was still deciding what to make of him.
tgt_seg:
感觉很好。很容易。就像穿上一直合身的衣服一样。
更衣室里充满了练习后的活力；胶带咔嚓作响，装备砸到凳子上发出沉闷的声音，以及从一个隔间到另一个隔间不断传来的啁啾声。
“对新来的不错，”一名防守队员笑着脱下球衣说。
德克兰眨了眨眼，解下护具。“我想先亮亮相，给大家留下点印象，然后明天就让大家服服帖帖。”
几个人发出大声的“哦哦”声，其中一人把卷起的袜子扔向他。
当他躲过了袜子时，德克兰注意到瑞恩从对面房间看着他。不是以敌对的方式，只是……安静地。在研究。就像他还在考虑如何对待他一样。

src_seg:
Before Declan could read into it, Ryan stood, tugged his hoodie over damp hair, and headed out without a word.
The rest of the guys were still laughing and joking around, but that moment stuck.
Declan finished peeling off his gear and slung the duffel over his shoulder. When he stepped out into the hallway, he spotted them; Kyle and Ryan, standing just outside the rink doors. Kyle’s hand rested on his son’s shoulder, his voice low and calm, the kind of tone only a dad could pull off.
Ryan nodded at something, eyes on the ground. Declan didn’t catch what was said, but he could tell instantly that they were close. Really close.
tgt_seg:
Declan还没来得及读懂，Ryan就站起来，把湿透的头发裹在连帽衫里，一言不发地出去了。
其他人还在笑闹，但那一刻让人印象深刻。
Declan把装备卸下，把背包搭在肩上。走到走廊时，他看到了他们：Kyle和Ryan站在冰场门口。Kyle的手放在儿子的肩上，声音低沉而平稳，只有爸爸才能有这样的语气。
Ryan对着什么点了点头，眼睛盯着地面。Declan没听到他们说了什么，但他立刻就能感觉到他们关系很亲密。真的很亲密。

src_seg:
It hit him in a way he didn’t expect.
Kyle glanced up and spotted Declan, a smile already forming as he lifted a hand in an easy wave. “There he is. You survive your first Coach Luc practice?”
Declan nodded, catching up to them. “Barely,” he said, though the grin tugging at the corner of his mouth gave him away.
Ryan gave him a short glance, but didn’t say much. Just gave a subtle nod, then walked ahead toward the parking lot.
“Come on,” Kyle said, clapping a hand gently on Declan’s back. “Let’s get you home.”
Home. The word sounded weird in his head. But as he followed them to the car, something in his chest loosened, just a little.
tgt_seg:
他没有想到会这样。
凯尔抬头一看，就看到了德克兰，他已经露出了笑容，轻松地挥了挥手。“他来了。你在教练卢克的第一次练习中存活下来了吗？”
德克兰点了点头，赶上他们。“勉强吧，”他说，嘴角露出笑容，露出了他的真实想法。
瑞恩简短地看了他一眼，但没有说什么。只是点了点头，然后朝停车场走去。
“来吧，”凯尔轻轻拍了拍德克兰的背。“我们送你回家。”
家。这个词在他的脑海里听起来很奇怪。但当他跟着他们走向车子时，胸口有些松动，只是松动了一点。

src_seg:
The car ride was quiet in a way Declan hadn’t realized he’d been craving. No one asked him questions or tried to fill the silence with small talk. Ryan had earbuds in, staring out his window. Kyle kept one hand on the wheel, the other resting casually on the console, humming now and then to the classic rock playing softly through the speakers.
Declan leaned his head against the window and watched the world roll by. The narrow roads wound through thick trees brushed with the first touches of fall; burnt oranges, deep reds, and gold. It was nothing like the city. The quiet felt intentional here. Peaceful.
tgt_seg:
车里的安静让德克兰意识到自己一直在渴望。没有人问他问题，也没有人试图用闲聊来填补寂静。瑞恩戴着耳机，凝视着车窗外。凯尔把一只手放在方向盘上，另一只手随意地放在中控台上，偶尔哼着从扬声器里轻轻传出的经典摇滚乐。
德克兰把头靠在车窗上，看着世界从车窗外飞驰而过。狭窄的道路穿过被秋天第一缕阳光抚摸过的密密层层的树林；烧焦的橙色、深红色和金色。这里与城市完全不同。这里的安静是有意为之的。宁静祥和。

src_seg:
He hadn’t noticed any of this from the bus, just the ache in his back and the buzz of nerves. But now…now it didn’t seem so bad.
The car turned off the main road and onto a quiet, tree-lined street, the tires humming softly against the worn asphalt. Declan glanced out the window, taking in the quaint homes tucked into the hillsides, most with wide porches and tidy yards. Everything felt still out here, like the whole world had taken a breath and held it.
They pulled into a modest driveway in front of a two-story house with deep blue siding and white trim. Warm yellow light glowed from the windows, casting a soft welcome as twilight settled over the neighborhood.
tgt_seg:
他从公交车上并没有注意到这些，只有背部的疼痛和神经的紧张。但现在……现在似乎不那么糟糕了。
汽车从主路转入一条安静的、树木成荫的街道，轮胎轻轻地在磨损的沥青上嗡嗡作响。德克兰从车窗往外看，看到了隐藏在山坡上的那些可爱的房子，大多数都有宽敞的门廊和整洁的院子。这里的一切都显得静谧，就像整个世界屏住了呼吸。
他们停在一个两层楼房的简朴车道前，房屋的侧面是深蓝色的，有白色装饰。黄色的温暖光芒从窗户中闪烁，随着黄昏的降临，整个社区都洋溢着温馨的气氛。

src_seg:
Kyle eased the car into park, the soft hum of the engine cutting through the quiet of the evening. He turned to look at Declan with a small smile. “This is us. Home sweet home,” he said, his tone light but with a quiet certainty, as if he were laying down an unspoken promise.
Declan didn’t answer, but he opened the door and stepped out. The air smelled faintly of pine and chimney smoke. Calmer than anything he’d felt in weeks.
Ryan was already unlocking the front door, his silhouette framed by the porch light.
Kyle gave Declan’s shoulder a gentle tap before heading up the steps. “Come on. Nicole’s got dinner waiting, and she’s been asking about you all day.”
tgt_seg:
凯尔轻轻将车停入停车位，引擎的柔和轰鸣声穿透了夜晚的宁静。他转向德克兰，脸上带着一丝微笑。“这就是我们。家，甜蜜的家，”他轻声说道，语气轻快，但带着一种低声许下的承诺。
德克兰没有回答，只是打开车门，走了出去。空气中隐约散发着松树和烟囱的烟味。比他几周来感受过的任何事情都要平静。
瑞恩已经在解锁前门，他的剪影被门廊的灯光映照。
凯尔轻轻拍了拍德克兰的肩膀，然后开始上楼梯。“来吧。尼科尔已经准备好晚餐了，她整天都在问你。”

src_seg:
The door swung open with a quiet creak, and warm air spilled out into the cool evening, carrying the unmistakable smell of garlic and tomato sauce. Declan stepped inside behind Kyle, the hardwood floors smooth under his sneakers and the house glowing with soft, ambient light that gave it a lived-in, welcoming feel.
“Hi!” a voice called from the kitchen. A moment later, a woman stepped out, wiping her hands on a dish towel. She was tall, athletic, with a sharp but warm energy that instantly filled the space. “You must be Declan.”
Declan hesitated for a moment, caught in the awkwardness of the moment. He nodded, unsure whether to wave or offer a handshake, his mind scrambling for a response. “Uh, yeah. Hi.”
tgt_seg:
门轻轻吱吱作响地打开了，暖气从凉爽的夜晚中溢出，带着无法混淆的蒜和番茄酱的香味。凯尔后面，迪克兰走了进来，硬木地板在他的运动鞋下滑顺，房子在柔和的环境光下闪耀，散发出一种居住过的、温馨的感觉。
“嗨！”厨房里传来一声声音。片刻之后，一个女人走了出来，用餐巾擦干了手。她身材高挑，健美，散发着锐利而温暖的气息，立刻充满了空间。“你一定是迪克兰。”
迪克兰犹豫了一下，被这个时刻的不自然感所困扰。他点了点头，不确定是挥手还是握手，他的脑子里乱成一团，不知道该如何回应。“嗯，是的。你好。”

src_seg:
Before he could say anything else, Nicole stepped forward, her arms open in a welcoming embrace. She pulled him into a hug without missing a beat.
“It’s so nice to meet you!” she said, rubbing his back gently in a motherly way before pulling back from the hug. “I’m Nicole. Hope you’re hungry, I made chicken parm. It’s a family favorite.”
“Yeah…starving, actually.”
Ryan had already disappeared upstairs, his footsteps fading above them, leaving the three of them in the open kitchen and living room. Declan took in the house. Family photos lined the walls, the dining table was half-set, and the smell from the kitchen was enough to make his stomach growl. Everything felt grounded, like people lived here and liked living here.
tgt_seg:
妮可没有说话，就向前迈进，双臂张开，热情地拥抱他。她毫不犹豫地把他紧紧地抱在怀里。
“见到你真是太高兴了！”她轻轻地抚摸着他的背，像母亲一样，然后松开了手。“我是妮可。希望你饿了，我做了鸡帕玛。这是家里的拿手菜。”
“是的……饿死了。”
瑞恩已经消失在楼上，他的脚步声渐渐消失，只留下三个人在开放式的厨房和客厅。德克兰环顾四周，看到了挂在墙上的家庭照片，餐桌上摆了一半的餐具，厨房里飘出的香味让他的肚子咕噜作响。一切都显得那么真实，就像这里的人们生活在这里，并且喜欢这里的生活。

src_seg:
Nicole gestured toward a stool at the island. “Sit, relax. Dinner’ll be ready in a few. Any food allergies I should know about?”
“Nope.”
Kyle was already pulling plates from the cabinet. “He held his own at practice,” he said casually over his shoulder, like it was no big deal.
Nicole raised a brow at Declan. “Impressive. First day and already showing off?”
He shrugged, a flicker of pride sneaking into his chest. “Just trying to keep up.”
It felt…comfortable in a way he hadn’t expected. Like maybe, for once, he wouldn’t have to brace himself all the time.
By the time they sat down for dinner, that feeling hadn't gone away.
tgt_seg:
妮可指向岛上的凳子。“坐下，放松。晚餐很快就做好了。有什么食物过敏吗？”
“没有。”
凯尔已经从橱柜里拿出盘子。“他在练习时表现得很好，”他漫不经心地从肩膀后面说，就像没什么大不了的。
妮可抬起眉毛看着迪克兰。“厉害。第一天就开始炫耀了？”
他耸耸肩，胸膛里闪过一丝自豪。“只是想跟上节奏。”
以一种他没想到的方式……感觉舒服。就像，也许，他不需要一直防备了。
到了吃晚餐的时候，这种感觉还没消失。

src_seg:
Declan hesitated only for a second before sliding into his seat next to Ryan, who was already digging in like it was a competitive sport. He glanced at his own portion and, after a quick taste, instantly understood why. The chicken parm was insanely good.
Declan took another bite, savoring the perfect balance of crispy breading and rich marinara. The flavors were way better than he expected, so much so that he couldn't help but mutter, “This is fucking good.”
The second the words left his mouth, the room fell dead silent. Ryan’s fork froze halfway to his mouth, his eyes snapping up to Declan with a mixture of shock and disbelief, like Declan had just unleashed a bomb at the dinner table.
tgt_seg:
德克兰犹豫了一下，然后就滑进了瑞恩旁边的座位，瑞恩已经像是在进行一场竞技比赛一样开始吃起来。他瞟了一眼自己的食物，品尝了一下，立刻明白了原因。鸡肉帕玛森（Chicken Parmesan）太好吃了。
德克兰又吃了一口，品味着酥脆的面包和丰富的马里纳拉酱的完美结合。味道远超他的预期，以至于他忍不住低声说：“这太他妈好吃了。”
话音刚落，教室里就鸦雀无声。瑞恩的叉子半空中停住了，他的眼睛瞪大了，充满了震惊和不可置信，就像德克兰在晚餐桌上放了一颗炸弹。

src_seg:
Declan, unaware of the shift, continued chewing, casually glancing around the table, still absorbed in the taste of his food.
Then he noticed it. The tension. The quiet.
Kyle’s voice broke the silence, calm but carrying an unmistakable authority. “Declan,” he said, his tone measured. “We don’t use that kind of language, especially not at the dinner table.”
Declan blinked, caught off guard. “Oh. Um, we...we’re hockey players though,” he shrugged, trying to brush it off. “It's kind of part of the deal.”
Kyle didn’t smile. His face remained impassive, though there was a flicker of something in his eyes, a reminder that this wasn’t some casual request. “Maybe on the ice, yeah, but even then, you’re too young for that kind of talk.”
tgt_seg:
德克兰，对这种变化浑然不觉，继续咀嚼食物，漫不经心地环顾四周，仍然沉浸在食物的味道中。
然后他注意到了。紧张。安静。
凯尔的声音打破了寂静，声音平静，但带着不可否认的权威。“德克兰，”他说，声音平稳。“我们不用那种语言，尤其是在晚餐桌上。”
德克兰眨了眨眼，措手不及。“哦。嗯，我们……我们是冰球运动员，”他耸耸肩，试图摆脱。“这有点是我们的一部分。”
凯尔没有笑。他的脸保持冷静，尽管他的眼睛闪过一丝光芒，提醒他这不是随便的请求。“也许在冰场上，是的，但即使在那里，你也太年轻了，不能说那种话。”

src_seg:
Declan’s brow furrowed, his words tripping over themselves. “You- what?”
Kyle’s gaze was steady, never wavering. “In this house, we keep it clean. We respect the people we’re around.”
Declan's confusion was evident as he leaned over to Ryan, lowering his voice. “You don’t talk like that?” he asked, genuinely curious, not sure what to make of it all.
Before Ryan could answer, Nicole's voice rang out, light but firm. “Not if he doesn’t want soap in his mouth.”
Ryan’s eyes widened comically, panic creeping into his voice. “Mom!”
Nicole didn’t bat an eye. “Just saying,” she added with a knowing smirk.
tgt_seg:
德克兰的眉头紧锁，他的话语磕磕绊绊。“你——”
凯尔的目光坚定，从未动摇。“在这个房子里，我们保持整洁。我们尊重周围的人。”
德克兰的困惑显而易见，他向瑞恩靠过来，低声说：“你不这样说吗？”他真诚地好奇，不知道该如何理解这一切。
在瑞恩回答之前，妮可的声音轻快而坚定。“如果他不想把肥皂放进嘴里，就别这样说。”
瑞恩的眼睛瞪得大大的，恐慌的声音传来。“妈妈！”
妮可没有回头。“只是说说而已，”她带着一丝知己的微笑补充道。

src_seg:
Declan’s chest tightened. Soap in his mouth? Was she serious? He shot a look toward Kyle, but there was no humor in his eyes, just a quiet, resolute discipline.
Kyle cleared his throat and leaned back, his expression softening just enough to show he wasn’t angry, but he wasn’t backing down either. 
“Look, we get it. Hockey culture, the locker room, it’s different. We don’t mind a little edge when it's warranted, but when you're in my house, there are lines we don’t cross.” He gave Declan a pointed look, making sure the weight of the words settled. “You’re not just here to play hockey, you’re here to grow. And that means learning discipline, both on and off the ice.”
tgt_seg:
德克兰的胸部紧绷。嘴里有肥皂？她是认真的吗？他朝凯尔看了一眼，凯尔的眼神中没有幽默，只有一种平静、坚定的纪律。
凯尔清了清嗓子，靠后坐下，他的表情软化了一些，足以表明他没有生气，但他也没有退缩。
“听着，我们明白。冰球文化，更衣室，情况不同。我们不介意有时候有点火气，但当你在我家的时候，有些界限不能越过。”他给德克兰投去了一眼，确保这些话的分量沉重。“你不是来这里打冰球的，你是来这里成长的。这意味着要学习纪律，无论是在冰场上还是在冰场外。”

src_seg:
Declan couldn’t deny the way those words landed on him. His gut twisted a little, not from anger, but from something else. It wasn’t exactly comfort , but maybe that’s what he needed: boundaries. 
Ryan eyed him again, his face unreadable now, like he was sizing Declan up all over again. Nicole, on the other hand, was already back to plating up another round of food, acting like nothing had happened. But Declan could tell, this family didn’t mess around.
Declan let out a small exhale, unsure what to say. “Yeah, sure. Sorry about that.” 
He leaned back in his chair and stared at his plate, trying to collect his thoughts. The sudden shift in atmosphere threw him off.
tgt_seg:
Declan 无法否认那些话语对他产生的影响。他的内心有些扭曲，不是因为愤怒，而是因为其他原因。这不是真正的安慰，但也许这正是他所需要的：界限。
Ryan 再次盯着他看，他的脸色现在已经无法辨认，仿佛他又在重新评估 Declan。Nicole 则已经开始摆放另一轮食物，表现得像什么都没发生过。但 Declan 可以感觉到，这个家庭不会轻易妥协。
Declan 深深地叹了口气，不知道该说什么。“是的，没问题。抱歉。”
他靠在椅子上，盯着盘子，试图理清思绪。突然的氛围变化让他感到困惑。

src_seg:
Kyle nodded, his voice softening again, but still carrying that same steady cadence. “It’s okay.” His mouth quirked in reassurance. “Alright. Now, eat up.”
Declan met Kyle’s gaze. He nodded, offering a sheepish grin. 
Ryan, still eyeing him like he’d just seen a rare species, let out a quiet sigh and turned his attention back to his food. Kyle gave Ryan a look that was all too familiar, a mix of casual suggestion and quiet command. 
“Hey, after dinner why don’t you help Declan get started on his homework?”
Ryan immediately groaned, his fork clattering against his plate. “I’m not a tutor.”
tgt_seg:
凯尔点了点头，他的声音再次变得柔和，但仍然保持着稳定的节奏。“没关系。”他的嘴角微微上扬，充满了安慰。“好吧。现在吃吧。”
德克兰看着凯尔的眼神。他点了点头，露出一丝尴尬的笑容。
瑞恩仍然盯着他，就像他刚看到一种稀有物种一样，轻声叹了口气，把注意力转回了他的食物。凯尔给瑞恩看了一眼，那是一眼再熟悉不过的眼神，既是随意的建议，也是轻轻的命令。
“嘿，晚饭后，你为什么不帮德克兰开始做作业呢？”
瑞恩立即抱怨起来，叉子敲打着盘子。“我不是辅导老师。”

src_seg:
Kyle didn’t flinch. He just raised his eyebrows, the eyebrows, stern but patient. The kind that said: You sure about that answer, kid?
Ryan deflated with a dramatic sigh, like he’d just been asked to scrub the entire rink with a toothbrush. “Dad, come on, I’ve got my own homework to finish. And I’m seriously wiped out.” He slouched even further, practically melting into his seat.
Before the tension could stretch any further, Declan spoke up, casually throwing Ryan a lifeline. “It’s fine. Mrs. Burke said I could get a tutor or something to catch up. No big deal.”
Kyle kept an eyebrow raised at Ryan, then looked back at Declan with a nod. “That works. We’ll talk to the school tomorrow, get someone lined up for you.”
tgt_seg:
凯尔没有闪避。他只是抬起眉毛，眉毛严厉而耐心。那种眉毛说：你确定答案，孩子？
瑞恩沮丧地深深叹了口气，就像他刚被要求用牙刷擦整个冰场一样。“爸爸，别这样，我还有作业要做。我真的很累。”他更往下靠，几乎融化在座位上。
在紧张局势进一步升级之前，德克兰插话了，随意地给瑞恩抛出一根救命稻草。“没关系。伯克太太说我可以找个辅导老师或什么来赶上。没什么大不了的。”
凯尔继续抬起眉毛看着瑞恩，然后看着德克兰点了点头。“行。我们明天和学校谈谈，为你安排一个人。”

src_seg:
Ryan shot Declan a look, something between surprised and quietly grateful. He didn’t say thank you, but his shoulders dropped a little, the way they do when someone realizes they’ve just been spared.
Declan just shrugged, like it wasn’t a big deal. 
Nicole bit back a smile. “Don’t worry about Ryan. He’s a lot more agreeable when there’s dessert on the line.”
Ryan groaned once again from his seat. “You act like I’m some kind of dessert-driven gremlin.”
Kyle laughed and stood, stretching. “Aren’t you?”
Nicole gave Declan a conspiratorial wink. “He once folded all the laundry in the house for a slice of triple chocolate cake. Don’t let the brooding fool you.”
tgt_seg:
瑞恩看了德克兰一眼，眼神中既惊讶又带着微微的感激。他没有说谢谢，但他的肩膀有些下垂，就像有人意识到自己刚刚逃过一劫一样。
德克兰只是耸了耸肩，就像这不是什么大事一样。
妮可忍住笑。“别担心瑞恩。他只要有甜点在身边就会变得更容易相处。”
瑞恩从座位上再次叹了口气。“你就像我是个被甜点驱动的恶魔。”
凯尔笑了，站起来伸了伸懒腰。“你不是吗？”
妮可对德克兰眨了眨眼睛。“他曾经为了一块三层巧克力蛋糕就把家里的所有洗衣服都洗了。别被他那副阴沉的样子给骗了。”

src_seg:
“I was ten.”
Declan smirked. “Good to know. I’ll keep chocolate cake in mind if I ever need a favor.”
The tight coil of nerves in his chest loosened just a little. The way they all moved around each other felt…safe.
He hadn’t realized how much he’d missed that kind of energy. Or maybe how little he’d ever had it in the first place.
After the last dish was rinsed and stacked, the clatter of plates gave way to the softer sounds of evening settling in. Kyle dried his hands on a kitchen towel and nodded toward the hallway. “C’mon, kid. Let’s get you set up.”
tgt_seg:
“我十岁了。”
德克兰轻轻一笑。“知道了。如果我需要帮忙，我会记得买巧克力蛋糕。”
他胸部的紧绷的神经线稍微放松了一些。他们彼此之间的互动感觉……安全。
他没有意识到自己有多么想念这种能量。或者他从来就没有多少这种能量。
最后一道菜被洗净并堆放好后，盘子的碰撞声让位于更加柔和的傍晚的声音。凯尔用厨房毛巾擦干手，然后向走廊点了点头。“来吧，孩子。让我们帮你安顿一下。”

src_seg:
Nicole offered a gentle smile, already halfway up the stairs with a fresh set of linens tucked under her arm. Declan followed, duffel slung over one shoulder, the adrenaline of the day slowly giving way to exhaustion. 
The guest room was just off the staircase, second door on the left. When Nicole pushed it open, Declan blinked, surprised.
The room was a lot bigger than he expected.
Not massive, but comfortably spacious. Soft gray walls, a queen bed with a green comforter and a real headboard, not the cinderblock-and-mattress setup he was used to. A big window overlooked the backyard, and a framed print of TD Garden hung over the dresser. A small desk sat under a shelf lined with books and picture frames. It didn’t feel like a guest room.
tgt_seg:
妮可带着温柔的微笑，已经半路上楼，手里还拎着一叠新换的床单。德克兰跟在后面，背着一个背包，一天的肾上腺素慢慢被疲惫所取代。
客房就在楼梯口不远，左边第二个门。妮可推开门，德克兰眨了眨眼，吃了一惊。
房间比他想象的大得多。
不算大，但足够宽敞。墙壁是柔和的灰色，床上铺着一床绿色的被子，床头是真正的床头板，而不是他习惯的砖头和床垫的组合。窗户可以看到后院，床头柜上挂着一幅TD Garden的照片。床头柜下面有一个小书桌，书架上摆满了书和相框。这感觉不像是客房。

src_seg:
“Wow,” he muttered. “This is… seriously nice.”
Behind him, Kyle chuckled. “Look at that. You didn’t even drop an F-bomb this time.”
Declan shot him a smirk over his shoulder. “I’m learning.”
Nicole grinned as she set a folded blanket at the foot of the bed. “Fast learner, too. That’s good news.”
Kyle knocked gently on the door connecting to the bathroom. “You and Ryan share this. Jack and Jill setup. Two sinks, one shower. Just don’t spend an hour in there or he’ll lose it.”
“Noted,” Declan said, still eyeing the space like it might vanish if he blinked.
tgt_seg:
“哇，” 他喃喃自语。“这……真的很不错。”
凯尔在他身后咯咯笑。“看看。你这次连 F 字都没说。”
德克兰从他肩后朝他瞟了一眼。“我在学习。”
妮可微笑着把折叠的毯子放在床脚。“你学的也挺快。这是个好消息。”
凯尔轻轻敲了敲通往浴室的门。“你和瑞安共享这个。杰克和吉尔的设置。两个水槽，一个淋浴。别在那里待太久，不然他会发疯。”
“记住了，” 德克兰说，仍然盯着这个空间，就像它可能会在他眨眼之间消失一样。

src_seg:
Nicole gave the comforter one last fluff. “Let us know if you need anything. Seriously. Make yourself at home.”
Kyle nodded once, giving him a brief clap on the shoulder. “Big day tomorrow, so get some rest.”
Nicole lingered for a second longer, then stepped forward and wrapped Declan in a quick, warm hug. He froze for half a beat, caught off guard, before awkwardly returning it.
“Good night, love,” she said softly, giving his arm a gentle squeeze before stepping back.
Declan blinked, unsure what to do with the sudden warmth in his chest. No one had called him that in…well, maybe ever.
tgt_seg:
妮可给这条被子最后一次拍打。“如果需要什么，随时告诉我们。真的。请尽情享受。”
凯尔点了点头，拍了拍他的肩膀。“明天是大日子，所以早点休息。”
妮可又犹豫了一下，然后向前走去，用热情的拥抱紧紧地抱住了德克兰。他愣了一下，被突然的拥抱吓了一跳，然后尴尬地把他还给了妮可。
“晚安，亲爱的，”她轻声说，轻轻地挤了挤他的胳膊，然后退后一步。
德克兰眨了眨眼，不知道该如何处理胸口突然涌起的温暖。没有人叫过他的“亲爱的”……嗯，也许从来没有。

src_seg:
“Night,” Declan mumbled, voice low.
Kyle paused at the door, gave him a look that was genuine. “We’re glad you’re here, Declan. Really.”
And just like that, they left him to it. The door left slightly ajar, like a quiet sign he wasn’t on his own here.
Declan stood for a moment, duffel still in hand, just taking it in. The house was quiet now, except for the faint sound of a TV down the hall and the occasional creak of floorboards.
He let out a long breath, dropped his bag by the desk, and sat on the edge of the bed. 
He kicked off his shoes and lay back, hands behind his head, eyes tracing the ceiling. Through the door of the Jack and Jill bathroom, he could hear faint movement; Ryan brushing his teeth maybe, or just walking around his own room. 
A shared wall, a shared life, starting now.
Maybe this year wouldn’t suck.
tgt_seg:
“夜晚，” 德克兰低声说。
凯尔在门口停下，给他一个真诚的眼神。“我们很高兴你来了，德克兰。真的。”
就这样，他们让他自己处理。门轻轻地敞开着，就像一个安静的信号，表示他在这里并不孤单。
德克兰站了一会儿，手里还拿着行李，只是吸收着这一切。现在房子安静了，除了走廊里电视的轻微声音和偶尔的地板吱吱作响。
他深吸一口气，把包放在桌子旁，坐在床边。
他脱下鞋子，躺下，双手放在头后，眼睛在天花板上打转。通过杰克和吉尔浴室的门，他可以听到微弱的动静；也许是瑞恩刷牙，或者只是走进自己的房间。
一堵墙，一个共同的生活，从现在开始。
也许今年不会糟糕。

src_seg: Sue Kay of Hawke's Bay, New Zealand writes: "I wish to thank all the kind people who helped my husband and me find our way from the airport to our hotel in the Sydney CBD. My husband is 90, and I'm 74 but, despite making ourselves known to our guide at the airport on arrival, we were left behind! We didn't know how to get to our hotel as we had the transfer organised. We must have asked at least six different people how to get to the Furama and everybody was so helpful and even helped us with our luggage. Sydneysiders may be big-city slickers but they have a small-town kindness!"
tgt_seg: 新西兰霍克湾的苏·凯写道：“我想感谢所有好心人，他们帮助我和丈夫从机场找到前往悉尼市中心的酒店的路。我丈夫90岁，我74岁，尽管我们在抵达机场后向导游报到，但我们还是被落下了！我们不知道如何到达酒店，因为我们已经安排了接送。我们一定问了至少六个人如何前往富华酒店，每个人都非常乐于助人，甚至帮我们提行李。悉尼人可能是大城市的精明人，但他们也有小镇的善良！”

src_seg: Some folks really do deserve a badge of honour for their pedantry (C8). Veronica Coyne of Springfield claims that "when bemoaning the loss of the express lane at Woolies "12 items or less," a friend told me she'd never used it on principle as it should have been "12 items or fewer.""
tgt_seg: 有些人确实值得为他们的严谨而获得荣誉奖章（C8）。斯普林菲尔德的维罗妮卡·科恩声称，“当我抱怨伍利斯超市（Woolies）失去‘12件或更少’的快速通道时，我的一个朋友告诉我，她从原则上从不使用它，因为它应该是‘12件或更少’。”

src_seg: "Talk of badges reminds of the famous one from the 1960s-70s," says Merran Loewenthal of Birchgrove. ""It Begins When You Sink in His Arms and Ends with Your Arms in His Sink."" Jonty Grinter of Katoomba has one that reads "Chronically Advantaged" and adds that "it should be standard issue for all over seventy."
tgt_seg: “谈到徽章，让我想起了20世纪60年代至70年代著名的徽章，”伯奇格罗夫的梅兰·洛文塔尔说。“它始于你沉浸在他的怀抱中，终于你的手臂沉浸在他的水槽里。”卡托姆巴的乔恩蒂·格林特有一个徽章，上面写着“长期受益者”，并补充说“这应该是所有70岁以上的人的标准配置。”

src_seg: As we haven't heard from Tony Nicod of Collaroy for nine months, one could consider this offering as a radical re-entry: "Finally the kids are back at school. No more grommets in the water taking waves off us retirees who like to surf "gentlemen's hours" from 8am."
tgt_seg: 由于我们已经九个月没收到科拉罗伊的托尼·尼科德的消息了，可以认为这篇文章是一种激进的回归：“孩子们终于回学校了。不再有小毛头在水中抢我们的浪，我们这些喜欢在‘绅士时间’——早上8点——冲浪的退休人员可以享受冲浪乐趣了。”

src_seg: Readers will take a shine to this item from Janice Creenaune of Austinmer: "Thanks for the wonderful memories Hendrik Kolenberg (C8). I kept my father's beautifully constructed wooden valet box. It remains filled with old Kiwi polish and brushes (some admittedly a little dried). He brushed my shoes every day of my school life to a high shine as he always thought it a sign of character. (My husband and I did maintain the task with our own children.) And the valet box remains well stocked, albeit sometimes with those little sponge squeeze bottles as well."
tgt_seg: 读者们一定会喜欢奥斯汀默的贾尼斯·克里瑙恩的这篇文章：“感谢亨德里克·科伦伯格（C8）带给我们的美好回忆。我保留了父亲精美制作的木制衣柜，里面仍然装满了旧的奇威鞋油和刷子（有些确实有点干了）。在我上学期间，他每天都给我擦鞋，把鞋子擦得锃亮，因为他认为这是品格的体现。（我和丈夫在抚养自己的孩子时也保持了这一习惯。）而且，衣柜里仍然备有充足的用品，尽管有时也会有一些小的海绵挤压瓶。”

src_seg: Peter Miniutti of Ashbury identifies the utility value in buying the good stuff: "Before the advent of the Internet, I'm sure I once used the sturdy turnkey from a tin of Kiwi shoe polish to open a tin of spam."
tgt_seg: 阿什伯里的彼得·米纽蒂指出了购买好东西的实用价值：“在互联网出现之前，我肯定曾经用过一罐奇威鞋油上坚固的钥匙来打开一罐午餐肉。”

src_seg: As we haven't heard from Tony Nicod of Collaroy for nine months, one could consider this offering as a radical re-entry: "Finally the kids are back at school. No more grommets in the water taking waves off us retirees who like to surf "gentlemen's hours" from 8am."
tgt_seg: 由于我们已经九个月没有收到来自科拉罗伊的托尼·尼科德的消息，人们可以认为这次投稿是一次激进的重新登场："孩子们终于回到学校了。水中不再有小冲浪者抢夺我们这些喜欢在上午8点'绅士时间'冲浪的退休人员的浪头。"

src_seg: Readers will take a shine to this item from Janice Creenaune of Austinmer: "Thanks for the wonderful memories Hendrik Kolenberg (C8). I kept my father's beautifully constructed wooden valet box. It remains filled with old Kiwi polish and brushes (some admittedly a little dried). He brushed my shoes every day of my school life to a high shine as he always thought it a sign of character. (My husband and I did maintain the task with our own children.) And the valet box remains well stocked, albeit sometimes with those little sponge squeeze bottles as well."
tgt_seg: 读者们会对来自奥斯汀默的詹妮丝·克里诺恩的这个故事感兴趣："感谢美好的回忆，亨德里克·科伦伯格（C8）。我保留了父亲精美制作的木制男士用品盒。里面仍然装满了旧的奇异鞋油和刷子（诚然有些已经有点干了）。在我整个学生时代，他每天都把我的鞋子刷得锃亮，因为他总是认为这是品格的象征。（我和丈夫也对自己的孩子保持了这个传统。）男士用品盒仍然库存充足，尽管有时也会有那些小海绵挤压瓶。"

src_seg: Peter Miniutti of Ashbury identifies the utility value in buying the good stuff: "Before the advent of the Internet, I'm sure I once used the sturdy turnkey from a tin of Kiwi shoe polish to open a tin of spam."
tgt_seg: 来自阿什伯里的彼得·米尼乌蒂指出了购买优质产品的实用价值："在互联网出现之前，我确信我曾经用奇异鞋油罐头上结实的开罐器打开过午餐肉罐头。"

src_seg: Sue Kay of Hawke's Bay, New Zealand writes: "I wish to thank all the kind people who helped my husband and me find our way from the airport to our hotel in the Sydney CBD. My husband is 90, and I'm 74 but, despite making ourselves known to our guide at the airport on arrival, we were left behind! We didn't know how to get to our hotel as we had the transfer organised. We must have asked at least six different people how to get to the Furama and everybody was so helpful and even helped us with our luggage. Sydneysiders may be big-city slickers but they have a small-town kindness!"
tgt_seg: 来自新西兰霍克斯湾的苏·凯写道：“我想感谢所有帮助我和我丈夫从机场到悉尼市中心酒店的好心人。我丈夫90岁了，我74岁，虽然我们到达机场后已经告知了接机人员，但他们却把我们给忘了！由于我们已经安排好了接送服务，所以我们不知道该如何到达酒店。我们至少问了六个人如何前往富丽华酒店，每个人都非常乐于助人，甚至还帮我们搬行李。悉尼人虽然生活在大城市，但他们却有着小城镇般的淳朴和善良！”

src_seg: Some folks really do deserve a badge of honour for their pedantry (C8). Veronica Coyne of Springfield claims that "when bemoaning the loss of the express lane at Woolies "12 items or less," a friend told me she'd never used it on principle as it should have been "12 items or fewer.""
tgt_seg: 有些人因为过于吹毛求疵，确实应该受到表扬（C8）。来自斯普林菲尔德的维罗妮卡·科因说，当她抱怨“伍尔沃斯超市取消了‘12件商品或更少’的快速通道”时，一位朋友告诉她，她一直坚持不用这个通道，因为她认为应该写成“12件商品或更少”。

tgt_seg: 科拉罗伊的托尼-尼科德（Tony Nicod）已经有九个月没有给我们写信了，我们可以把他的这封信看作是一次彻底的回归："孩子们终于回到学校了。我们这些喜欢从早上 8 点开始在 "绅士时间 "冲浪的退休人员再也不用在水里冲浪了"。

src_seg: Readers will take a shine to this item from Janice Creenaune of Austinmer: "Thanks for the wonderful memories Hendrik Kolenberg (C8). I kept my father's beautifully constructed wooden valet box. It remains filled with old Kiwi polish and brushes (some admittedly a little dried). He brushed my shoes every day of my school life to a high shine as he always thought it a sign of character. (My husband and I did maintain the task with our own children.) And the valet box remains well stocked, albeit sometimes with those little sponge squeeze bottles as well."
tgt_seg: 奥斯汀默的 Janice Creenaune 会给读者留下深刻印象："感谢 Hendrik Kolenberg（C8）给我留下的美好回忆。我一直保留着父亲做工精美的木制行李箱。盒子里仍然装满了旧的奇异果鞋油和刷子（当然有些已经有点干了）。在我的学生时代，他每天都会把我的鞋子刷得锃亮，因为他一直认为这是品格的象征。(我和我丈夫在自己的孩子身上也一直坚持着这项工作。）而且，代客泊车箱里的东西依然很齐全，尽管有时也会放一些海绵挤压的小瓶子。

src_seg: Peter Miniutti of Ashbury identifies the utility value in buying the good stuff: "Before the advent of the Internet, I'm sure I once used the sturdy turnkey from a tin of Kiwi shoe polish to open a tin of spam."
tgt_seg: Ashbury 公司的彼得-米尼乌蒂（Peter Miniutti）指出了购买好东西的实用价值："在互联网出现之前，我肯定曾经用一罐奇异果鞋油的坚固钥匙打开过一罐垃圾邮件"。

src_seg: Sue Kay of Hawke's Bay, New Zealand writes: "I wish to thank all the kind people who helped my husband and me find our way from the airport to our hotel in the Sydney CBD. My husband is 90, and I'm 74 but, despite making ourselves known to our guide at the airport on arrival, we were left behind! We didn't know how to get to our hotel as we had the transfer organised. We must have asked at least six different people how to get to the Furama and everybody was so helpful and even helped us with our luggage. Sydneysiders may be big-city slickers but they have a small-town kindness!"
tgt_seg: 来自新西兰霍克湾的苏·凯写道：“我想感谢所有帮助我和丈夫从机场到悉尼市中心酒店的友善人士。我丈夫90岁了，我74岁，但尽管我们在抵达机场时已告知了我们的导游，我们还是被落下了！由于我们已经安排好了接送，我们不知道如何到达酒店。我们至少问了六个人如何到达富丽华酒店，每个人都非常乐于助人，甚至帮助我们搬运行李。悉尼人可能看起来像大城市的时尚人士，但他们却有着小城镇的善良！”

tgt_seg: 有人真的因为小题大做而配得上荣誉勋章（C8）。斯普林菲尔德的维罗妮卡·科伊恩声称：“当有人抱怨沃利斯超市”12 item or less“快速通道的取消时，有一位朋友告诉我，她一向就坚决不用这个通道，因为这个通道应该叫”12 items or fewer“。”

src_seg: "Talk of badges reminds of the famous one from the 1960s-70s," says Merran Loewenthal of Birchgrove. ""It Begins When You Sink in His Arms and Ends with Your Arms in His Sink."" Jonty Grinter of Katoomba has one that reads "Chronically Advantaged" and adds that "it should be standard issue for all over seventy."
tgt_seg: 伯奇格罗夫市的梅兰·罗温塔尔（Merran Lowenthal）表示，“谈论徽章让我想起20世纪60、70年代的一个著名的徽章。”“这枚徽章上写着：‘当你沉浸在他的怀抱中，便已是尽头，你的双臂却又深深陷入他身下。’”凯托姆巴（Katoomba）的琼蒂·格兰特（Jonty Grinter）佩戴着一枚“长期享受优惠待遇”的徽章，并补充道，“这个徽章应当作为所有60岁以上人士的标准配备。”

src_seg: As we haven't heard from Tony Nicod of Collaroy for nine months, one could consider this offering as a radical re-entry: "Finally the kids are back at school. No more grommets in the water taking waves off us retirees who like to surf "gentlemen's hours" from 8am."
tgt_seg: Collaroy 的 Tony Nicod 九个月来没有和我们取得联系，因此我们可以将他的这条推文视作一个激进的回归之举：“终于孩子们回到了学校。我们这些喜欢在”绅士时间“ (从早上 8 点开始) 冲浪的退休人士，再也不用让那些水边的小家伙们来制造浪花了！”

src_seg: Readers will take a shine to this item from Janice Creenaune of Austinmer: "Thanks for the wonderful memories Hendrik Kolenberg (C8). I kept my father's beautifully constructed wooden valet box. It remains filled with old Kiwi polish and brushes (some admittedly a little dried). He brushed my shoes every day of my school life to a high shine as he always thought it a sign of character. (My husband and I did maintain the task with our own children.) And the valet box remains well stocked, albeit sometimes with those little sponge squeeze bottles as well."
tgt_seg: 来自奥斯廷莫尔的珍妮丝·克里努恩 (Janice Creenaune) 写到：“对我们来说，这个纪念品太有意义了。”“感谢你给我们的美好回忆，亨里克·科伦贝格 (Hendrik Kolenberg, C8)。我一直保存着我爸爸做的木质鞋盒，盒子里还摆满了旧的西兰鞋油和刷子（部分刷子用久已经干了）。从小学到高中，爸爸每天都会给我的鞋子上油，让它们闪闪发光。他总认为这代表了一个人的气质，我们夫妻俩长大后也把这件事带到了自己的孩子身上。我们现在家里还有木质鞋盒，不过有时候也会存一些海绵挤压瓶（小瓶瓶）。 ”

src_seg: Peter Miniutti of Ashbury identifies the utility value in buying the good stuff: "Before the advent of the Internet, I'm sure I once used the sturdy turnkey from a tin of Kiwi shoe polish to open a tin of spam."
tgt_seg: 艾什伯里的 Peter Miniutti 指出购买优质商品的实用价值：“在互联网兴起之前，我有过用 Kiwi 鞋油罐子的铁封条打开罐头的经历。”

src_seg: Sue Kay of Hawke's Bay, New Zealand writes: "I wish to thank all the kind people who helped my husband and me find our way from the airport to our hotel in the Sydney CBD. My husband is 90, and I'm 74 but, despite making ourselves known to our guide at the airport on arrival, we were left behind! We didn't know how to get to our hotel as we had the transfer organised. We must have asked at least six different people how to get to the Furama and everybody was so helpful and even helped us with our luggage. tgt_seg: 阿什伯里的彼得·米纽蒂指出了购买优质商品的实用价值：“在互联网出现之前，我肯定用过奇异鸟鞋油罐上的坚固开罐器来打开午餐肉罐头。”

src_seg: Sue Kay of Hawke's Bay, New Zealand writes: "I wish to thank all the kind people who helped my husband and me find our way from the airport to our hotel in the Sydney CBD. My husband is 90, and I'm 74 but, despite making ourselves known to our guide at the airport on arrival, we were left behind! We didn't know how to get to our hotel as we had the transfer organised. We must have asked at least six different people how to get to the Furama and everybody was so helpful and even helped us with our luggage. Sydneysiders may be big-city slickers but they have a small-town kindness!"
tgt_seg: 新西兰霍克湾的苏·凯（Sue Kay）写道：“我要感谢所有帮助我和我丈夫从机场找到悉尼中央商务区酒店的善良人士。我丈夫90岁，我74岁，尽管我们在抵达机场时向导游说明了情况，但我们还是被落下！由于我们已经安排了接驳服务，所以我们不知道如何到达酒店。我们至少向六个人询问了如何到达富拉玛酒店，每个人都非常乐于助人，甚至还帮我们拿行李。悉尼人可能都是大城市的精明人士，但他们也有小镇的善良！”

src_seg: Some folks really do deserve a badge of honour for their pedantry (C8). Veronica Coyne of Springfield claims that "when bemoaning the loss of the express lane at Woolies "12 items or less," a friend told me she'd never used it on principle as it should have been "12 items or fewer.""
tgt_seg: 有些人确实应该因为他们的刻板印象而获得荣誉徽章（C8）。斯普林菲尔德的维罗尼卡·科恩（Veronica Coyne）声称：“当我抱怨伍利斯（Woolies）超市取消了“12件或更少”的快捷通道时，一个朋友告诉我，她从原则上就从未使用过这个通道，因为它应该是“12件或更少”。

src_seg: "Talk of badges reminds of the famous one from the 1960s-70s," says Merran Loewenthal of Birchgrove. ""It Begins When You Sink in His Arms and Ends with Your Arms in His Sink."" Jonty Grinter of Katoomba has one that reads "Chronically Advantaged" and adds that "it should be standard issue for all over seventy."
tgt_seg: 伯奇格罗夫的梅兰·洛温森塔尔（Merran Loewenthal）说：“关于徽章的话题让我想起了20世纪60年代至70年代的著名徽章。”“它从你沉入他怀抱开始，到你的手伸进他的水槽结束。”来自卡图姆巴的乔蒂·格林特（Jonty Grinter）有一枚徽章上写着“慢性优势”，并补充说：“这应该成为所有七十岁以上人的标准装备。”

src_seg: As we haven't heard from Tony Nicod of Collaroy for nine months, one could consider this offering as a radical re-entry: "Finally the kids are back at school. No more grommets in the water taking waves off us retirees who like to surf "gentlemen's hours" from 8am."
tgt_seg: 由于我们已经九个月没有收到来自克拉罗伊的托尼·尼科德（Tony Nicod）的来信，我们可以将以下内容视为他激进的重新加入：“终于，孩子们又回到了学校。早上8点以后，我们这些喜欢在‘绅士时段’冲浪的退休人员再也不用担心水中的冲浪者会抢走我们的浪了。”

src_seg: Readers will take a shine to this item from Janice Creenaune of Austinmer: "Thanks for the wonderful memories Hendrik Kolenberg (C8). I kept my father's beautifully constructed wooden valet box. It remains filled with old Kiwi polish and brushes (some admittedly a little dried). He brushed my shoes every day of my school life to a high shine as he always thought it a sign of character. (My husband and I did maintain the task with our own children.) And the valet box remains well stocked, albeit sometimes with those little sponge squeeze bottles as well."

tgt_seg: “说到徽章，让我想起了上世纪60至70年代那枚广为人知的徽章，”伯奇格罗夫（Birchgrove）的梅兰·洛文塔尔（Merran Loewenthal）说，“上面写着：‘爱情始于你投入他的怀抱，终于你双手浸入他家的洗碗池’。”卡图姆巴（Katoomba）的乔蒂·格林特（Jonty Grinter）拥有一枚写着“长期受益者”（Chronically Advantaged）的徽章，并补充道：“这应该成为所有年过七旬的老人的标配。”

src_seg: As we haven't heard from Tony Nicod of Collaroy for nine months, one could consider this offering as a radical re-entry: "Finally the kids are back at school. No more grommets in the water taking waves off us retirees who like to surf "gentlemen's hours" from 8am."
tgt_seg: 我们已有九个月没有收到来自科拉罗伊的托尼·尼科德的任何消息，此次他的投稿可谓是“强势回归”：“孩子们终于回到学校了；再没有那些刚学会冲浪的小毛孩在水里和我们这些喜欢在早上 8 点冲浪的退休人员争抢海浪了。”

src_seg: Readers will take a shine to this item from Janice Creenaune of Austinmer: "Thanks for the wonderful memories Hendrik Kolenberg (C8). I kept my father's beautifully constructed wooden valet box. It remains filled with old Kiwi polish and brushes (some admittedly a little dried). He brushed my shoes every day of my school life to a high shine as he always thought it a sign of character. (My husband and I did maintain the task with our own children.) And the valet box remains well stocked, albeit sometimes with those little sponge squeeze bottles as well."
tgt_seg: 读者们一定会喜欢来自奥斯汀默（Austinmer）的珍妮丝·克里诺（Janice Creenaune）的这则分享：“感谢亨德里克·科伦伯格（C8）带来的美好回忆。我一直保留着父亲精心制作的那个做工精美的木制擦鞋盒。里面至今仍装满了旧款‘Kiwi’牌鞋油和鞋刷（尽管有些确实已经干涸了）。在我整个学生时代，父亲每天都为我擦鞋，因为他一直认为这代表着一个人的品格。（我和丈夫也将这一习惯延续到了自己的孩子身上。）如今，这个擦鞋盒依然‘库存充足’，尽管有时也会使用那种小巧的、带有海绵头的瓶装鞋油。”

src_seg: Peter Miniutti of Ashbury identifies the utility value in buying the good stuff: "Before the advent of the Internet, I'm sure I once used the sturdy turnkey from a tin of Kiwi shoe polish to open a tin of spam."
tgt_seg: 阿什伯里的彼得·米努蒂指出了购买优质产品的实用价值：“在互联网出现之前，我确信自己曾用过 Kiwi 鞋油罐上那个坚固的开罐器来打开午餐肉罐头。”

src_seg: Sue Kay of Hawke's Bay, New Zealand writes: "I wish to thank all the kind people who helped my husband and me find our way from the airport to our hotel in the Sydney CBD. My husband is 90, and I'm 74 but, despite making ourselves known to our guide at the airport on arrival, we were left behind! We didn't know how to get to our hotel as we had the transfer organised. We must have asked at least six different people how to get to the Furama and everybody was so helpful and even helped us with our luggage. Sydneysiders may be big-city slickers but they have a small-town kindness!"
tgt_seg: 新西兰霍克斯湾的苏·凯写道：“我要感谢所有好心人，他们帮助我和我丈夫找到了从机场到悉尼中央商务区酒店的路。我丈夫90岁，我74岁，尽管我们抵达机场后向导游报了到，但还是被落下了！我们不知道该如何去酒店，因为我们的接送服务是安排好的。我们至少向六位不同的人询问如何到达富丽华酒店，每个人都非常热心，甚至还帮我们拿行李。悉尼人或许是见多识广的都市人，但他们却有着小镇般的善良！”

src_seg: Some folks really do deserve a badge of honour for their pedantry (C8). Veronica Coyne of Springfield claims that "when bemoaning the loss of the express lane at Woolies "12 items or less," a friend told me she'd never used it on principle as it should have been "12 items or fewer.""

We must have asked at least six different people how to get to the Furama and everybody was so helpful and even helped us with our luggage. Sydneysiders may be big-city slickers but they have a small-town kindness!"
tgt_seg: 新西兰霍克斯湾的Sue Kay写道：“我要感谢所有帮助我和丈夫从机场前往悉尼中央商务区酒店的好心人。我的丈夫已经90岁了，我也有74岁，尽管我们在抵达机场时已向导游表明身份，但还是被落下了！我们不知道如何前往酒店，因为我们已经安排好了接送。我们至少向六位不同的人询问如何到达富丽华酒店，每个人都非常热心，甚至还帮我们提行李。悉尼人也许是大城市里的人，但他们却有着小镇的善良！”

src_seg: Some folks really do deserve a badge of honour for their pedantry (C8). Veronica Coyne of Springfield claims that "when bemoaning the loss of the express lane at Woolies "12 items or less," a friend told me she'd never used it on principle as it should have been "12 items or fewer.""
tgt_seg: 有些人确实值得因其吹毛求疵而获得荣誉徽章（C8）。Springfield的Veronica Coyne称：“当我抱怨Woolies超市‘12件或以下’快速通道取消时，一位朋友告诉我，她从未用过那条通道，因为原则上应该写‘12件或更少’。”

src_seg: "Talk of badges reminds of the famous one from the 1960s-70s," says Merran Loewenthal of Birchgrove. ""It Begins When You Sink in His Arms and Ends with Your Arms in His Sink."" Jonty Grinter of Katoomba has one that reads "Chronically Advantaged" and adds that "it should be standard issue for all over seventy."
tgt_seg: “说到徽章，让我想起了上世纪六七十年代著名的那一句，”Birchgrove的Merran Loewenthal说，“‘它开始于你沉浸在他的怀抱中，结束于你的双臂在他的水槽里。’”Katoomba的Jonty Grinter有一个写着“长期受益者”的徽章，并补充说，“这应该成为所有七十岁以上人士的标配。”

src_seg: As we haven't heard from Tony Nicod of Collaroy for nine months, one could consider this offering as a radical re-entry: "Finally the kids are back at school. No more grommets in the water taking waves off us retirees who like to surf "gentlemen's hours" from 8am."
tgt_seg: 由于我们已有九个月未收到Collaroy的Tony Nicod的来信，这次投稿可谓是一次激进的回归：“孩子们终于回到学校了。再也没有那些在水里抢我们这些喜欢在‘绅士时间’（早上8点）冲浪的退休人士浪头的小家伙了。”

src_seg: Readers will take a shine to this item from Janice Creenaune of Austinmer: "Thanks for the wonderful memories Hendrik Kolenberg (C8). I kept my father's beautifully constructed wooden valet box. It remains filled with old Kiwi polish and brushes (some admittedly a little dried). He brushed my shoes every day of my school life to a high shine as he always thought it a sign of character. (My husband and I did maintain the task with our own children.) And the valet box remains well stocked, albeit sometimes with those little sponge squeeze bottles as well."
tgt_seg: 读者们一定会喜欢来自Austinmer的Janice Creenaune的这则投稿：“感谢Hendrik Kolenberg（C8）带来的美好回忆。我一直保留着父亲精心制作的木制男士梳妆盒，里面至今还装满了旧的Kiwi鞋油和刷子（有些确实有点干了）。我上学期间，父亲每天都把我的鞋子擦得锃亮，因为他一直认为这是一种品格的体现。（我和丈夫也坚持为我们的孩子做这件事。）梳妆盒至今依然备货充足，虽然有时也会放些小型海绵挤压瓶。”

tgt_seg: 2大行业领涨市场。博通可能拥有另一家定制芯片合作伙伴

src_seg: Every weekday, the CNBC Investing Club with Jim Cramer releases the Homestretch - an actionable afternoon update, just in time for the last hour of trading on Wall Street. Market moves: Stocks were higher to start the new week, with the Dow, the S&P 500, and the Nasdaq shrugging off the trade and tariff headlines that caused weakness on Wall Street last week. Energy was the top-performing sector Monday, thanks to gains in oil and natural gas prices. Our lone oil and nat gas name, Coterra Energy, was jumping roughly 3.8%. Tech, however, was the main driver of the overall market gains due to the strength in the Magnificent Seven stocks. The Club owns six of them: Apple, Alphabet, Amazon, Meta Platforms, Microsoft, and Nvidia. The seventh Mag 7 stock is Tesla. The only two sectors sitting out Monday's rally were health care and financials. Both sectors are among the top gainers so far this year but have come under pressure in February. All three of our financial positions - Wells Fargo, Goldman Sachs, and BlackRock - are presenting at conferences on Tuesday. So, we'll hear the latest from each of them.
tgt_seg: 每逢工作日，吉姆·克莱默（Jim Cramer）的CNBC投资俱乐部都会发布午后更新——《冲刺》（Homestretch），为华尔街最后1小时的交易提供可行的参考。市场动态：新的一周伊始，股市上涨，道琼斯指数、标普500指数和纳斯达克指数摆脱了上周因贸易和关税头条新闻导致的疲软。能源板块周一表现最佳，得益于油价和天然气价格的上涨。我们唯一持有的油气股票——Coterra Energy股价大涨约3.8%。然而，由于“七巨头”股票的强劲表现，科技板块成为整体市场涨幅的主要驱动力。我们的投资组合中持有其中六只股票：苹果、Alphabet、亚马逊、Meta Platforms、微软和英伟达。第七只“七巨头”股票是特斯拉。医疗保健和金融板块是周一涨势中仅有的两个旁观者。尽管这两个板块今年迄今为止都是最大的赢家之一，但二月份以来却面临压力。我们的三只金融股——富国银行、高盛和贝莱德——都将在周二的会议上作报告。因此，我们将听到他们各自的最新消息。

src_seg: Broadcom: One of Broadcom 's new custom AI chip partnerships is coming into focus. Reuters reported Monday that ChatGPT creator OpenAI is finalizing the design for its first in-house chip. The story suggests the chip is in the later stages and could begin to be mass-produced later this year. Taiwan Semiconductor is the fab that will manufacture this new custom chip, but the story says the chip was designed by OpenAI's in-house team in collaboration with Broadcom. The Hock Tan-led Broadcom currently has three custom AI chip customers, and those clients are widely believed to be Alphabet and Meta - and most recently, ByteDance, the Chinese owner of TikTok. When Broadcom last reported earnings in December, one of the reasons why the stock soared almost 25% was Tan's reveal that the company was in advanced AI chip development with two additional hyperscalers. Based on previous media reports, OpenAI and Apple are believed to be those two customers. Microsoft is a financial backer and partner of OpenAI. On Broadcom's December earnings call, Tan estimated the company's service addressable market (SAM) for its AI business, which includes sales of both custom and networking chips, was $60 billion to $90 billion. That bullish target did not include custom silicon sales from these two new customers. If all the reporting is true, having a fourth AI chip customer in production is great news for Broadcom's ability to capture this large SAM. Broadcom shares jumped 4.5% on Monday. But they were still below their Jan. 24 close before Chinese startup DeepSeek went viral with claims of a cheaper AI model that slammed chip stocks.

src_seg: Broadcom: One of Broadcom 's new custom AI chip partnerships is coming into focus. Reuters reported Monday that ChatGPT creator OpenAI is finalizing the design for its first in-house chip. src_seg: Every weekday, the CNBC Investing Club with Jim Cramer releases the Homestretch - an actionable afternoon update, just in time for the last hour of trading on Wall Street. Market moves: Stocks were higher to start the new week, with the Dow, the S&P 500, and the Nasdaq shrugging off the trade and tariff headlines that caused weakness on Wall Street last week. Energy was the top-performing sector Monday, thanks to gains in oil and natural gas prices. Our lone oil and nat gas name, Coterra Energy, was jumping roughly 3.8%. Tech, however, was the main driver of the overall market gains due to the strength in the Magnificent Seven stocks. The Club owns six of them: Apple, Alphabet, Amazon, Meta Platforms, Microsoft, and Nvidia. The seventh Mag 7 stock is Tesla. The only two sectors sitting out Monday's rally were health care and financials. Both sectors are among the top gainers so far this year but have come under pressure in February. All three of our financial positions - Wells Fargo, Goldman Sachs, and BlackRock - are presenting at conferences on Tuesday. So, we'll hear the latest from each of them.

src_seg: Broadcom: One of Broadcom 's new custom AI chip partnerships is coming into focus. Reuters reported Monday that ChatGPT creator OpenAI is finalizing the design for its first in-house chip. The story suggests the chip is in the later stages and could begin to be mass-produced later this year. Taiwan Semiconductor is the fab that will manufacture this new custom chip, but the story says the chip was designed by OpenAI's in-house team in collaboration with Broadcom. The Hock Tan-led Broadcom currently has three custom AI chip customers, and those clients are widely believed to be Alphabet and Meta - and most recently, ByteDance, the Chinese owner of TikTok. When Broadcom last reported earnings in December, one of the reasons why the stock soared almost 25% was Tan's reveal that the company was in advanced AI chip development with two additional hyperscalers. Based on previous media reports, OpenAI and Apple are believed to be those two customers. Microsoft is a financial backer and partner of OpenAI. On Broadcom's December earnings call, Tan estimated the company's service addressable market (SAM) for its AI business, which includes sales of both custom and networking chips, was $60 billion to $90 billion. That bullish target did not include custom silicon sales from these two new customers. If all the reporting is true, having a fourth AI chip customer in production is great news for Broadcom's ability to capture this large SAM. Broadcom shares jumped 4.5% on Monday. But they were still below their Jan. 24 close before Chinese startup DeepSeek went viral with claims of a cheaper AI model that slammed chip stocks.
tgt_seg: Broadcom：Broadcom 的新定制 AI 芯片合作伙伴关系之一正在引起关注。周一，路透社报道，ChatGPT 创始人 OpenAI 正在完成其首个内部芯片的设计。报道称，该芯片处于后期阶段，可能在今年晚些时候开始大规模生产。台湾半导体公司将制造这款新定制芯片，但报道称，该芯片是由 OpenAI 内部团队与 Broadcom 合作设计的。Hock Tan 领导的 Broadcom 目前有三个定制 AI 芯片客户，这些客户被广泛认为是 Alphabet 和 Meta - 最近是 ByteDance，中国 TikTok 的所有者。当 Broadcom 上次报告收益时，Tan 透露公司正在与另外两个超大规模企业进行 AI 芯片开发，这使得股价几乎上涨 25%。根据之前的媒体报道，OpenAI 和苹果被认为是这两个客户。微软是 OpenAI 的财务支持者和合作伙伴。在 Broadcom 12 月收益电话中，Tan 估计公司 AI 业务的服务可达市场（SAM），包括定制和网络芯片的销售，为 600 亿美元至 900 亿美元。这一乐观目标不包括这两个新客户的定制硅销售。如果所有报道属实，拥有生产的第四个 AI 芯片客户对 Broadcom 捕获这个大型 SAM 来说是个好消息。Broadcom 股价周一上涨 4.5%，但仍低于 1 月 24 日中国初创公司 DeepSeek 病毒式传播声称更便宜的 AI 模型导致芯片股下跌之前的收盘价。

src_seg: South African opener Matthew Breetzke etched his name into the record books by becoming the first batter to score 150 runs on ODI debut in second match of the ongoing tri-series against New Zealand at the Gaddafi Stadium on Monday. His stunning knock of 150 off 148 balls, laced with 11 fours and five sixes, surpassed the previous record held by the legendary West Indies' batter Desmond Haynes, who scored 148 in his maiden ODI innings against Australia back in 1978. Before Breetzke's innings, the highest score on ODI debut for South Africa was 124 by Colin Ingram against Zimbabwe in 2010. Now, Breetzke stands alone at the top, delivering a performance that showcased patience, aggression, and remarkable shot selection as South Africa posted a mammoth 304/6.
tgt_seg: 南非队开局击球手马修·布雷茨克在周一与新西兰队进行的正在进行的三角系列赛第二场比赛中，在卡达菲体育场成为首位在 ODI 首秀中得分 150 分的击球手，从而将自己的名字刻入了记录簿。他以 148 个球打出 150 分，其中包括 11 个四分和 5 个六分，超越了此前由传奇的西印度击球手德斯蒙德·海恩斯保持的记录，后者在 1978 年对阵澳大利亚的首场 ODI 比赛中得分 148 分。在布雷茨克的比赛之前，南非队在 ODI 首秀中的最高得分是 2010 年科林·英格拉姆对阵津巴布韦时的 124 分。现在，布雷茨克独自站在榜首，他的表现展现了耐心、攻击性和出色的选球能力，南非队最终以 304/6 的巨大比分收官。

src_seg: Fresh off a month-long stint in the SA20 2025 season, Breetzke seamlessly transitioned into the ODI format, forming a crucial second-wicket stand of 93 runs with Jason Smith (41). He reached his half-century off 68 balls and continued to build on his solid start, eventually reaching his maiden century in 128 deliveries with the help of six boundaries and two sixes. In doing so, he became only the fourth South African to score an ODI century on debut, joining an elite club featuring Ingram, his current captain Temba Bavuma, and Reeza Hendricks.
tgt_seg: 刚刚结束为期一个月的 SA20 2025 赛季比赛，布雷茨克无缝地转换到了 ODI 赛制，与杰森·史密斯（41 分）建立了关键的第二 विकेट合作伙伴关系，共得 93 分。他在 68 个球中达到半个世纪，并继续巩固他的稳固开局，最终在 128 个球中达到他的首个世纪，其中包括 6 个边界和 2 个六分。在此过程中，他成为仅有的第四位在 ODI 首秀中得分百的南非球员，加入了由英格拉姆、现任队长滕巴·巴伐马和里扎·亨德里克斯组成的精英俱乐部。

src_seg: Post-century, Breetzke punished O'Rourke with two boundaries and a six in a single over, thus accelerating South Africa's late-innings scoring and building momentum for the Proteas. While his partnership with Smith provided early stability, he went on to forge another century stand for the fourth wicket with Wiaan Mulder (64), pushing South Africa past the 300-run mark. Breetzke, who will later join the Lucknow Super Giants in IPL 2025, exhibited complete dominance at the crease, enabling South Africa to establish a formidable total and providing their bowlers with a substantial platform in their bowling defence.
tgt_seg: 在达到世纪之后，布雷茨克在一个回合中对奥鲁尔克进行了两次边界和一次六分的打击，从而加快了南非队的后期得分，并为保护者队积聚了势头。虽然他与史密斯的合作提供了早期的稳定性，但他继续与威安·穆德尔（64 分）建立了另一个世纪的合作伙伴关系，为第四个三柱门，南非队最终超过了 300 分的门槛。布雷茨克后来将加入 IPL 2025 的勒克瑙超级巨人队，他在击球区表现出完全的统治力，使南非队能够建立一个强大的总分，并为他们的投球手在防守中提供了一个坚实的基础。

While his partnership with Smith provided early stability, he went on to forge another century stand for the fourth wicket with Wiaan Mulder (64), pushing South Africa past the 300-run mark. Breetzke, who will later join the Lucknow Super Giants in IPL 2025, exhibited complete dominance at the crease, enabling South Africa to establish a formidable total and providing their bowlers with a substantial platform in their bowling defence.
tgt_seg: 打出百分后，布雷茨克在一轮比赛中以两记边界球和一记六分球重创了奥罗克，从而加速了南非队在后期的得分，并为南非队积蓄了力量。他与史密斯的搭档为比赛初期提供了稳定，并帮助维安·穆尔德（64分）在第四个三柱门再次打出百分，帮助南非队突破300分大关。布雷茨克随后将加盟勒克瑙超级巨人队征战2025年印度超级联赛，他在击球线上展现了绝对的统治力，帮助南非队取得了令人瞩目的总分，并为他们的投球手在防守端提供了坚实的平台。

src_seg: South African opener Matthew Breetzke etched his name into the record books by becoming the first batter to score 150 runs on ODI debut in second match of the ongoing tri-series against New Zealand at the Gaddafi Stadium on Monday. His stunning knock of 150 off 148 balls, laced with 11 fours and five sixes, surpassed the previous record held by the legendary West Indies' batter Desmond Haynes, who scored 148 in his maiden ODI innings against Australia back in 1978. Before Breetzke's innings, the highest score on ODI debut for South Africa was 124 by Colin Ingram against Zimbabwe in 2010. Now, Breetzke stands alone at the top, delivering a performance that showcased patience, aggression, and remarkable shot selection as South Africa posted a mammoth 304/6.
tgt_seg: 南非首发球员马修·布里茨克 (Matthew Breetzke) 在周一在卡扎菲体育场对阵新西兰的三局系列赛的第二场比赛中成为首位在ODI首秀中得分150分的击球手.他惊人的148球中的150个击球,加上11个四球和五个六球,超越了传奇的西印度群岛击球手德斯蒙德·海恩斯 (Desmond Haynes) 之前的纪录,他在1978年对阵澳大利亚的首场ODI局中得分148分.在布里茨克的局前,南非首场ODI首秀的最高得分是2010年对阵津巴布韦的科林·英格拉姆 (Colin Ingram) 的124分.现在,布里茨克独自站在顶部,表现出耐心,侵略和出色的射门选择,因为南非发布了巨大的304/6.

src_seg: Fresh off a month-long stint in the SA20 2025 season, Breetzke seamlessly transitioned into the ODI format, forming a crucial second-wicket stand of 93 runs with Jason Smith (41). He reached his half-century off 68 balls and continued to build on his solid start, eventually reaching his maiden century in 128 deliveries with the help of six boundaries and two sixes. In doing so, he became only the fourth South African to score an ODI century on debut, joining an elite club featuring Ingram, his current captain Temba Bavuma, and Reeza Hendricks.

In doing so, he became only the fourth South African to score an ODI century on debut, joining an elite club featuring Ingram, his current captain Temba Bavuma, and Reeza Hendricks.
tgt_seg: 布雷茨基刚刚结束了为期一个月的 2025 赛季 SA20 比赛，随后便顺利切换到 ODI 比赛模式，与杰森·史密斯 (Jason Smith, 41岁) 组成了关键的二号搭档，两人一起打出了 93 分。布雷茨基在第 68 球便得分 50 分，随后他的表现依然非常出色，最终在第 128 球得分 100 分，这也令他成为了第 4 位首次亮相 ODI 比赛就得分 100 分的南非人，与英格拉姆、现任队长坦姆巴·巴夫玛（Temba Bavuma）和雷兹·亨德里克斯 (Reeza Hendricks) 等名将并列。

src_seg: Post-century, Breetzke punished O'Rourke with two boundaries and a six in a single over, thus accelerating South Africa's late-innings scoring and building momentum for the Proteas. While his partnership with Smith provided early stability, he went on to forge another century stand for the fourth wicket with Wiaan Mulder (64), pushing South Africa past the 300-run mark. Breetzke, who will later join the Lucknow Super Giants in IPL 2025, exhibited complete dominance at the crease, enabling South Africa to establish a formidable total and providing their bowlers with a substantial platform in their bowling defence.
tgt_seg: 进入新世纪后，布雷茨基在一个单局内连续罚出两支界外球和一支六分球，这加速了南非队后攻得分速度，为南部非洲队创造了冲势。他和史密斯搭档时带来了比赛早期的稳定性，而随后他又与第4位击球手维安·穆德（Wiaan Mulder，得分 64 分）搭档时又达成了打破百分的成就，使得南非队的得分超过了 300 分大关。布雷茨基将在 2025 年加入印超联赛拉合尔超级巨人队，他在打击区展现的完全支配力帮助南非队建立了一个稳固的得分总和，为南部非洲队的防守投球手提供了一个重要的基础。

src_seg: South African opener Matthew Breetzke etched his name into the record books by becoming the first batter to score 150 runs on ODI debut in second match of the ongoing tri-series against New Zealand at the Gaddafi Stadium on Monday. His stunning knock of 150 off 148 balls, laced with 11 fours and five sixes, surpassed the previous record held by the legendary West Indies' batter Desmond Haynes, who scored 148 in his maiden ODI innings against Australia back in 1978. Before Breetzke's innings, the highest score on ODI debut for South Africa was 124 by Colin Ingram against Zimbabwe in 2010. Now, Breetzke stands alone at the top, delivering a performance that showcased patience, aggression, and remarkable shot selection as South Africa posted a mammoth 304/6.

tgt_seg: 在SA20 2025赛季的月度停赛后，布雷茨基顺利过渡到ODI形式，与杰森·史密斯（41）形成了关键的第二支队，得分93分。他以68球打出半个世纪，继续建立在稳固的开始之上，最终在128次投球中以6个边界和2个六分之一的帮助下打出他的第一个世纪。这样做，他成为了南非在首秀中打出ODI世纪的第四位球员，加入了英格拉姆、他的现任队长滕巴·巴维马和里兹·亨德里克斯的精英俱乐部。

src_seg: Post-century, Breetzke punished O'Rourke with two boundaries and a six in a single over, thus accelerating South Africa's late-innings scoring and building momentum for the Proteas. While his partnership with Smith provided early stability, he went on to forge another century stand for the fourth wicket with Wiaan Mulder (64), pushing South Africa past the 300-run mark. Breetzke, who will later join the Lucknow Super Giants in IPL 2025, exhibited complete dominance at the crease, enabling South Africa to establish a formidable total and providing their bowlers with a substantial platform in their bowling defence.
tgt_seg: 在打出世纪后，布雷茨基在单一局中用两个边界和一个六分之一惩罚了奥罗克，从而加速了南非的晚期得分，为保护者建立了势头。虽然他的与史密斯的合作提供了早期的稳定性，但他继续与Wiaan Mulder（64）在第四支队形成了另一个世纪的合作，将南非推向了300分以上的得分。布雷茨基将在2025年的IPL中加入勒克瑙超级巨人队，展现了他在球场上的完全统治地位，使南非能够建立一个强大的总数，并为他们的防守提供了一个重要的平台。

src_seg: This will be the year that Guinness loses its cool. Cheers to that!
tgt_seg: 今年将是健力士啤酒不再流行的年份，干杯！

src_seg: I'm not sure I can remember exactly when I sensed it. Maybe it was when some of the more gimmicky London pubs introduced "stamp cards" to ration out Guinness after news of a shortage; maybe it was when I was served the 500th London Guinness rating video by my Instagram algorithm. Regardless of the precise moment the notion arrived, however, I have felt for a while that we are heading for a change when it comes to the pint du jour. For a few years now, Guinness has been the fashionable choice for millennial and gen Z drinkers, swept up in the aesthetic renaissance of the Good Old-Fashioned Bloody Pub. But I think the tide is turning. This will probably be the year that the Irish stout stops being cool.
tgt_seg: 我不太确定自己是什么时候意识到这一点的。可能是在伦敦一些更为另类的酒吧推出“集章卡”来限量供应健力士啤酒之后，因为当时有消息称啤酒短缺；也可能是在我的Instagram算法向我推送了第500个伦敦健力士评分视频时。不管这个想法是在什么时候产生的，我都感觉到，我们对每日精选啤酒的态度即将发生变化。几年来，健力士啤酒一直是千禧一代和Z世代饮酒者的时尚选择，他们沉浸在“老式血腥酒吧”的美学复兴中。但我认为潮流正在转变。今年很可能是爱尔兰黑啤停止流行的年份。

src_seg: I'm pretty sure that what will finally usher the Guinness hype train back into the station will be the same thing that came for Aperol spritzes and truffle: overexposure. The Aperol, once a genuinely trendy, vaguely Sex and the City-ish aperitivo-style drink is now a cultural behemoth in its own right - delicious, certainly, but definitely no longer "cool." And truffle, well ... would you like a side of truffle fries for that truffle mac and cheese garnished with truffle oil?
tgt_seg: 我相当确定，最终让健力士啤酒的热潮回归平静的因素，将是与Aperol苏打水和松露相同的因素：过度曝光。Aperol曾经是一种真正时尚的、带有《欲望都市》风格的开胃酒式饮料，现在已经成为一种文化巨头——当然很美味，但绝对不再“流行”。而松露嘛……你想在松露通心粉和奶酪（淋上松露油）旁边再来一份松露薯条吗？

src_seg: Overexposure, of course, is the death knell for cool in most cases (or at least self-conscious, trend-following "coolness," as I mean it here). This is particularly true amid the one-upmanship of contemporary food and drink culture which, as defined by social media, is always about being the first to find the undiscovered or most novel thing - the "hidden gem," the bakery and "pasta space" in London's zone 6 or what have you ("Come with me to the pub in Richmond that regularly floods"). And while Guinness's current round of popularity began because it was once viewed among younger pubgoers as a left-field choice - an "if you know, you know" order - it now couldn't be less of a secret.
tgt_seg: 当然，在大多数情况下，过度曝光是流行消亡的丧钟（或者至少是我在这里所指的自我意识强、追随潮流的“流行”）。在当代食品和饮料文化中，特别是在社交媒体定义的背景下，情况尤其如此。这种文化总是关于成为第一个发现未被发现或最新鲜事物的人——“隐藏的宝藏”，伦敦第6区的小面包店和“意大利面空间”，或者诸如此类的东西（“跟我来里士满的这家经常发洪水的酒吧”）。虽然健力士啤酒的当前流行始于它在年轻酒吧顾客中被视为一种非主流选择——一种“懂的人才知道”的点单方式——但现在它已经不再是什么秘密了。

src_seg: Undeniably, Guinness is everywhere. For the 2024-25 season, it shafted Budweiser to become the official beer of the Premier League, and will hold this honour for the next four years. It is the official beer of rugby's Six Nations tournament (meaning that for the next month, it is also the official beer of people called Henry). And a few months ago, news broke that the brand will be opening a Guinness Storehouse attraction, described as a "microbrewery and culture hub," in Covent Garden - despite the fact that London has nothing to do with Guinness or its 250-year-old heritage. Add to this the countless Hinge prompts about "splitting the G," and the impenetrable gaggle of gilets that pretty much always surrounds Soho's Guinness Disneyland, otherwise known as the wildly successful Devonshire pub, and you have to admit that the brand's cool stock is sinking.
tgt_seg: 毋庸置疑，健力士啤酒无处不在。在2024-25赛季，它取代百威啤酒成为英超联赛的官方啤酒，并将在未来四年内享有这一荣誉。它是橄榄球六国锦标赛的官方啤酒（这意味着在接下来的一个月里，它也是那些叫亨利的人的官方啤酒）。几个月前，有消息称该品牌将在考文特花园开设一家健力士啤酒厂景点，被描述为“微型酿酒厂和文化中心”——尽管伦敦与健力士啤酒或其250年的历史遗产毫无关系。除此之外，还有无数的交友软件个人主页提到“分摊健力士账单”，以及在索霍的健力士迪士尼乐园（即非常成功的德文郡酒吧）周围总是围着的那群穿着背心的顾客，你不得不承认，该品牌的流行度正在下降。

src_seg: I don't speak as a Guinness naysayer. On the contrary, I grew up with a Dublin man and former pub landlord for a grandfather, so reverence for the stout is all but in my blood. As such, Guinness is pretty much the only pint I regularly drink, and I'll even admit that I'm One Of Those People who has long-winded opinions about their favourite Guinness in London, and who really does believe that it differs in quality depending on where you order it (it's all in the gas, the installation and the line-cleaning).
tgt_seg: 我并不是一个健力士啤酒的反对者。相反，我的祖父是一位都柏林人和前酒吧老板，所以对这种黑啤的崇敬几乎是我的血液中的一部分。因此，健力士啤酒几乎是我经常喝的唯一一种啤酒，我甚至承认，我是那些对自己在伦敦最喜欢的健力士啤酒有长篇大论的人之一，我真的相信，根据你在哪里点酒，啤酒的质量是不同的（这一切都与气体、安装和管道清洁有关）。

src_seg: While Guinness may be at significant risk of losing its edge among, say, people who queue outside bakeries, this hardly matters to its bottom line. It has surpassed cult status, and has in essence become too big to fail. Debra Crew, chief executive of Diageo, the drinks conglomerate that owns the brand, told press this week that demand for the stout in October and November 2024 had surpassed even the amount called for during St Patrick's Day celebrations, noting that the clamour was "unprecedented." Crew also stated that Diageo is spending €200m (£170m) on a new Guinness factory in Kildare to keep supplies up to the level now required.
tgt_seg: 虽然健力士啤酒在那些在面包店外排队的人中可能正在失去其优势，但这对其底线几乎没有影响。它已经超越了狂热状态，基本上已经变得太大而不能倒。拥有该品牌的酒类集团Diageo的首席执行官Debra Crew本周对媒体表示，2024年10月和11月对该黑啤的需求甚至超过了圣帕特里克节庆祝活动期间的需求，并指出这种需求是“前所未有的”。Crew还表示，Diageo正在Kildare投资2亿欧元（合1.7亿英镑）建设一家新的健力士啤酒厂，以保持供应达到现在所需的水平。

src_seg: Music to my ears, really - I'm just pleased that while years ago you could walk into a pub and reasonably expect that Guinness wouldn't be served there, these days I can pretty much get my preferred pint anywhere. And, among all of the arguments to explain the surge in approval for the drink, it is important to acknowledge the obvious one: its smooth texture and subtly rich taste do just combine to offer something genuinely delicious, even when you get a mediocre one.
tgt_seg: 这对我来说真是个好消息——我很高兴，虽然多年前你走进一家酒吧，还可以合理地预期那里不会供应健力士啤酒，但如今我几乎可以在任何地方喝到我喜欢的啤酒。而且，在解释这种饮料受欢迎程度飙升的所有论点中，重要的是要承认一个显而易见的事实：它的顺滑质地和细腻的丰富味道确实结合在一起，提供了一种真正美味的体验，即使你喝到的是中等品质的啤酒。

src_seg: Ultimately, I'm more than happy to let the hype move on to a less obvious drink (over the past couple of weeks, I've been in two south-east London pubs that have recently installed the rival stout Murphy's, owing to local demand - go figure). Because as annoying as social media Guinness chat might be, and despite the extent to which the Schooner Scorer's camera angles haunt my nightmares (I mean it, don't Google it), it's like a wise man called Robbie Williams once sang: "You can't argue with popularity. Well you could, but you'd be wrong."
tgt_seg: 最终，我很高兴让这股热潮转移到一种不那么显眼的饮料上（在过去几周里，我去了东南伦敦的两家酒吧，它们最近安装了竞争对手黑啤Murphy's，因为当地有需求——真有趣）。因为尽管社交媒体上的健力士啤酒讨论可能很烦人，尽管“酒杯评分者”的拍摄角度让我夜不能寐（我是说真的，别谷歌搜索了），但就像罗比·威廉姆斯曾经唱的那样：“你无法与流行争辩。好吧，你可以争辩，但你错了。”

tgt_seg: 我不太确定具体是什么时候开始意识到这件事的。也许是当伦敦的一些酒吧为了应对吉尼斯啤酒短缺问题，开始推出“集章卡”来限量供应吉尼斯啤酒时；又或者是我在Instagram上被推送了第500个关于伦敦吉尼斯啤酒的评价视频。无论具体是什么时候，我一直觉得，在“当下的流行饮品”这个问题上，我们即将迎来一场变革。在过去的几年里，吉尼斯啤酒一直是千禧一代和Z世代年轻人最喜欢的选择，他们沉迷于这种“复古英式酒吧”的氛围。但我认为，这种潮流正在逐渐改变。今年很可能就是吉尼斯啤酒不再“酷”的一年。

src_seg: I'm pretty sure that what will finally usher the Guinness hype train back into the station will be the same thing that came for Aperol spritzes and truffle: overexposure. The Aperol, once a genuinely trendy, vaguely Sex and the City-ish aperitivo-style drink is now a cultural behemoth in its own right - delicious, certainly, but definitely no longer "cool." And truffle, well ... would you like a side of truffle fries for that truffle mac and cheese garnished with truffle oil?
tgt_seg: 我认为，最终让“健力士”热潮退却的，以及让“Aperol”和“松露”不再流行的，都是同一个原因：过度曝光。曾经风靡一时、颇具“《欲望都市》”风格的“Aperol”现在已经成为一种文化现象，虽然味道不错，但已经不再“时髦”了。至于“松露”嘛……您要来一份搭配松露油的松露通心粉，再来一份松露薯条吗？

src_seg: Overexposure, of course, is the death knell for cool in most cases (or at least self-conscious, trend-following "coolness," as I mean it here). This is particularly true amid the one-upmanship of contemporary food and drink culture which, as defined by social media, is always about being the first to find the undiscovered or most novel thing - the "hidden gem," the bakery and "pasta space" in London's zone 6 or what have you ("Come with me to the pub in Richmond that regularly floods"). And while Guinness's current round of popularity began because it was once viewed among younger pubgoers as a left-field choice - an "if you know, you know" order - it now couldn't be less of a secret.
tgt_seg: 当然，过度曝光往往会使任何事物失去“酷”的魅力（或者说，失去那种追逐潮流、自命不凡的“酷”）。尤其是在当今的餐饮文化中，这种现象更为明显。在社交媒体的影响下，人们总是想成为第一个发现“隐藏的宝藏”、伦敦“第六区”的特色面包店或“意面店”，或者“去里士满那家经常被淹的酒吧”的人——总之，就是要走在潮流前沿。而吉尼斯啤酒之所以再次流行起来，最初是因为它曾被年轻的酒吧顾客视为一种“另类”选择，一种“懂的人自然懂”的饮品。但现在，它已经不再是什么秘密了。

src_seg: Undeniably, Guinness is everywhere. For the 2024-25 season, it shafted Budweiser to become the official beer of the Premier League, and will hold this honour for the next four years. It is the official beer of rugby's Six Nations tournament (meaning that for the next month, it is also the official beer of people called Henry). And a few months ago, news broke that the brand will be opening a Guinness Storehouse attraction, described as a "microbrewery and culture hub," in Covent Garden - despite the fact that London has nothing to do with Guinness or its 250-year-old heritage. Add to this the countless Hinge prompts about "splitting the G," and the impenetrable gaggle of gilets that pretty much always surrounds Soho's Guinness Disneyland, otherwise known as the wildly successful Devonshire pub, and you have to admit that the brand's cool stock is sinking.
tgt_seg: 毋庸置疑，健力士啤酒（Guinness）无处不在。在2024-2025赛季，健力士啤酒取代百威啤酒，成为了英超联赛的官方啤酒，并且将保持这一荣誉长达四年。它还是橄榄球“六国锦标赛”的官方啤酒（这意味着在接下来的一个月里，它也是所有名叫“亨利”的人的官方啤酒）。此外，几个月前，有消息称该品牌将在伦敦的科文特花园开设一个“健力士啤酒体验馆”，该体验馆被描述为“微型啤酒厂和文化中心”，尽管伦敦与健力士啤酒或其250年的历史渊源并不深。再加上社交媒体上关于“一起喝健力士”的各种话题，以及总是围绕着伦敦索霍区“健力士啤酒乐园”（也就是非常受欢迎的德文郡酒吧）的人群，不得不承认，这个品牌的“酷”形象正在逐渐下滑。

src_seg: I don't speak as a Guinness naysayer. On the contrary, I grew up with a Dublin man and former pub landlord for a grandfather, so reverence for the stout is all but in my blood. As such, Guinness is pretty much the only pint I regularly drink, and I'll even admit that I'm One Of Those People who has long-winded opinions about their favourite Guinness in London, and who really does believe that it differs in quality depending on where you order it (it's all in the gas, the installation and the line-cleaning).
tgt_seg: 我并不是要批评健力士啤酒。恰恰相反，我的祖父是都柏林人，而且曾是酒吧老板，从小我就耳濡目染，对这种黑啤酒充满了敬意，可以说，这种敬意已经深深地融入了我的血液。因此，健力士啤酒几乎是我唯一经常喝的啤酒，而且我甚至可以承认，我是那种对伦敦各家酒吧的健力士啤酒品质都有着自己独特见解的人，并且我真的相信，不同酒吧的健力士啤酒品质确实存在差异（这都取决于啤酒的气体含量、安装方式以及管道清洁情况）。

src_seg: While Guinness may be at significant risk of losing its edge among, say, people who queue outside bakeries, this hardly matters to its bottom line. It has surpassed cult status, and has in essence become too big to fail. Debra Crew, chief executive of Diageo, the drinks conglomerate that owns the brand, told press this week that demand for the stout in October and November 2024 had surpassed even the amount called for during St Patrick's Day celebrations, noting that the clamour was "unprecedented." Crew also stated that Diageo is spending €200m (£170m) on a new Guinness factory in Kildare to keep supplies up to the level now required.
tgt_seg: 虽然健力士啤酒可能会面临失去一部分消费者的风险，比如那些经常排队购买面包的人，但这并不会对它的盈利造成太大影响。健力士啤酒已经超越了“小众品牌”的地位，并且已经发展到“大到无法倒闭”的程度。本周，健力士啤酒的母公司——饮料巨头帝亚吉欧（Diageo）的首席执行官德布拉·克鲁（Debra Crew）表示，2024年10月和11月健力士啤酒的需求量甚至超过了圣帕特里克节期间的需求量，并指出这种需求“前所未有”。克鲁还表示，帝亚吉欧正在爱尔兰基尔代尔（Kildare）投资2亿欧元（约1.7亿英镑）建设新的健力士啤酒厂，以满足目前日益增长的需求。

src_seg: Music to my ears, really - I'm just pleased that while years ago you could walk into a pub and reasonably expect that Guinness wouldn't be served there, these days I can pretty much get my preferred pint anywhere. And, among all of the arguments to explain the surge in approval for the drink, it is important to acknowledge the obvious one: its smooth texture and subtly rich taste do just combine to offer something genuinely delicious, even when you get a mediocre one.
tgt_seg: 听到这个消息真是太好了！以前，如果你走进一家酒吧，很难保证他们会提供健力士啤酒，但现在，几乎在任何地方都能喝到我喜欢的啤酒了。而且，在解释健力士啤酒越来越受欢迎的各种原因中，我们必须承认一个显而易见的原因：它口感顺滑、味道醇厚，即使是品质一般的健力士啤酒，也能给人带来一种非常美味的享受。

src_seg: Ultimately, I'm more than happy to let the hype move on to a less obvious drink (over the past couple of weeks, I've been in two south-east London pubs that have recently installed the rival stout Murphy's, owing to local demand - go figure). Because as annoying as social media Guinness chat might be, and despite the extent to which the Schooner Scorer's camera angles haunt my nightmares (I mean it, don't Google it), it's like a wise man called Robbie Williams once sang: "You can't argue with popularity. Well you could, but you'd be wrong."
tgt_seg: 总而言之，我很乐意让这种“炒作”转移到其他不太知名的酒品上（最近几周，我去了伦敦东南部的两家酒吧，它们都因为当地顾客的要求而开始供应竞争对手的黑啤酒“墨菲”，真是令人惊讶）。虽然社交媒体上关于健力士啤酒的讨论可能会让人感到厌烦，而且“斯库纳得分”的拍摄角度也常常让我做噩梦（我说的是真的，千万不要去搜索它），但正如一位名叫罗比·威廉姆斯的智者曾经唱过的：“你无法反驳流行，就算你反驳，你也一定是错的。”

And a few months ago, news broke that the brand will be opening a Guinness Storehouse attraction, described as a "microbrewery and culture hub," in Covent Garden - despite the fact that London has nothing to do with Guinness or its 250-year-old heritage. As such, Guinness is pretty much the only pint I regularly drink, and I'll even admit that I'm One Of Those People who has long-winded opinions about their favourite Guinness in London, and who really does believe that it differs in quality depending on where you order it (it's all in the gas, the installation and the line-cleaning).

src_seg: While Guinness may be at significant risk of losing its edge among, say, people who queue outside bakeries, this hardly matters to its bottom line. Crew also stated that Diageo is spending €200m (£170m) on a new Guinness factory in Kildare to keep supplies up to the level now required.

tgt_seg: 我并不是在唱衰吉尼斯。相反，我的祖父是一位来自都柏林、曾经营过酒吧的人，所以我对这款黑啤几乎有着与生俱来的敬意。因此，吉尼斯几乎是我唯一常喝的啤酒，我甚至承认自己是那种对伦敦哪家酒吧的吉尼斯最好喝有长篇大论观点的人，而且我真的相信在不同地方点的吉尼斯质量确实不同（这全看气体、设备安装和管线清洁）。

src_seg: While Guinness may be at significant risk of losing its edge among, say, people who queue outside bakeries, this hardly matters to its bottom line. It has surpassed cult status, and has in essence become too big to fail. Debra Crew, chief executive of Diageo, the drinks conglomerate that owns the brand, told press this week that demand for the stout in October and November 2024 had surpassed even the amount called for during St Patrick's Day celebrations, noting that the clamour was "unprecedented." Crew also stated that Diageo is spending €200m (£170m) on a new Guinness factory in Kildare to keep supplies up to the level now required.
tgt_seg: 尽管吉尼斯可能正面临在那些愿意在面包店外排队的人群中失去吸引力的风险，但这对它的实际利润几乎毫无影响。它已经超越了“小众文化”的范畴，实际上已经大到不会失败。拥有该品牌的饮料巨头帝亚吉欧（Diageo）首席执行官德布拉·克鲁（Debra Crew）本周对媒体表示，2024年10月和11月对吉尼斯黑啤的需求甚至超过了圣帕特里克节期间的水平，并指出这种需求“前所未有”。克鲁还表示，帝亚吉欧将投资2亿欧元（约合1.7亿英镑）在基尔代尔新建一家吉尼斯工厂，以满足目前所需的供应水平。

src_seg: Music to my ears, really - I'm just pleased that while years ago you could walk into a pub and reasonably expect that Guinness wouldn't be served there, these days I can pretty much get my preferred pint anywhere. And, among all of the arguments to explain the surge in approval for the drink, it is important to acknowledge the obvious one: its smooth texture and subtly rich taste do just combine to offer something genuinely delicious, even when you get a mediocre one.
tgt_seg: 这对我来说简直是天籁之音——我感到欣慰的是，过去走进酒吧时，你可能根本喝不到吉尼斯，而如今几乎在任何地方都能喝到我最喜欢的这杯啤酒。在所有解释这款啤酒受欢迎程度上升的理由中，有一点很重要：即使你喝到的是一杯平庸的吉尼斯，它那顺滑的口感和微妙浓郁的味道确实能带来真正的美味享受。

src_seg: Ultimately, I'm more than happy to let the hype move on to a less obvious drink (over the past couple of weeks, I've been in two south-east London pubs that have recently installed the rival stout Murphy's, owing to local demand - go figure). Because as annoying as social media Guinness chat might be, and despite the extent to which the Schooner Scorer's camera angles haunt my nightmares (I mean it, don't Google it), it's like a wise man called Robbie Williams once sang: "You can't argue with popularity. Well you could, but you'd be wrong."
tgt_seg: 归根结底，我很乐意让潮流转向另一种不那么显眼的饮品（在过去几周里，我去了两家位于伦敦东南部的酒吧，由于当地需求，它们最近都引进了竞争对手墨菲黑啤（Murphy's Stout）——你猜怎么着）。因为尽管社交媒体上关于吉尼斯的讨论可能令人厌烦，尽管“双桅帆船记分员”（Schooner Scorer）的拍摄角度在我的噩梦中挥之不去（我是认真的，别去谷歌搜索），就像一位名叫罗比·威廉姆斯（Robbie Williams）的智者曾经唱过的那样：“你无法与流行争辩。嗯，你可以争，但你会错。”

src_seg: This will be the year that Guinness loses its cool. Cheers to that!
tgt_seg: 今年将是健力士啤酒（Guinness）失去其潮流光环的一年。为此干杯！

src_seg: I'm not sure I can remember exactly when I sensed it. Maybe it was when some of the more gimmicky London pubs introduced "stamp cards" to ration out Guinness after news of a shortage; maybe it was when I was served the 500th London Guinness rating video by my Instagram algorithm. Regardless of the precise moment the notion arrived, however, I have felt for a while that we are heading for a change when it comes to the pint du jour. For a few years now, Guinness has been the fashionable choice for millennial and gen Z drinkers, swept up in the aesthetic renaissance of the Good Old-Fashioned Bloody Pub. But I think the tide is turning. This will probably be the year that the Irish stout stops being cool.
tgt_seg: 我不确定自己是从何时开始察觉这一趋势的。或许是当伦敦某些爱搞噱头的酒吧因缺货新闻推出"限量兑换卡"时；又或许是当Instagram算法第500次给我推送伦敦健力士测评视频时。但无论这个念头何时萌生，我早已预感这款当红啤酒即将迎来转折。多年来，随着"复古血统酒吧"的美学复兴，健力士一直是千禧一代和Z世代饮酒者的时尚之选。但我认为风向正在转变——今年很可能就是这款爱尔兰黑啤跌落神坛的年份。

src_seg: I'm pretty sure that what will finally usher the Guinness hype train back into the station will be the same thing that came for Aperol spritzes and truffle: overexposure. The Aperol, once a genuinely trendy, vaguely Sex and the City-ish aperitivo-style drink is now a cultural behemoth in its own right - delicious, certainly, but definitely no longer "cool." And truffle, well ... would you like a side of truffle fries for that truffle mac and cheese garnished with truffle oil?
tgt_seg: 我确信终结健力士热潮的，终将是与阿佩罗开胃酒（Aperol）和松露相同的宿命：过度曝光。曾几何时，阿佩罗气泡酒还是带着《欲望都市》影子的时髦开胃酒，如今却成了文化现象本身——好喝依旧，但绝对不再"酷"。至于松露...您需要为松露油焗通心粉配份松露薯条吗？

src_seg: Overexposure, of course, is the death knell for cool in most cases (or at least self-conscious, trend-following "coolness," as I mean it here). This is particularly true amid the one-upmanship of contemporary food and drink culture which, as defined by social media, is always about being the first to find the undiscovered or most novel thing - the "hidden gem," the bakery and "pasta space" in London's zone 6 or what have you ("Come with me to the pub in Richmond that regularly floods"). And while Guinness's current round of popularity began because it was once viewed among younger pubgoers as a left-field choice - an "if you know, you know" order - it now couldn't be less of a secret.

src_seg: Undeniably, Guinness is everywhere. For the 2024-25 season, it shafted Budweiser to become the official beer of the Premier League, and will hold this honour for the next four years. And a few months ago, news broke that the brand will be opening a Guinness Storehouse attraction, described as a "microbrewery and culture hub," in Covent Garden - despite the fact that London has nothing to do with Guinness or its 250-year-old heritage. Add to this the countless Hinge prompts about "splitting the G," and the impenetrable gaggle of gilets that pretty much always surrounds Soho's Guinness Disneyland, otherwise known as the wildly successful Devonshire pub, and you have to admit that the brand's cool stock is sinking.
