tgt_seg: 最后，我很高兴能让这场热潮转移到另一种不那么显眼的饮品上（在过去几周里，我去了伦敦东南部的两家酒吧，那里的酒吧最近因为当地的需求而引入了竞争品牌玛菲（Murphy's）的黑啤酒——真是令人百思不得其解）。因为尽管社交媒体上的吉尼斯话题可能令人厌烦，而且“Schooner Scorer”的摄像头镜头让我梦魇缠身（我是认真的，别去网上查），但正如一位叫罗比·威廉姆斯的智者曾经唱过的：“你无法与流行抗衡。你可以试试，但你会错的。”

src_seg: This will be the year that Guinness loses its cool. Cheers to that!
tgt_seg: 今年将是健力士（Guinness）啤酒不再酷的一年。为此干杯！

src_seg: I'm not sure I can remember exactly when I sensed it. Maybe it was when some of the more gimmicky London pubs introduced "stamp cards" to ration out Guinness after news of a shortage; maybe it was when I was served the 500th London Guinness rating video by my Instagram algorithm. Regardless of the precise moment the notion arrived, however, I have felt for a while that we are heading for a change when it comes to the pint du jour. For a few years now, Guinness has been the fashionable choice for millennial and gen Z drinkers, swept up in the aesthetic renaissance of the Good Old-Fashioned Bloody Pub. But I think the tide is turning. This will probably be the year that the Irish stout stops being cool.
tgt_seg: 我不确定自己是何时察觉到这一点的。或许是当一些噱头十足的伦敦酒吧在传出缺货消息后，推出了“集点卡”来限量供应健力士啤酒；又或许是当Instagram算法给我推送了第500个伦敦健力士啤酒评分视频时。但无论这个念头是何时冒出来的，一段时间以来，我一直觉得，在“时下最流行的啤酒”这个问题上，我们即将迎来风向的转变。几年来，在千禧一代和Z世代饮酒者中，健力士一直是时髦之选，他们沉浸在“传统老派酒吧”的美学复兴浪潮中。但我认为，这股潮流正在逆转。今年，这款爱尔兰世涛啤酒或许将不再酷了。

src_seg: I'm pretty sure that what will finally usher the Guinness hype train back into the station will be the same thing that came for Aperol spritzes and truffle: overexposure. The Aperol, once a genuinely trendy, vaguely Sex and the City-ish aperitivo-style drink is now a cultural behemoth in its own right - delicious, certainly, but definitely no longer "cool." And truffle, well ... would you like a side of truffle fries for that truffle mac and cheese garnished with truffle oil?
tgt_seg: 我敢肯定，让健力士这股热潮最终退去的，将是与曾经的阿佩罗橙光（Aperol spritz）鸡尾酒和松露一样的宿命：过度曝光。阿佩罗橙光，这款曾经真正时髦、略带《欲望都市》风格的开胃酒，如今已然成为一个文化符号——固然美味，但绝对不再“酷”了。至于松露，嗯……您的松露通心粉配松露油，要不要再来一份松露薯条？

src_seg: Overexposure, of course, is the death knell for cool in most cases (or at least self-conscious, trend-following "coolness," as I mean it here). This is particularly true amid the one-upmanship of contemporary food and drink culture which, as defined by social media, is always about being the first to find the undiscovered or most novel thing - the "hidden gem," the bakery and "pasta space" in London's zone 6 or what have you ("Come with me to the pub in Richmond that regularly floods"). And while Guinness's current round of popularity began because it was once viewed among younger pubgoers as a left-field choice - an "if you know, you know" order - it now couldn't be less of a secret.
tgt_seg: 当然，在大多数情况下，过度曝光是“酷”的丧钟（至少是我在此处所指的那种刻意追逐潮流的“酷”）。在当代饮食文化中，这一点尤为真实。这种由社交媒体所定义的文化，核心在于攀比炫耀，争先恐后地发现未被发掘或最新奇的事物——所谓的“隐藏的宝藏”，比如伦敦六区的某家面包店和“意面空间”之类（“跟我去里士满那家经常被水淹的酒吧”）。健力士之所以能掀起当前的这轮流行，正是因为它曾被年轻的酒吧常客视为一种小众的选择——一种“懂的都懂”的点单选择——而如今，它早已不是什么秘密了。

src_seg: Undeniably, Guinness is everywhere. For the 2024-25 season, it shafted Budweiser to become the official beer of the Premier League, and will hold this honour for the next four years. It is the official beer of rugby's Six Nations tournament (meaning that for the next month, it is also the official beer of people called Henry). And a few months ago, news broke that the brand will be opening a Guinness Storehouse attraction, described as a "microbrewery and culture hub," in Covent Garden - despite the fact that London has nothing to do with Guinness or its 250-year-old heritage. Add to this the countless Hinge prompts about "splitting the G," and the impenetrable gaggle of gilets that pretty much always surrounds Soho's Guinness Disneyland, otherwise known as the wildly successful Devonshire pub, and you have to admit that the brand's cool stock is sinking.
tgt_seg: 不可否认，健力士无处不在。在2024-25赛季，它取代了百威，成为英超联赛的官方啤酒，并将在未来四年持有这一荣誉。它还是橄榄球六国锦标赛的官方啤酒（这意味着在接下来的一个月里，它也成了那些名叫亨利的人的官方啤酒）。几个月前，有消息称，该品牌将在伦敦考文特花园开设一个健力士啤酒展览馆（Guinness Storehouse）景点，被描述为“小型酿酒厂和文化中心”——尽管伦敦与健力士及其250年的历史传承毫无关系。再加上Hinge（一款交友软件）上无数关于“一起喝杯健力士”的搭讪开场白，以及苏豪区那家大获成功的德文郡酒吧（又被称为“健力士迪士尼”）门口，总是被一群穿着马甲背心、密不透风的人群包围。你不得不承认，该品牌的“酷”值正在下跌。

src_seg: I don't speak as a Guinness naysayer. On the contrary, I grew up with a Dublin man and former pub landlord for a grandfather, so reverence for the stout is all but in my blood. As such, Guinness is pretty much the only pint I regularly drink, and I'll even admit that I'm One Of Those People who has long-winded opinions about their favourite Guinness in London, and who really does believe that it differs in quality depending on where you order it (it's all in the gas, the installation and the line-cleaning).
tgt_seg: 我这么说，并非是在唱衰健力士。恰恰相反，我的祖父是都柏林人，还曾是酒吧老板，在这样的家庭中长大，因此，对这款世涛啤酒的敬意几乎融入了我的血液。所以，健力士几乎是我唯一常喝的啤酒，我甚至得承认，我就是“那种人”：会对自己在伦敦最喜欢的健力士啤酒发表长篇大论，并且坚信，在不同地方点到的健力士品质确实有别（关键在于气体、设备安装和酒管清洁）。

src_seg: While Guinness may be at significant risk of losing its edge among, say, people who queue outside bakeries, this hardly matters to its bottom line. It has surpassed cult status, and has in essence become too big to fail. Debra Crew, chief executive of Diageo, the drinks conglomerate that owns the brand, told press this week that demand for the stout in October and November 2024 had surpassed even the amount called for during St Patrick's Day celebrations, noting that the clamour was "unprecedented." Crew also stated that Diageo is spending €200m (£170m) on a new Guinness factory in Kildare to keep supplies up to the level now required.
tgt_seg: 虽然健力士在那些会去面包店外排队的人群中，可能正面临失去其潮流优势的巨大风险，但这对其利润几乎没有影响。它已经超越了小众追捧的地位，本质上已经变得“大到不能倒”。拥有该品牌的酒业巨头帝亚吉欧（Diageo）的首席执行官黛布拉·克鲁（Debra Crew）本周向媒体透露，2023年10月和11月对这款世涛啤酒的需求量，甚至超过了圣帕特里克节庆祝活动期间的需求，并指出这股热潮“前所未有”。克鲁还表示，帝亚吉欧正投资2亿欧元（合1.7亿英镑）在基尔代尔新建一家健力士工厂，以确保供应能满足当前的需求水平。

src_seg: Music to my ears, really - I'm just pleased that while years ago you could walk into a pub and reasonably expect that Guinness wouldn't be served there, these days I can pretty much get my preferred pint anywhere. And, among all of the arguments to explain the surge in approval for the drink, it is important to acknowledge the obvious one: its smooth texture and subtly rich taste do just combine to offer something genuinely delicious, even when you get a mediocre one.
tgt_seg: 这对我来说真是天大的好消息——我只是很高兴，几年前你走进一家酒吧，很可能那里不卖健力士，而如今我几乎在哪儿都能喝到我最爱的那款啤酒。而且，在所有解释这款酒为何大受欢迎的论点中，我们必须承认一个最显而易见的原因：它顺滑的口感和馥郁又微妙的味道相结合，确实带来了真正的美味，即使你喝到的是一杯平庸之作。

src_seg: Ultimately, I'm more than happy to let the hype move on to a less obvious drink (over the past couple of weeks, I've been in two south-east London pubs that have recently installed the rival stout Murphy's, owing to local demand - go figure). Because as annoying as social media Guinness chat might be, and despite the extent to which the Schooner Scorer's camera angles haunt my nightmares (I mean it, don't Google it), it's like a wise man called Robbie Williams once sang: "You can't argue with popularity. Well you could, but you'd be wrong."
tgt_seg: 说到底，我非常乐意看到这股热潮转向另一款更小众的饮品（过去几周，我去了伦敦东南部的两家酒吧，它们都因为当地的需求，最近引进了健力士的竞争对手——墨菲（Murphy's）世涛啤酒，真是有趣）。因为，尽管社交媒体上关于健力士的讨论可能很烦人，尽管“大杯评分家”（Schooner Scorer）的拍摄角度在我的噩梦中挥之不去（我是认真的，别去搜），但这就像一位名叫罗比·威廉姆斯的智者曾经唱过的那样：“你无法与流行争辩。好吧，你可以，但你错了。”

src_seg: Overexposure, of course, is the death knell for cool in most cases (or at least self-conscious, trend-following "coolness," as I mean it here). This is particularly true amid the one-upmanship of contemporary food and drink culture which, as defined by social media, is always about being the first to find the undiscovered or most novel thing - the "hidden gem," the bakery and "pasta space" in London's zone 6 or what have you ("Come with me to the pub in Richmond that regularly floods"). And while Guinness's current round of popularity began because it was once viewed among younger pubgoers as a left-field choice - an "if you know, you know" order - it now couldn't be less of a secret.
tgt_seg: 过度曝光通常是酷的死亡铃声（或者自我意识、流行遵从的“酷”，我在这里所指的）。这尤其是在当代食品和饮料文化中，这种文化被定义为社交媒体，总是关于找到未发现的或最新的东西 - “隐藏宝藏”，伦敦区6的面包店和“粥空间”或者什么其他东西（“来跟我到富mond那家发洪的酒吧”）。Guinness的当前流行开始是因为它之前被年轻饮客视为一个左倾的选择 - “如果你知道，你知道”的订单，但现在已经不再是一个秘密。

src_seg: Undeniably, Guinness is everywhere. For the 2024-25 season, it shafted Budweiser to become the official beer of the Premier League, and will hold this honour for the next four years. It is the official beer of rugby's Six Nations tournament (meaning that for the next month, it is also the official beer of people called Henry). And a few months ago, news broke that the brand will be opening a Guinness Storehouse attraction, described as a "microbrewery and culture hub," in Covent Garden - despite the fact that London has nothing to do with Guinness or its 250-year-old heritage. Add to this the countless Hinge prompts about "splitting the G," and the impenetrable gaggle of gilets that pretty much always surrounds Soho's Guinness Disneyland, otherwise known as the wildly successful Devonshire pub, and you have to admit that the brand's cool stock is sinking.
tgt_seg: 无可否认，Guinness处处可见。2024-25季度，它抢夺了布逊威斯兹的冠军，成为了英超联盟的官方啤酒，将持续四年。它也是六国杯橄榄球赛的官方啤酒（这意味着下个月，它也将成为Henry这些人的官方啤酒）。几个月前，新闻曝光，品牌将在伦敦的科文园区开设一个Guinness Storehouse吸引式景点，描述为一个“小麦酒厂和文化中心”。尽管伦敦与Guinness和其250年历史无关，但它还是在那里开设了这个吸引式景点。加上无数次Hinge提示“分割G”，以及Soho的Guinness迷宫（也称为成功的Devonshire酒吧）周围的不可抗拒的衬衫军队，你必须承认Guinness的酷度正在下降。

src_seg: I don't speak as a Guinness naysayer. On the contrary, I grew up with a Dublin man and former pub landlord for a grandfather, so reverence for the stout is all but in my blood. As such, Guinness is pretty much the only pint I regularly drink, and I'll even admit that I'm One Of Those People who has long-winded opinions about their favourite Guinness in London, and who really does believe that it differs in quality depending on where you order it (it's all in the gas, the installation and the line-cleaning).
tgt_seg: 我不是Guinness的反对者。相反，我长大的一个纽伦堡人和前酒吧老板的祖父，所以对于麦酒的尊敬几乎在我的血液中。因此，Guinness是我最常喝的一种啤酒，我甚至会承认自己是那些人之一，会长篇大论自己最喜欢的伦敦的Guinness，并认为它的质量因处所的不同而有所不同（这都在气体、安装和清洁线上）。

src_seg: While Guinness may be at significant risk of losing its edge among, say, people who queue outside bakeries, this hardly matters to its bottom line. It has surpassed cult status, and has in essence become too big to fail. Debra Crew, chief executive of Diageo, the drinks conglomerate that owns the brand, told press this week that demand for the stout in October and November 2024 had surpassed even the amount called for during St Patrick's Day celebrations, noting that the clamour was "unprecedented." Crew also stated that Diageo is spending €200m (£170m) on a new Guinness factory in Kildare to keep supplies up to the level now required.
tgt_seg: 尽管Guinness可能面临失去酷的危险，但这对于其收益线来说并不重要。它已经超越了文化状态，已经成为了无法失败的。Diageo，拥有品牌的饮料集团的总裁Debra Crew在本周告诉媒体，10月和11月2024年Guinness的需求超过了圣诞节和圣路易斯节的需求，并指出这一点是“前所未有的”。Crew还表示，Diageo将投资2000万欧元（1700万英镑）在吉尔德尔（Kildare）建立一个新的Guinness工厂，以保持供应量达到现在所需的水平。

src_seg: Music to my ears, really - I'm just pleased that while years ago you could walk into a pub and reasonably expect that Guinness wouldn't be served there, these days I can pretty much get my preferred pint anywhere. And, among all of the arguments to explain the surge in approval for the drink, it is important to acknowledge the obvious one: its smooth texture and subtly rich taste do just combine to offer something genuinely delicious, even when you get a mediocre one.

src_seg: Ultimately, I'm more than happy to let the hype move on to a less obvious drink (over the past couple of weeks, I've been in two south-east London pubs that have recently installed the rival stout Murphy's, owing to local demand - go figure). tgt_seg: 我并非以吉尼斯啤酒的批评者身份发言。恰恰相反，我的祖父是一位来自都柏林的男人，也是一位前酒吧老板，我对这种黑啤的敬畏几乎刻在骨子里。因此，吉尼斯几乎是我唯一常喝的啤酒，我甚至承认自己是那些对自己在伦敦最喜欢的吉尼斯啤酒有着冗长见解的人，并且真的相信它的品质会因购买地点而有所不同（这全在于气体、安装和清洁管道）。

src_seg: While Guinness may be at significant risk of losing its edge among, say, people who queue outside bakeries, this hardly matters to its bottom line. It has surpassed cult status, and has in essence become too big to fail. Debra Crew, chief executive of Diageo, the drinks conglomerate that owns the brand, told press this week that demand for the stout in October and November 2024 had surpassed even the amount called for during St Patrick's Day celebrations, noting that the clamour was "unprecedented." Crew also stated that Diageo is spending €200m (£170m) on a new Guinness factory in Kildare to keep supplies up to the level now required.
tgt_seg: 虽然吉尼斯啤酒可能面临在例如面包店外排队的人群中失去其吸引力的风险，但这对于其盈利能力来说几乎无关紧要。它已经超越了狂热追随者的地位，本质上已经成为了“不可失败”的品牌。 Diageo首席执行官黛布拉·克鲁（Debra Crew）本周向媒体表示，2024年10月和11月的吉尼斯啤酒需求已经超过了圣帕特里克节期间的需求量，她称这种需求是“前所未有的”。克鲁还表示，Diageo正在在基尔代尔（Kildare）投资2亿欧元（1.7亿英镑）建设新的吉尼斯啤酒厂，以保持供应量达到目前所需的水平。

src_seg: Music to my ears, really - I'm just pleased that while years ago you could walk into a pub and reasonably expect that Guinness wouldn't be served there, these days I can pretty much get my preferred pint anywhere. And, among all of the arguments to explain the surge in approval for the drink, it is important to acknowledge the obvious one: its smooth texture and subtly rich taste do just combine to offer something genuinely delicious, even when you get a mediocre one.
tgt_seg: 这真是悦耳的声音——我真的很高兴，几年前你走进一家酒吧，可以合理地预期那里不会提供健力士啤酒，但如今我几乎可以在任何地方找到我喜欢的这杯啤酒。在解释健力士啤酒受欢迎程度飙升的各种论点中，重要的是要承认一个显而易见的事实：它的顺滑口感和微妙的丰富味道确实结合在一起，提供了一种真正美味的体验，即使是品质一般的健力士啤酒也一样如此。

src_seg: Ultimately, I'm more than happy to let the hype move on to a less obvious drink (over the past couple of weeks, I've been in two south-east London pubs that have recently installed the rival stout Murphy's, owing to local demand - go figure). Because as annoying as social media Guinness chat might be, and despite the extent to which the Schooner Scorer's camera angles haunt my nightmares (I mean it, don't Google it), it's like a wise man called Robbie Williams once sang: "You can't argue with popularity. Well you could, but you'd be wrong."
tgt_seg: 最终，我很乐意让炒作转移到一种不太显眼的饮品上（在过去的几周里，我去了两家位于东南伦敦的酒吧，它们最近安装了竞争对手的麦芽酒Murphy's，这要归功于当地的需求——真是令人费解）。因为尽管社交媒体上的吉尼斯讨论可能令人烦恼，而且尽管“Schooner Scorer”的摄像机角度让我做噩梦（我真的说的是，不要在谷歌上搜索它），但就像一位名叫罗比·威廉姆斯的智者曾经唱过的那样：“你无法反驳受欢迎程度。你可以尝试，但你会是错的。”

src_seg: This will be the year that Guinness loses its cool. Cheers to that!
tgt_seg: 这将是吉尼斯失去魅力的一年。干杯！

src_seg: I'm not sure I can remember exactly when I sensed it. Maybe it was when some of the more gimmicky London pubs introduced "stamp cards" to ration out Guinness after news of a shortage; maybe it was when I was served the 500th London Guinness rating video by my Instagram algorithm. Regardless of the precise moment the notion arrived, however, I have felt for a while that we are heading for a change when it comes to the pint du jour. For a few years now, Guinness has been the fashionable choice for millennial and gen Z drinkers, swept up in the aesthetic renaissance of the Good Old-Fashioned Bloody Pub. But I think the tide is turning. This will probably be the year that the Irish stout stops being cool.
tgt_seg: 我不确定确切是什么时候我意识到这一点。也许是在伦敦的一些酒吧开始推出“盖章卡”来限量供应吉尼斯，因为听说有短缺的时候；也许是在Instagram算法推送了我第500个伦敦吉尼斯评分视频的时候。不管确切的时刻是什么时候，我感觉我们正朝着吉尼斯的“小杯”发生改变。过去几年，吉尼斯一直是千禧一代和Z世代的时尚选择，他们被传统酒吧复兴的美学所吸引。但我认为潮流正在改变。这可能是吉尼斯不再酷的一年。

src_seg: I'm pretty sure that what will finally usher the Guinness hype train back into the station will be the same thing that came for Aperol spritzes and truffle: overexposure. The Aperol, once a genuinely trendy, vaguely Sex and the City-ish aperitivo-style drink is now a cultural behemoth in its own right - delicious, certainly, but definitely no longer "cool." And truffle, well ... would you like a side of truffle fries for that truffle mac and cheese garnished with truffle oil?
tgt_seg: 我确信最终会让吉尼斯的热潮回到终点站的，将是过度曝光。曾经真正流行、略带《欲望都市》风格的阿佩罗桑普西，现在已经成了文化巨兽——当然很好喝，但已经不再“酷”了。至于松露，你想要一份松露薯条配那用松露油装饰的松露奶酪吗？

src_seg: Overexposure, of course, is the death knell for cool in most cases (or at least self-conscious, trend-following "coolness," as I mean it here). This is particularly true amid the one-upmanship of contemporary food and drink culture which, as defined by social media, is always about being the first to find the undiscovered or most novel thing - the "hidden gem," the bakery and "pasta space" in London's zone 6 or what have you ("Come with me to the pub in Richmond that regularly floods"). And while Guinness's current round of popularity began because it was once viewed among younger pubgoers as a left-field choice - an "if you know, you know" order - it now couldn't be less of a secret.
tgt_seg: 过度曝光往往是大多数情况下“酷”的终结者（至少是自意识的、跟风的“酷”）。尤其是在当今美食和饮料文化的竞争中，这种“酷”在社交媒体定义下总是关于成为第一个发现最独特或最新颖的事物——“隐藏的宝石”，伦敦六区的面包店和“意面空间”（去里士满的一家定期泛滥的酒吧）。而尽管吉尼斯的当前流行始于它曾被视为年轻酒吧顾客中的一个意外选择——一个“懂的人自然懂”的点单——但现在它已经不再是个秘密。

src_seg: Undeniably, Guinness is everywhere. For the 2024-25 season, it shafted Budweiser to become the official beer of the Premier League, and will hold this honour for the next four years. It is the official beer of rugby's Six Nations tournament (meaning that for the next month, it is also the official beer of people called Henry). And a few months ago, news broke that the brand will be opening a Guinness Storehouse attraction, described as a "microbrewery and culture hub," in Covent Garden - despite the fact that London has nothing to do with Guinness or its 250-year-old heritage. Add to this the countless Hinge prompts about "splitting the G," and the impenetrable gaggle of gilets that pretty much always surrounds Soho's Guinness Disneyland, otherwise known as the wildly successful Devonshire pub, and you have to admit that the brand's cool stock is sinking.

src_seg: This will be the year that Guinness loses its cool. Cheers to that!

src_seg: I'm not sure I can remember exactly when I sensed it. Maybe it was when some of the more gimmicky London pubs introduced "stamp cards" to ration out Guinness after news of a shortage; maybe it was when I was served the 500th London Guinness rating video by my Instagram algorithm. Regardless of the precise moment the notion arrived, however, I have felt for a while that we are heading for a change when it comes to the pint du jour. For a few years now, Guinness has been the fashionable choice for millennial and gen Z drinkers, swept up in the aesthetic renaissance of the Good Old-Fashioned Bloody Pub. But I think the tide is turning. This will probably be the year that the Irish stout stops being cool.
tgt_seg: 我不太确定自己确切地意识到这一点是什么时候。也许是当一些伦敦的酒吧推出“集章卡”来限量供应健力士啤酒，在缺货的消息传出后；也许是我在Instagram算法中收到了第五百个伦敦健力士啤酒的评分视频。无论具体时刻是什么，我一直觉得我们正朝着一种变化前进，尤其是在当下的“当季啤酒”选择上。在过去的几年里，健力士啤酒一直是千禧一代和Z世代饮酒者的时尚选择，被老式血统酒吧的美学复兴所吸引。但我认为潮流正在转变。这很可能将是爱尔兰黑啤酒不再流行的那一年。

src_seg: I'm pretty sure that what will finally usher the Guinness hype train back into the station will be the same thing that came for Aperol spritzes and truffle: overexposure. The Aperol, once a genuinely trendy, vaguely Sex and the City-ish aperitivo-style drink is now a cultural behemoth in its own right - delicious, certainly, but definitely no longer "cool." And truffle, well ... would you like a side of truffle fries for that truffle mac and cheese garnished with truffle oil?
tgt_seg: 我相信最终会使健力士啤酒的热潮退去的原因，与阿佩罗开胃酒和松露的命运相同：过度曝光。阿佩罗开胃酒曾经是一种真正流行的、略带《欲望都市》风格的餐前酒，现在已经成为一种文化巨头——当然很美味，但绝对不再“潮流”。至于松露……您要来一份松露薯条搭配松露芝士通心粉，再淋上松露油吗？

src_seg: Overexposure, of course, is the death knell for cool in most cases (or at least self-conscious, trend-following "coolness," as I mean it here). This is particularly true amid the one-upmanship of contemporary food and drink culture which, as defined by social media, is always about being the first to find the undiscovered or most novel thing - the "hidden gem," the bakery and "pasta space" in London's zone 6 or what have you ("Come with me to the pub in Richmond that regularly floods"). And while Guinness's current round of popularity began because it was once viewed among younger pubgoers as a left-field choice - an "if you know, you know" order - it now couldn't be less of a secret.
tgt_seg: 过度曝光，当然，通常是“潮流”的丧钟（或者至少是自知之明的、追逐潮流的“潮流”）。这在当代餐饮文化中尤其如此，这种文化以社交媒体为导向，总是关于第一个发现未被发现或最独特的事物——“隐藏的宝石”、伦敦第六区的一家面包店和“意面店”，或者类似的地方（“跟我去里士满的一家经常被淹的酒吧”）。虽然健力士啤酒目前的流行始于它曾经被年轻的酒吧顾客视为一种非主流的选择——一种“懂的人自然知道”的订单，但现在它已经不再是什么秘密。

src_seg: Undeniably, Guinness is everywhere. For the 2024-25 season, it shafted Budweiser to become the official beer of the Premier League, and will hold this honour for the next four years. It is the official beer of rugby's Six Nations tournament (meaning that for the next month, it is also the official beer of people called Henry). And a few months ago, news broke that the brand will be opening a Guinness Storehouse attraction, described as a "microbrewery and culture hub," in Covent Garden - despite the fact that London has nothing to do with Guinness or its 250-year-old heritage. Add to this the countless Hinge prompts about "splitting the G," and the impenetrable gaggle of gilets that pretty much always surrounds Soho's Guinness Disneyland, otherwise known as the wildly successful Devonshire pub, and you have to admit that the brand's cool stock is sinking.
tgt_seg: 不可否认，健力士啤酒无处不在。在2024-25赛季，它取代百威啤酒，成为英超联赛的官方啤酒，并将保持这一荣誉四年。它是橄榄球六国锦标赛的官方啤酒（这意味着在接下来的一个月里，它也是名叫亨利的人的官方啤酒）。几个月前，有消息称该品牌将在科文特花园开设一家健力士体验馆，被描述为“微型啤酒厂和文化中心”——尽管伦敦与健力士啤酒或其250年的历史毫无关系。再加上无数Hinge应用上的关于“分一杯健力士”的提示，以及几乎总是围绕着索霍“健力士迪士尼乐园”（也就是大受欢迎的德文郡酒吧）密密麻麻的马甲，你不得不承认该品牌的“潮流”正在下降。

src_seg: I don't speak as a Guinness naysayer. On the contrary, I grew up with a Dublin man and former pub landlord for a grandfather, so reverence for the stout is all but in my blood. As such, Guinness is pretty much the only pint I regularly drink, and I'll even admit that I'm One Of Those People who has long-winded opinions about their favourite Guinness in London, and who really does believe that it differs in quality depending on where you order it (it's all in the gas, the installation and the line-cleaning).
tgt_seg: 我并不是在贬低健力士啤酒。相反，我的祖父是一位都柏林人，前酒吧老板，从小我就受到对这种黑啤酒的敬畏。因此，健力士啤酒几乎是我血液中的一部分。因此，健力士啤酒几乎是我经常喝的唯一啤酒，我甚至承认我是一个对伦敦最喜欢的健力士啤酒有长篇大论的人，并且真的相信它的质量取决于你订购的地点（这都取决于气体、安装和管线清洁）。

src_seg: While Guinness may be at significant risk of losing its edge among, say, people who queue outside bakeries, this hardly matters to its bottom line. It has surpassed cult status, and has in essence become too big to fail. Debra Crew, chief executive of Diageo, the drinks conglomerate that owns the brand, told press this week that demand for the stout in October and November 2024 had surpassed even the amount called for during St Patrick's Day celebrations, noting that the clamour was "unprecedented." Crew also stated that Diageo is spending €200m (£170m) on a new Guinness factory in Kildare to keep supplies up to the level now required.
tgt_seg: 虽然健力士啤酒可能面临失去在那些排队等候面包店的人们中“潮流”的风险，但这对它的利润底线影响不大。它已经超越了小众地位，本质上已经变得“大到不能倒”。达美乐公司（Diageo）首席执行官德布拉·克鲁（Debra Crew）本周告诉媒体，2024年10月和11月健力士啤酒的需求甚至超过了圣帕特里克节期间的需求，并指出这种热潮是“前所未有”的。克鲁还表示，达美乐公司正在投资2亿欧元（1.7亿英镑）在基尔代尔建造一家新的健力士啤酒厂，以满足目前所需的供应量。

src_seg: Music to my ears, really - I'm just pleased that while years ago you could walk into a pub and reasonably expect that Guinness wouldn't be served there, these days I can pretty much get my preferred pint anywhere. And, among all of the arguments to explain the surge in approval for the drink, it is important to acknowledge the obvious one: its smooth texture and subtly rich taste do just combine to offer something genuinely delicious, even when you get a mediocre one.

src_seg: Ultimately, I'm more than happy to let the hype move on to a less obvious drink (over the past couple of weeks, I've been in two south-east London pubs that have recently installed the rival stout Murphy's, owing to local demand - go figure). Because as annoying as social media Guinness chat might be, and despite the extent to which the Schooner Scorer's camera angles haunt my nightmares (I mean it, don't Google it), it's like a wise man called Robbie Williams once sang: "You can't argue with popularity. Well you could, but you'd be wrong."

src_seg: Undeniably, Guinness is everywhere. For the 2024-25 season, it shafted Budweiser to become the official beer of the Premier League, and will hold this honour for the next four years. It is the official beer of rugby's Six Nations tournament (meaning that for the next month, it is also the official beer of people called Henry). And a few months ago, news broke that the brand will be opening a Guinness Storehouse attraction, described as a "microbrewery and culture hub," in Covent Garden - despite the fact that London has nothing to do with Guinness or its 250-year-old heritage. Add to this the countless Hinge prompts about "splitting the G," and the impenetrable gaggle of gilets that pretty much always surrounds Soho's Guinness Disneyland, otherwise known as the wildly successful Devonshire pub, and you have to admit that the brand's cool stock is sinking.
tgt_seg: 无可否认，健力士无处不在。2024-25 赛季，它超越百威成为英超联赛的官方啤酒，并将在接下来的四年里保持这一荣誉。它是橄榄球六国锦标赛的官方啤酒（这意味着接下来一个月，它也是被称为亨利的人们的官方啤酒）。几个月前，有消息称该品牌将在考文特花园开设一处被称为“微酿酒厂和文化中心”的健力士店，尽管伦敦与健力士及其 250 年的悠久历史毫无关系。再加上无数次关于“分担 G”的 Hinge 提示，以及总是围绕着苏荷区的健力士迪士尼乐园（也就是大获成功的德文郡酒吧）的不可穿透的围裙群，你不得不承认，这家品牌的“酷”度正在下降。

src_seg: I don't speak as a Guinness naysayer. On the contrary, I grew up with a Dublin man and former pub landlord for a grandfather, so reverence for the stout is all but in my blood. As such, Guinness is pretty much the only pint I regularly drink, and I'll even admit that I'm One Of Those People who has long-winded opinions about their favourite Guinness in London, and who really does believe that it differs in quality depending on where you order it (it's all in the gas, the installation and the line-cleaning).

src_seg: While Guinness may be at significant risk of losing its edge among, say, people who queue outside bakeries, this hardly matters to its bottom line. It has surpassed cult status, and has in essence become too big to fail. Debra Crew, chief executive of Diageo, the drinks conglomerate that owns the brand, told press this week that demand for the stout in October and November 2024 had surpassed even the amount called for during St Patrick's Day celebrations, noting that the clamour was "unprecedented." Crew also stated that Diageo is spending €200m (£170m) on a new Guinness factory in Kildare to keep supplies up to the level now required.
tgt_seg: 尽管健力士可能在那些排队进入面包店的人中失去了其独特的魅力，但这对其利润几乎没有影响。它已经超越了邪教地位，本质上变得太大而不能失败。Diageo 饮料集团首席执行官 Debra Crew 告诉媒体，2024 年 10 月和 11 月对健力士的需求已经超过了圣帕特里克节庆祝活动期间的需求，并指出这种需求是“前所未有的”。Crew 还表示，Diageo 正在为 Kildare 的新健力士工厂投资 2 亿欧元（1.7 亿英镑），以确保供应量达到目前所需的水平。

src_seg: Music to my ears, really - I'm just pleased that while years ago you could walk into a pub and reasonably expect that Guinness wouldn't be served there, these days I can pretty much get my preferred pint anywhere. It has surpassed cult status, and has in essence become too big to fail. Debra Crew, chief executive of Diageo, the drinks conglomerate that owns the brand, told press this week that demand for the stout in October and November 2024 had surpassed even the amount called for during St Patrick's Day celebrations, noting that the clamour was "unprecedented." Crew also stated that Diageo is spending €200m (£170m) on a new Guinness factory in Kildare to keep supplies up to the level now required.
tgt_seg: 虽然健力士可能面临在面包店门前排队的顾客群中失去市场份额的重大风险，但这对其盈利根本不构成威胁。它已经超越了经典饮品的地位，规模庞大到足以无往不利。拥有该品牌的饮料巨头百利酿酒公司首席执行官德布拉·克鲁（Debra Crew）本周在接受采访时表示，2023 年 10 月和 11 月对健力士的需求甚至超过了圣帕特里克节时的需求，并评论称这种需求“史无前例”。她还提到，百利酿酒公司耗资 2 亿欧元（1 亿 7 千万英镑）在基尔代尔郡（Kildare）建设新工厂，以保持供应量达到当前需求水平。

src_seg: Music to my ears, really - I'm just pleased that while years ago you could walk into a pub and reasonably expect that Guinness wouldn't be served there, these days I can pretty much get my preferred pint anywhere. And, among all of the arguments to explain the surge in approval for the drink, it is important to acknowledge the obvious one: its smooth texture and subtly rich taste do just combine to offer something genuinely delicious, even when you get a mediocre one.
tgt_seg: 这听起来令人振奋——几年前，只要你走进一家酒吧，基本上就能预料到不会卖Guinness，但今天我几乎可以在任何地方买到我喜欢的那种啤酒。在众多解释这种饮料之所以备受欢迎的理论中，最显而易见的是：其细腻的质地和微妙的丰富味道组合在一起，即使喝到一杯不怎么好的啤酒，也能令人品尝到美妙的感觉。

src_seg: Ultimately, I'm more than happy to let the hype move on to a less obvious drink (over the past couple of weeks, I've been in two south-east London pubs that have recently installed the rival stout Murphy's, owing to local demand - go figure). Because as annoying as social media Guinness chat might be, and despite the extent to which the Schooner Scorer's camera angles haunt my nightmares (I mean it, don't Google it), it's like a wise man called Robbie Williams once sang: "You can't argue with popularity. Well you could, but you'd be wrong."
tgt_seg: 最终，我乐见这股热潮转移到其他不那么显眼的饮品上（过去几周，伦敦东南部的两家酒吧因顾客需求增加，相继引进了另一种啤酒——墨菲斯 (Murphy’s)）。因为社交媒体上的健力士啤酒话题虽然令人厌烦，尽管那艘运酒船的镜头一直困扰着我的夜晚梦境（我是认真的，不要 Google 它）。但正如罗比·威廉姆斯 (Robbie Williams) 曾经唱的那句歌词所道出：“无法质疑其受欢迎程度。如果你敢质疑，那你肯定是错的。”

src_seg: This will be the year that Guinness loses its cool. Cheers to that!

src_seg: I'm not sure I can remember exactly when I sensed it. Maybe it was when some of the more gimmicky London pubs introduced "stamp cards" to ration out Guinness after news of a shortage; maybe it was when I was served the 500th London Guinness rating video by my Instagram algorithm. Regardless of the precise moment the notion arrived, however, I have felt for a while that we are heading for a change when it comes to the pint du jour. For a few years now, Guinness has been the fashionable choice for millennial and gen Z drinkers, swept up in the aesthetic renaissance of the Good Old-Fashioned Bloody Pub. But I think the tide is turning. This will probably be the year that the Irish stout stops being cool.
tgt_seg: 我不确定我能确切地记得我是什么时候感觉到的。 也许是当一些比较噱头的伦敦酒吧推出"邮票卡"在短缺消息后定量配给吉尼斯时;也许是当我通过我的instagram算法获得第500届伦敦吉尼斯评级视频时。 然而，不管这个概念是在什么时候到来的，我有一段时间觉得我们正在改变品脱。 几年来，吉尼斯一直是千禧一代和z世代饮酒者的时尚选择，在老式血腥酒吧的美学复兴中席卷而来。 但我认为潮流正在转向。 这可能是爱尔兰粗壮停止冷静的一年。

src_seg: I'm pretty sure that what will finally usher the Guinness hype train back into the station will be the same thing that came for Aperol spritzes and truffle: overexposure. The Aperol, once a genuinely trendy, vaguely Sex and the City-ish aperitivo-style drink is now a cultural behemoth in its own right - delicious, certainly, but definitely no longer "cool." And truffle, well ... would you like a side of truffle fries for that truffle mac and cheese garnished with truffle oil?
tgt_seg: 我很确定，最终将迎来吉尼斯炒作火车回到车站的将是Aperol spritzes和truffle的同样的事情：过度曝光。 Aperol曾经是一种真正时尚，隐约的性爱和城市风格的开胃酒，现在本身就是一种文化庞然大物-美味，当然，但绝对不再"酷"。"还有松露。.. 你想吃块菌薯条和用块菌油装饰的奶酪吗？

src_seg: Overexposure, of course, is the death knell for cool in most cases (or at least self-conscious, trend-following "coolness," as I mean it here). This is particularly true amid the one-upmanship of contemporary food and drink culture which, as defined by social media, is always about being the first to find the undiscovered or most novel thing - the "hidden gem," the bakery and "pasta space" in London's zone 6 or what have you ("Come with me to the pub in Richmond that regularly floods"). And while Guinness's current round of popularity began because it was once viewed among younger pubgoers as a left-field choice - an "if you know, you know" order - it now couldn't be less of a secret.
tgt_seg: 当然，在大多数情况下，过度曝光是冷静的丧钟（或者至少是自我意识，追随潮流的"冷静"，就像我在这里的意思一样）。 在当代食品和饮料文化的一举一动中尤其如此，正如社交媒体所定义的那样，它总是第一个找到未被发现或最新颖的东西--伦敦6区的"隐藏的宝石"、面包店和"意大利面空间"，或者你有什么（"和我一起去里士满经常泛滥的酒吧"）。 虽然吉尼斯目前的受欢迎程度是因为它曾经在年轻的酒吧观众中被视为左场选择-一个"如果你知道，你知道"的命令-现在它不能少于一个秘密。

src_seg: Undeniably, Guinness is everywhere. For the 2024-25 season, it shafted Budweiser to become the official beer of the Premier League, and will hold this honour for the next four years. It is the official beer of rugby's Six Nations tournament (meaning that for the next month, it is also the official beer of people called Henry). And a few months ago, news broke that the brand will be opening a Guinness Storehouse attraction, described as a "microbrewery and culture hub," in Covent Garden - despite the fact that London has nothing to do with Guinness or its 250-year-old heritage. Add to this the countless Hinge prompts about "splitting the G," and the impenetrable gaggle of gilets that pretty much always surrounds Soho's Guinness Disneyland, otherwise known as the wildly successful Devonshire pub, and you have to admit that the brand's cool stock is sinking.

src_seg: This will be the year that Guinness loses its cool. Cheers to that!

src_seg: I'm not sure I can remember exactly when I sensed it. Maybe it was when some of the more gimmicky London pubs introduced "stamp cards" to ration out Guinness after news of a shortage; maybe it was when I was served the 500th London Guinness rating video by my Instagram algorithm. Regardless of the precise moment the notion arrived, however, I have felt for a while that we are heading for a change when it comes to the pint du jour. For a few years now, Guinness has been the fashionable choice for millennial and gen Z drinkers, swept up in the aesthetic renaissance of the Good Old-Fashioned Bloody Pub. But I think the tide is turning. This will probably be the year that the Irish stout stops being cool.
tgt_seg: 我不太确定自己何时开始感受到这一点。也许是当一些较为哗众取宠的伦敦酒吧推出“印章卡”，以配合缺货的消息时；也许是当我的 Instagram 算法为我推送了第五百个伦敦吉尼斯评分视频时。不论这个念头何时出现，我感到一种变化即将来临，涉及每日的啤酒选择。近几年来，吉尼斯在千禧一代和 Z 世代饮酒者中一直是时尚之选，融入了复古酒吧的审美复兴之中。但我认为潮流正在转变。今年可能会是这款爱尔兰黑啤停止流行的一年。

src_seg: I'm pretty sure that what will finally usher the Guinness hype train back into the station will be the same thing that came for Aperol spritzes and truffle: overexposure. The Aperol, once a genuinely trendy, vaguely Sex and the City-ish aperitivo-style drink is now a cultural behemoth in its own right - delicious, certainly, but definitely no longer "cool." And truffle, well ... would you like a side of truffle fries for that truffle mac and cheese garnished with truffle oil?
tgt_seg: 我相当确定，最终将把吉尼斯热度送回站台的，正是导致阿佩罗尔·斯普里茨和松露凉菜失去吸引力的同一原因：过度曝光。阿佩罗尔曾是一个真正时尚、略带《欲望都市》风格的开胃饮品，如今则成为了自己的文化巨头——当然美味，但肯定不再“酷”。至于松露……你想要松露味薯条搭配松露味奶酪吗？

src_seg: Overexposure, of course, is the death knell for cool in most cases (or at least self-conscious, trend-following "coolness," as I mean it here). This is particularly true amid the one-upmanship of contemporary food and drink culture which, as defined by social media, is always about being the first to find the undiscovered or most novel thing - the "hidden gem," the bakery and "pasta space" in London's zone 6 or what have you ("Come with me to the pub in Richmond that regularly floods"). And while Guinness's current round of popularity began because it was once viewed among younger pubgoers as a left-field choice - an "if you know, you know" order - it now couldn't be less of a secret.
tgt_seg: 过度曝光，当然，在大多数情况下是流行魅力的丧钟（或者至少我所指的那种自我意识的、追随潮流的“酷”）。在当今的饮食文化中尤为如此，这种文化在社交媒体的定义下，始终是关于优先发现未被发掘的独特事物——“隐藏的瑰宝”、位于伦敦第六区的面包店和“意大利面餐馆”，或者类似的地方（“跟我来，去那个常常被淹的里士满酒吧”）。而吉尼斯目前的流行因其曾被年轻酒客视作冷门选择——“知道的人才知道”的点单——如今已经显得不再是秘密。

src_seg: Undeniably, Guinness is everywhere. For the 2024-25 season, it shafted Budweiser to become the official beer of the Premier League, and will hold this honour for the next four years. It is the official beer of rugby's Six Nations tournament (meaning that for the next month, it is also the official beer of people called Henry). And a few months ago, news broke that the brand will be opening a Guinness Storehouse attraction, described as a "microbrewery and culture hub," in Covent Garden - despite the fact that London has nothing to do with Guinness or its 250-year-old heritage. Add to this the countless Hinge prompts about "splitting the G," and the impenetrable gaggle of gilets that pretty much always surrounds Soho's Guinness Disneyland, otherwise known as the wildly successful Devonshire pub, and you have to admit that the brand's cool stock is sinking.
tgt_seg: 毋庸置疑，吉尼斯随处可见。在 2024-25 赛季，它取代百威成为英超联赛的官方啤酒，并将在接下来的四年中保持这一荣誉。它还是橄榄球六国锦标赛的官方啤酒（这意味着在接下来的一个月里，它也将成为名为亨利的人的官方啤酒）。几个月前，有消息称该品牌将在考文特花园开设一个吉尼斯博物馆，称为微酿酒厂和文化中心——尽管伦敦与吉尼斯或其 250 年的遗产毫无关系。再加上无数关于“分摊吉”的 Hinge 提示，以及围绕索霍吉尼斯迪士尼乐园（即备受欢迎的德文郡酒吧）几乎总是存在源源不断的羊毛背心，你不得不承认这个品牌的流行价值正在下降。

src_seg: I don't speak as a Guinness naysayer. On the contrary, I grew up with a Dublin man and former pub landlord for a grandfather, so reverence for the stout is all but in my blood. As such, Guinness is pretty much the only pint I regularly drink, and I'll even admit that I'm One Of Those People who has long-winded opinions about their favourite Guinness in London, and who really does believe that it differs in quality depending on where you order it (it's all in the gas, the installation and the line-cleaning).
tgt_seg: 我并不是一个吉尼斯的否定者。相反，我的祖父是来自都柏林的一位前酒吧老板，因此对这款黑啤的敬仰几乎已在我血液中流淌。因此，吉尼斯几乎是我定期饮用的唯一啤酒，我甚至承认自己是那些对伦敦最喜欢的吉尼斯有长篇大论看法的人，确实相信根据你点的地方，其质量会有所不同（这全在于气体、安装和清洗管道）。

src_seg: While Guinness may be at significant risk of losing its edge among, say, people who queue outside bakeries, this hardly matters to its bottom line. It has surpassed cult status, and has in essence become too big to fail. Debra Crew, chief executive of Diageo, the drinks conglomerate that owns the brand, told press this week that demand for the stout in October and November 2024 had surpassed even the amount called for during St Patrick's Day celebrations, noting that the clamour was "unprecedented." Crew also stated that Diageo is spending €200m (£170m) on a new Guinness factory in Kildare to keep supplies up to the level now required.
tgt_seg: 虽然吉尼斯在某些人群中，比如那些排队等待面包的人中，失去吸引力的风险显著，但这对其底线几乎毫无影响。它已超越了崇拜的地位，实际上变得太大而无法倒下。持有该品牌的饮品巨头帝亚吉欧的首席执行官黛布拉·克鲁本周向媒体透露，2024 年 10 月和 11 月对该款黑啤的需求甚至超出了圣帕特里克节庆祝时的需求，称这种热潮是“前所未有的。”克鲁还表示，帝亚吉欧正在凯尔代尔投资 2 亿欧元（1.7 亿英镑）建立新的吉尼斯工厂，以确保供应满足目前的需求。

src_seg: Music to my ears, really - I'm just pleased that while years ago you could walk into a pub and reasonably expect that Guinness wouldn't be served there, these days I can pretty much get my preferred pint anywhere. And, among all of the arguments to explain the surge in approval for the drink, it is important to acknowledge the obvious one: its smooth texture and subtly rich taste do just combine to offer something genuinely delicious, even when you get a mediocre one.
tgt_seg: 这真是对我耳边的好消息——我很高兴，虽然几年前你可能走进一个酒吧合理地预期不会在那里喝到吉尼斯，如今我几乎可以在任何地方都喝到我喜欢的啤酒。而在解释这款饮品好评激增的所有论点中，重要的是要承认一个明显的原因：其顺滑的质地和微妙丰富的口感确实组合在一起，提供了真正美味的享受，即便是当你喝到平庸的品种时。

src_seg: Ultimately, I'm more than happy to let the hype move on to a less obvious drink (over the past couple of weeks, I've been in two south-east London pubs that have recently installed the rival stout Murphy's, owing to local demand - go figure). Because as annoying as social media Guinness chat might be, and despite the extent to which the Schooner Scorer's camera angles haunt my nightmares (I mean it, don't Google it), it's like a wise man called Robbie Williams once sang: "You can't argue with popularity. Well you could, but you'd be wrong."

This is particularly true amid the one-upmanship of contemporary food and drink culture which, as defined by social media, is always about being the first to find the undiscovered or most novel thing - the "hidden gem," the bakery and "pasta space" in London's zone 6 or what have you ("Come with me to the pub in Richmond that regularly floods"). And while Guinness's current round of popularity began because it was once viewed among younger pubgoers as a left-field choice - an "if you know, you know" order - it now couldn't be less of a secret.
tgt_seg: 当然，过度曝光在大多数情况下都是“酷”的终结（或者说，我在这里指的是自我意识、追随潮流的“酷”。）这在当代餐饮文化的攀比中尤其如此，根据社交媒体的定义，总是要成为第一个发现未被发现或最新奇事物的人 - “隐藏的瑰宝”，伦敦6区的面包店和“意大利面馆”，或者其他什么（“跟我一起去里士满的酒吧，那里经常会淹水。”）虽然吉尼斯啤酒目前的流行始于它曾经被年轻的酒吧顾客视为一种另类选择 - 一种“如果你知道，你就知道”的点单 - 但现在它已经不再是一个秘密了。

src_seg: Undeniably, Guinness is everywhere. For the 2024-25 season, it shafted Budweiser to become the official beer of the Premier League, and will hold this honour for the next four years. It is the official beer of rugby's Six Nations tournament (meaning that for the next month, it is also the official beer of people called Henry). And a few months ago, news broke that the brand will be opening a Guinness Storehouse attraction, described as a "microbrewery and culture hub," in Covent Garden - despite the fact that London has nothing to do with Guinness or its 250-year-old heritage. Add to this the countless Hinge prompts about "splitting the G," and the impenetrable gaggle of gilets that pretty much always surrounds Soho's Guinness Disneyland, otherwise known as the wildly successful Devonshire pub, and you have to admit that the brand's cool stock is sinking.
tgt_seg: 无可否认，吉尼斯啤酒无处不在。在2024-25赛季，它取代百威成为英超联赛的官方啤酒，并将拥有这一荣誉四年。它是橄榄球六国锦标赛的官方啤酒（这意味着在接下来的一个月里，它也是叫亨利的人的官方啤酒）。几个月前，有消息称，该品牌将在伦敦的考文特花园开设一家吉尼斯啤酒厂，被称为“微型啤酒厂和文化中心”，尽管伦敦与吉尼斯啤酒及其250年的历史毫无关系。再加上关于“分账吉尼斯”的无数Hinge约会提示，以及围绕着伦敦的吉尼斯啤酒迪士尼，也就是广受欢迎的德文郡酒吧的围观者，你不得不承认，该品牌的酷感正在下降。

src_seg: I don't speak as a Guinness naysayer. On the contrary, I grew up with a Dublin man and former pub landlord for a grandfather, so reverence for the stout is all but in my blood. As such, Guinness is pretty much the only pint I regularly drink, and I'll even admit that I'm One Of Those People who has long-winded opinions about their favourite Guinness in London, and who really does believe that it differs in quality depending on where you order it (it's all in the gas, the installation and the line-cleaning).
tgt_seg: 我不是吉尼斯啤酒的反对者。相反，我的祖父是都柏林人，曾是一名酒吧老板，所以对黑啤的敬意几乎融入了我的血液。因此，吉尼斯啤酒几乎是我经常喝的唯一一杯啤酒，我甚至承认我是那种对伦敦的吉尼斯啤酒有长篇大论的人，并且真的相信，根据你点单的地点，它的质量会有所不同（一切都取决于气体、安装和清洗管道）。

src_seg: While Guinness may be at significant risk of losing its edge among, say, people who queue outside bakeries, this hardly matters to its bottom line. It has surpassed cult status, and has in essence become too big to fail. Debra Crew, chief executive of Diageo, the drinks conglomerate that owns the brand, told press this week that demand for the stout in October and November 2024 had surpassed even the amount called for during St Patrick's Day celebrations, noting that the clamour was "unprecedented." Crew also stated that Diageo is spending €200m (£170m) on a new Guinness factory in Kildare to keep supplies up to the level now required.
tgt_seg: 虽然吉尼斯啤酒在说队列在面包店外排队的人群中失去吸引力，但这对它的底线影响不大。它已经超越了邪教地位，本质上已经变得不可或缺。吉尼斯啤酒的母公司帝亚吉欧首席执行官黛布拉·克鲁本周告诉媒体，2024年10月和11月的黑啤需求甚至超过了圣帕特里克节庆祝活动期间的需求，并指出这种需求是“前所未有的”。克鲁还表示，帝亚吉欧正在斥资2亿欧元（1.7亿英镑）在基尔代尔建造一座新的吉尼斯啤酒厂，以满足目前所需的供应量。

src_seg: Music to my ears, really - I'm just pleased that while years ago you could walk into a pub and reasonably expect that Guinness wouldn't be served there, these days I can pretty much get my preferred pint anywhere. And, among all of the arguments to explain the surge in approval for the drink, it is important to acknowledge the obvious one: its smooth texture and subtly rich taste do just combine to offer something genuinely delicious, even when you get a mediocre one.
tgt_seg: 这真是我耳中的音乐 - 我只是高兴，几年前你走进一家酒吧，合理地期望那里不会供应吉尼斯啤酒，而现在，我几乎可以在任何地方得到我喜欢的啤酒。而且，在解释这种饮料受欢迎程度激增的所有论点中，重要的是要承认一个显而易见的事实：即使你得到了一杯平庸的啤酒，它的顺滑质地和微妙丰富的味道也确实结合在一起，提供了真正美味的体验。

src_seg: Ultimately, I'm more than happy to let the hype move on to a less obvious drink (over the past couple of weeks, I've been in two south-east London pubs that have recently installed the rival stout Murphy's, owing to local demand - go figure). Because as annoying as social media Guinness chat might be, and despite the extent to which the Schooner Scorer's camera angles haunt my nightmares (I mean it, don't Google it), it's like a wise man called Robbie Williams once sang: "You can't argue with popularity. Well you could, but you'd be wrong."
tgt_seg: 最终，我很乐意让这种热潮转移到一种不太显眼的饮料上（在过去的几周里，我在伦敦东南部有两家酒吧最近安装了竞争对手的麦芽威士忌，因为当地需求 - 很难理解）。因为尽管社交媒体上的吉尼斯啤酒聊天可能很烦人，尽管Schooner Scorer的镜头角度在我的噩梦中挥之不去（我是认真的，不要搜索它），但正如一位名叫罗比·威廉姆斯的智者曾经唱的那样：“你不能与流行相争。好吧，你可以，但你会错的。”

Regardless of the precise moment the notion arrived, however, I have felt for a while that we are heading for a change when it comes to the pint du jour. tgt_seg: 我并非对吉尼斯啤酒持否定态度。恰恰相反，我的祖父是一位都柏林人，曾经经营酒吧，我对这种黑啤酒的敬意根深蒂固。因此，吉尼斯啤酒几乎是我常喝的唯一一种啤酒，我甚至承认自己是那些对伦敦最爱的吉尼斯啤酒有着详细的看法的人，并且确实相信它的品质会因购买地点而异（取决于气体、安装和清洁管道）。

src_seg: While Guinness may be at significant risk of losing its edge among, say, people who queue outside bakeries, this hardly matters to its bottom line. It has surpassed cult status, and has in essence become too big to fail. Debra Crew, chief executive of Diageo, the drinks conglomerate that owns the brand, told press this week that demand for the stout in October and November 2024 had surpassed even the amount called for during St Patrick's Day celebrations, noting that the clamour was "unprecedented." Crew also stated that Diageo is spending €200m (£170m) on a new Guinness factory in Kildare to keep supplies up to the level now required.
tgt_seg: 尽管吉尼斯啤酒可能在例如经常排队购买面包的人群中面临失去吸引力的风险，但这对其盈利状况影响甚微。它已经超越了 cult 级地位，本质上已成为“不可失败”的品牌。拥有该品牌的饮料集团——迪亚吉欧首席执行官戴布拉·克鲁本周向媒体表示，2024年10月和11月的吉尼斯啤酒需求甚至超过了圣帕特里克节期间的销量，她称之为“前所未有”。克鲁还表示，迪亚吉欧正在爱尔兰的基尔达投资2亿欧元，相当于170亿英镑，建设一座新的吉尼斯啤酒厂，以满足目前所需的供应量。

src_seg: Music to my ears, really - I'm just pleased that while years ago you could walk into a pub and reasonably expect that Guinness wouldn't be served there, these days I can pretty much get my preferred pint anywhere. And, among all of the arguments to explain the surge in approval for the drink, it is important to acknowledge the obvious one: its smooth texture and subtly rich taste do just combine to offer something genuinely delicious, even when you get a mediocre one.
tgt_seg: 确实令人欣慰——我很高兴的是，过去走进酒吧，你很可能找不到吉尼斯啤酒，而现在，几乎可以在任何地方喝到我喜欢的这款啤酒。在解释这款啤酒声誉日益提升的各种原因时，不得不承认一个显而易见的事实：其顺滑的口感和微妙醇厚的味道确实完美结合，即使是品质一般的吉尼斯啤酒，也依然令人感到美味。

src_seg: Ultimately, I'm more than happy to let the hype move on to a less obvious drink (over the past couple of weeks, I've been in two south-east London pubs that have recently installed the rival stout Murphy's, owing to local demand - go figure). Because as annoying as social media Guinness chat might be, and despite the extent to which the Schooner Scorer's camera angles haunt my nightmares (I mean it, don't Google it), it's like a wise man called Robbie Williams once sang: "You can't argue with popularity. Well you could, but you'd be wrong."
tgt_seg: 最终，我很高兴看到这种关注转移到其他不太常见的饮品上（在过去的几周里，我去了位于东南伦敦的两家酒吧，他们最近安装了竞争对手麦克维格斯黑啤酒，这满足了当地的需求——也挺有趣的）。尽管社交媒体上关于吉尼斯啤酒的讨论令人厌烦，而且即使我仍然被比赛中的摄像头角度影响着（我真的说的是，请不要在网上搜索），但就像一位名叫罗比·威廉姆斯的智者唱过的那样：“你无法否认受欢迎的力量。你可以尝试，但你会是错的。”

src_seg: This will be the year that Guinness loses its cool. Cheers to that!
tgt_seg: 今年将是健力士失去酷炫魅力的一年。为此干杯！

src_seg: I'm not sure I can remember exactly when I sensed it. Maybe it was when some of the more gimmicky London pubs introduced "stamp cards" to ration out Guinness after news of a shortage; maybe it was when I was served the 500th London Guinness rating video by my Instagram algorithm. Regardless of the precise moment the notion arrived, however, I have felt for a while that we are heading for a change when it comes to the pint du jour. For a few years now, Guinness has been the fashionable choice for millennial and gen Z drinkers, swept up in the aesthetic renaissance of the Good Old-Fashioned Bloody Pub. But I think the tide is turning. This will probably be the year that the Irish stout stops being cool.
tgt_seg: 我不确定我是否能准确回忆起我何时察觉到这一点。也许是在一些更具噱头的伦敦酒吧引入“集点卡”以配给健力士的消息传出后；也许是在我的Instagram算法向我推送了第500个伦敦健力士评级视频时。然而，无论这个想法是在何时出现的，我已经感觉到我们正在迎来一个关于当日啤酒的变化。多年来，健力士一直是千禧一代和Z世代饮酒者的时尚选择，他们被复古风格的“老式英式酒吧”的美学复兴所吸引。但我觉得潮流正在转变。今年可能是爱尔兰黑啤酒不再酷炫的一年。

src_seg: I'm pretty sure that what will finally usher the Guinness hype train back into the station will be the same thing that came for Aperol spritzes and truffle: overexposure. The Aperol, once a genuinely trendy, vaguely Sex and the City-ish aperitivo-style drink is now a cultural behemoth in its own right - delicious, certainly, but definitely no longer "cool." And truffle, well ... would you like a side of truffle fries for that truffle mac and cheese garnished with truffle oil?
tgt_seg: 我相当确定，最终将健力士热潮带回起点的将是与阿佩罗开胃酒和松露相同的原因：过度曝光。阿佩罗，曾经是一种真正时尚、略带《欲望都市》风格的开胃酒，现在已经成为一种文化巨兽 - 当然美味，但绝对不再“酷炫”。至于松露，嗯……你想来一份松露薯条搭配松露油调味的松露通心粉和奶酪吗？

src_seg: Overexposure, of course, is the death knell for cool in most cases (or at least self-conscious, trend-following "coolness," as I mean it here). This is particularly true amid the one-upmanship of contemporary food and drink culture which, as defined by social media, is always about being the first to find the undiscovered or most novel thing - the "hidden gem," the bakery and "pasta space" in London's zone 6 or what have you ("Come with me to the pub in Richmond that regularly floods"). And while Guinness's current round of popularity began because it was once viewed among younger pubgoers as a left-field choice - an "if you know, you know" order - it now couldn't be less of a secret.
tgt_seg: 当然，过度曝光在大多数情况下（或者至少是自我意识的、追逐潮流的“酷炫”，正如我在这里所指的）是酷炫的丧钟。在当代食品和饮料文化中，这种现象尤其明显，这种文化由社交媒体定义，总是关于成为第一个发现未被发现或最独特事物的人 - “隐藏的宝石”，伦敦6区的面包店和“意大利面空间”，或者类似的东西（“跟我去经常被淹的里士满酒吧”）。虽然健力士目前的流行始于它曾被视为年轻酒吧顾客的另类选择 - 一种“如果你懂，你就懂”的点单 - 但现在它已经不再是秘密了。

src_seg: Undeniably, Guinness is everywhere. For the 2024-25 season, it shafted Budweiser to become the official beer of the Premier League, and will hold this honour for the next four years. It is the official beer of rugby's Six Nations tournament (meaning that for the next month, it is also the official beer of people called Henry). And a few months ago, news broke that the brand will be opening a Guinness Storehouse attraction, described as a "microbrewery and culture hub," in Covent Garden - despite the fact that London has nothing to do with Guinness or its 250-year-old heritage. Add to this the countless Hinge prompts about "splitting the G," and the impenetrable gaggle of gilets that pretty much always surrounds Soho's Guinness Disneyland, otherwise known as the wildly successful Devonshire pub, and you have to admit that the brand's cool stock is sinking.

tgt_seg: 说真的，这对我来说真是天籁之音——我只是很高兴，几年前走进一家酒吧，你很可能会发现那里不卖健力士，而如今我几乎在哪儿都能喝到我偏爱的那一杯。在所有解释这款饮品为何广受欢迎的论点中，有一个显而易见的原因不容忽视：它柔滑的口感和微妙丰富的味道相结合，确实带来了真正的美味，即使你喝到的是一杯平庸之作。

src_seg: Ultimately, I'm more than happy to let the hype move on to a less obvious drink (over the past couple of weeks, I've been in two south-east London pubs that have recently installed the rival stout Murphy's, owing to local demand - go figure). Because as annoying as social media Guinness chat might be, and despite the extent to which the Schooner Scorer's camera angles haunt my nightmares (I mean it, don't Google it), it's like a wise man called Robbie Williams once sang: "You can't argue with popularity. Well you could, but you'd be wrong."
tgt_seg: 归根结底，我很乐意看到这股热潮转向其他不那么显眼、但同样受欢迎的饮品（过去几周，我光顾的两家位于伦敦东南部的酒吧都因当地消费者的需求，新引进了竞争对手品牌墨菲黑啤（Murphy’s Stout）——这正说明市场总在变化）。尽管社交媒体上关于健力士（Guinness）的讨论令人感到厌烦，尽管“Schooner Scorer”那种诡异的拍摄角度总在我的噩梦中反复出现（说真的，别去谷歌搜索），但正如那位名叫罗比·威廉姆斯（Robbie Williams）的智者所唱的那样：“你无法与流行趋势抗衡。当然你可以尝试，但结果只会是失败。”

src_seg: This will be the year that Guinness loses its cool. Cheers to that!
tgt_seg: 今年将是健力士（Guinness）失去其酷炫光环的一年。为此干杯！

src_seg: I'm not sure I can remember exactly when I sensed it. Maybe it was when some of the more gimmicky London pubs introduced "stamp cards" to ration out Guinness after news of a shortage; maybe it was when I was served the 500th London Guinness rating video by my Instagram algorithm. Regardless of the precise moment the notion arrived, however, I have felt for a while that we are heading for a change when it comes to the pint du jour. For a few years now, Guinness has been the fashionable choice for millennial and gen Z drinkers, swept up in the aesthetic renaissance of the Good Old-Fashioned Bloody Pub. But I think the tide is turning. This will probably be the year that the Irish stout stops being cool.
tgt_seg: 我不确定自己是何时察觉到这一点的。或许是当一些比较花哨的伦敦酒吧在健力士短缺的消息传出后，推出了“盖章卡”来限量供应；又或许是当我的Instagram算法给我推送了第500个伦敦健力士评分视频时。然而，无论这个念头是何时出现的，我一直感觉，在“当日特选啤酒”这个话题上，我们正迎来一场变革。几年来，健力士一直是千禧一代和Z世代饮酒者的时尚之选，他们沉浸在“纯正老式酒吧”美学的复兴浪潮中。但我认为潮流正在转向，今年可能就是这款爱尔兰黑啤不再 “酷” 的一年。

src_seg: I'm pretty sure that what will finally usher the Guinness hype train back into the station will be the same thing that came for Aperol spritzes and truffle: overexposure. The Aperol, once a genuinely trendy, vaguely Sex and the City-ish aperitivo-style drink is now a cultural behemoth in its own right - delicious, certainly, but definitely no longer "cool." And truffle, well ... would you like a side of truffle fries for that truffle mac and cheese garnished with truffle oil?
tgt_seg: 我敢肯定，最终让健力士这股炒作热潮退去的，将是与阿佩罗橙光鸡尾酒（Aperol spritz）和松露同样的遭遇：过度曝光。曾几何时，阿佩罗是一款真正时髦、带有些许《欲望都市》风格的开胃酒，如今它本身已成为一个文化巨头——味道当然不错，但绝对不再“酷”了。至于松露，嗯……您点的松露通心粉，要不要配一份淋上松露油的松露薯条？

src_seg: Overexposure, of course, is the death knell for cool in most cases (or at least self-conscious, trend-following "coolness," as I mean it here). This is particularly true amid the one-upmanship of contemporary food and drink culture which, as defined by social media, is always about being the first to find the undiscovered or most novel thing - the "hidden gem," the bakery and "pasta space" in London's zone 6 or what have you ("Come with me to the pub in Richmond that regularly floods"). And while Guinness's current round of popularity began because it was once viewed among younger pubgoers as a left-field choice - an "if you know, you know" order - it now couldn't be less of a secret.
tgt_seg: 当然，在大多数情况下，过度曝光是“酷”的丧钟（至少是我在此所指的那种刻意追逐潮流的“酷”）。在当代饮食文化的攀比心态中尤其如此，这种文化由社交媒体定义，永远追求第一个发现未被发掘或最新奇的事物——所谓的“隐藏的宝藏”，比如伦敦六区的面包店和“意面空间”，或是别的什么（“跟我去里士满那家经常被水淹的酒吧”）。虽然健力士当前的这轮流行之所以兴起，是因为它曾被年轻的泡吧族视为一种出人意料的选择——一种“懂的都懂”的点单——但现在，它早已不是什么秘密了。

src_seg: Undeniably, Guinness is everywhere. For the 2024-25 season, it shafted Budweiser to become the official beer of the Premier League, and will hold this honour for the next four years. It is the official beer of rugby's Six Nations tournament (meaning that for the next month, it is also the official beer of people called Henry). And a few months ago, news broke that the brand will be opening a Guinness Storehouse attraction, described as a "microbrewery and culture hub," in Covent Garden - despite the fact that London has nothing to do with Guinness or its 250-year-old heritage. Add to this the countless Hinge prompts about "splitting the G," and the impenetrable gaggle of gilets that pretty much always surrounds Soho's Guinness Disneyland, otherwise known as the wildly successful Devonshire pub, and you have to admit that the brand's cool stock is sinking.
tgt_seg: 不可否认，健力士无处不在。在2024-25赛季，它取代了百威，成为英超联赛的官方啤酒，并将在未来四年保持这一荣誉。它还是六国橄榄球锦标赛的官方啤酒（这意味着在接下来的一个月里，它也成了那些名叫亨利的人的官方啤酒）。几个月前，有消息称该品牌将在科文特花园开设一个健力士啤酒展览馆景点，被称为“微型酿酒厂和文化中心”——尽管伦敦与健力士及其250年的历史并无关联。再加上交友软件Hinge上无数关于“分享一杯G”（G指Guinness）的个人简介，以及在苏荷区那家被称为健力士迪士尼乐园、大获成功的德文郡酒吧周围，总是围着一群穿着马甲、挤都挤不进去的人。你不得不承认，该品牌的“酷”值正在下降。

src_seg: I don't speak as a Guinness naysayer. On the contrary, I grew up with a Dublin man and former pub landlord for a grandfather, so reverence for the stout is all but in my blood. As such, Guinness is pretty much the only pint I regularly drink, and I'll even admit that I'm One Of Those People who has long-winded opinions about their favourite Guinness in London, and who really does believe that it differs in quality depending on where you order it (it's all in the gas, the installation and the line-cleaning).
tgt_seg: 我这么说，并非是健力士的反对者。恰恰相反，我的外祖父是一位都柏林人，也曾是酒吧老板，所以对这款烈性黑啤的敬畏几乎融入了我的血液。因此，健力士几乎是我常喝的唯一一种品脱啤酒，我甚至承认我就是那种人——对伦敦哪里的健力士最好喝有长篇大论，我真心认为，根据点酒地点的不同，这酒的品质也会有所差异（全在于气泡、设备安装和管道清洁）。

src_seg: While Guinness may be at significant risk of losing its edge among, say, people who queue outside bakeries, this hardly matters to its bottom line. It has surpassed cult status, and has in essence become too big to fail. Debra Crew, chief executive of Diageo, the drinks conglomerate that owns the brand, told press this week that demand for the stout in October and November 2024 had surpassed even the amount called for during St Patrick's Day celebrations, noting that the clamour was "unprecedented." Crew also stated that Diageo is spending €200m (£170m) on a new Guinness factory in Kildare to keep supplies up to the level now required.
tgt_seg: 虽然健力士在那些喜欢在面包店外排队的人群中可能面临失去其前卫优势的巨大风险，但这对其利润几乎没有影响。它已经超越了小众追捧的地位，基本上变得“大到不能倒”。拥有该品牌的酒业集团帝亚吉欧（Diageo）的首席执行官黛布拉·克鲁本周告诉媒体，2024年10月和11月对这款烈性黑啤的需求甚至超过了圣帕特里克节庆祝活动期间的需求量，并指出这种热潮是“前所未有的”。克鲁还表示，帝亚吉欧正斥资2亿欧元（合1.7亿英镑）在基尔代尔新建一家健力士工厂，以满足当前所需的供应水平。

tgt_seg: 我不确定我是否能准确地记得我是什么时候察觉到的。也许是在一些更花哨的伦敦酒吧在短缺消息传来后推出“盖章卡”来限量供应健力士啤酒时；也许是我在Instagram算法推送给我第500个伦敦健力士啤酒评分视频时。然而，无论这个概念出现的准确时刻是什么，我有一段时间一直觉得，我们正在走向日常一杯啤酒的变化。几年来，健力士一直是千禧一代和Z世代饮酒者的时尚选择，他们被古老的“血腥酒吧”美学复兴所吸引。但我认为潮流正在改变。今年很可能是爱尔兰黑啤不再酷的年份。

src_seg: I'm pretty sure that what will finally usher the Guinness hype train back into the station will be the same thing that came for Aperol spritzes and truffle: overexposure. The Aperol, once a genuinely trendy, vaguely Sex and the City-ish aperitivo-style drink is now a cultural behemoth in its own right - delicious, certainly, but definitely no longer "cool." And truffle, well ... would you like a side of truffle fries for that truffle mac and cheese garnished with truffle oil?
tgt_seg: 我敢肯定，最终让金氏世界纪录的热潮回归正轨的，将与 Aperol spritzes 和松露一样，是过度曝光。Aperol 曾经是一种真正时尚的、略带《欲望都市》风格的开胃酒，现在它本身就是一种文化巨头——美味，当然，但绝对不再“酷”。至于松露，嗯……你想在配有松露油的松露蛋奶粉旁边再加一份松露薯条吗？

src_seg: Overexposure, of course, is the death knell for cool in most cases (or at least self-conscious, trend-following "coolness," as I mean it here). This is particularly true amid the one-upmanship of contemporary food and drink culture which, as defined by social media, is always about being the first to find the undiscovered or most novel thing - the "hidden gem," the bakery and "pasta space" in London's zone 6 or what have you ("Come with me to the pub in Richmond that regularly floods"). And while Guinness's current round of popularity began because it was once viewed among younger pubgoers as a left-field choice - an "if you know, you know" order - it now couldn't be less of a secret.
tgt_seg: 当然，过度曝光在大多数情况下是酷感的丧钟（或者至少是我在这里所指的自我意识和追随潮流的“酷”。）这在当代餐饮文化的攀比中尤其明显，根据社交媒体的定义，它总是关于成为第一个发现未被发现或最新颖事物的人 - “隐藏的瑰宝”，伦敦第六区的面包店和“意大利面馆”，或者其他什么（“跟我一起去里士满的酒吧，那里经常会泛滥成灾。”）虽然吉尼斯啤酒目前的流行始于它曾经被年轻的酒吧顾客视为一种另类选择 - 一种“如果你知道，你就知道”的订单 - 但现在它已经不再是一个秘密了。

src_seg: Undeniably, Guinness is everywhere. For the 2024-25 season, it shafted Budweiser to become the official beer of the Premier League, and will hold this honour for the next four years. It is the official beer of rugby's Six Nations tournament (meaning that for the next month, it is also the official beer of people called Henry). And a few months ago, news broke that the brand will be opening a Guinness Storehouse attraction, described as a "microbrewery and culture hub," in Covent Garden - despite the fact that London has nothing to do with Guinness or its 250-year-old heritage. Add to this the countless Hinge prompts about "splitting the G," and the impenetrable gaggle of gilets that pretty much always surrounds Soho's Guinness Disneyland, otherwise known as the wildly successful Devonshire pub, and you have to admit that the brand's cool stock is sinking.
tgt_seg: 不可否认，健力士无处不在。对于2024-25赛季，它取代百威成为英超联赛的官方啤酒，并将拥有这一荣誉四年。它是橄榄球六国锦标赛的官方啤酒（这意味着在接下来的一个月里，它也是名叫亨利的人的官方啤酒）。几个月前，有消息称，该品牌将在伦敦的考文特花园开设一家健力士酒窖景点，被描述为“微型啤酒厂和文化中心”——尽管伦敦与健力士及其250年的历史毫无关系。再加上无数关于“分裂G”的Hinge提示，以及几乎总是围绕在苏荷区健力士迪士尼乐园（也称为非常成功的德文郡酒吧）周围的无法穿透的夹克群，不得不承认，该品牌的酷度正在下降。

src_seg: I don't speak as a Guinness naysayer. On the contrary, I grew up with a Dublin man and former pub landlord for a grandfather, so reverence for the stout is all but in my blood. As such, Guinness is pretty much the only pint I regularly drink, and I'll even admit that I'm One Of Those People who has long-winded opinions about their favourite Guinness in London, and who really does believe that it differs in quality depending on where you order it (it's all in the gas, the installation and the line-cleaning).
tgt_seg: 我不是吉尼斯啤酒的反对者。相反，我的祖父是都柏林人，曾是一名酒吧老板，因此我对黑啤酒的敬意几乎融入了我的血脉。因此，吉尼斯啤酒几乎是我唯一经常喝的啤酒，我甚至承认我是那种对伦敦最喜欢的吉尼斯啤酒有冗长观点的人，并且真的相信根据你点啤酒的地方不同，它的质量也会有所不同（这都归功于气体、安装和管道清洁）。

src_seg: While Guinness may be at significant risk of losing its edge among, say, people who queue outside bakeries, this hardly matters to its bottom line. It has surpassed cult status, and has in essence become too big to fail. Debra Crew, chief executive of Diageo, the drinks conglomerate that owns the brand, told press this week that demand for the stout in October and November 2024 had surpassed even the amount called for during St Patrick's Day celebrations, noting that the clamour was "unprecedented." Crew also stated that Diageo is spending €200m (£170m) on a new Guinness factory in Kildare to keep supplies up to the level now required.
tgt_seg: 虽然吉尼斯在面包房外排队等候的人群中可能会失去其优势，但这对其实际收益影响不大。它已经超越了崇拜状态，本质上已经变得不可或缺。吉尼斯品牌的所有者帝亚吉欧集团首席执行官黛布拉·克鲁（Debra Crew）本周告诉媒体，2024 年 10 月和 11 月对黑啤的需求甚至超过了圣帕特里克节庆祝活动期间的需求，并指出这种需求是“前所未有的”。克鲁还表示，帝亚吉欧集团正在斥资 2 亿欧元（1.7 亿英镑）在基尔代尔建造一家新的吉尼斯工厂，以保持供应量达到目前所需的水平。

src_seg: Music to my ears, really - I'm just pleased that while years ago you could walk into a pub and reasonably expect that Guinness wouldn't be served there, these days I can pretty much get my preferred pint anywhere. And, among all of the arguments to explain the surge in approval for the drink, it is important to acknowledge the obvious one: its smooth texture and subtly rich taste do just combine to offer something genuinely delicious, even when you get a mediocre one.

src_seg: Ultimately, I'm more than happy to let the hype move on to a less obvious drink (over the past couple of weeks, I've been in two south-east London pubs that have recently installed the rival stout Murphy's, owing to local demand - go figure). It is the official beer of rugby's Six Nations tournament (meaning that for the next month, it is also the official beer of people called Henry). And a few months ago, news broke that the brand will be opening a Guinness Storehouse attraction, described as a "microbrewery and culture hub," in Covent Garden - despite the fact that London has nothing to do with Guinness or its 250-year-old heritage. Add to this the countless Hinge prompts about "splitting the G," and the impenetrable gaggle of gilets that pretty much always surrounds Soho's Guinness Disneyland, otherwise known as the wildly successful Devonshire pub, and you have to admit that the brand's cool stock is sinking.
tgt_seg: 不可否认，健力士无处不在。2024-25赛季，它取代百威成为英超联赛官方啤酒，并将在未来四年保持这一荣誉。它还是橄榄球六国锦标赛的官方啤酒（这意味着在接下来的一个月里，它也是所有叫亨利的人的官方啤酒）。几个月前，有消息称该品牌将在考文特花园开设一家健力士体验馆，被描述为“微型酿酒厂和文化中心”——尽管伦敦与健力士及其250年的历史毫无关联。再加上无数关于“分G喝法”的交友软件提示，以及几乎总是围绕在索霍区健力士“迪士尼乐园”（即大获成功的Devonshire酒吧）外的羽绒马甲人群，不得不承认，这个品牌的“酷感”正在下滑。

src_seg: I don't speak as a Guinness naysayer. On the contrary, I grew up with a Dublin man and former pub landlord for a grandfather, so reverence for the stout is all but in my blood. As such, Guinness is pretty much the only pint I regularly drink, and I'll even admit that I'm One Of Those People who has long-winded opinions about their favourite Guinness in London, and who really does believe that it differs in quality depending on where you order it (it's all in the gas, the installation and the line-cleaning).
tgt_seg: 我并不是健力士的反对者。恰恰相反，我的祖父是都柏林人，也是前酒吧老板，对黑啤的敬仰几乎融入了我的血液。因此，健力士几乎是我唯一经常饮用的啤酒，我甚至承认自己是那种会对伦敦哪家健力士最好喝发表长篇大论的人，并且真的相信不同酒吧的健力士品质有所差异（关键在于气体、设备安装和管道清洁）。

src_seg: While Guinness may be at significant risk of losing its edge among, say, people who queue outside bakeries, this hardly matters to its bottom line. It has surpassed cult status, and has in essence become too big to fail. Debra Crew, chief executive of Diageo, the drinks conglomerate that owns the brand, told press this week that demand for the stout in October and November 2024 had surpassed even the amount called for during St Patrick's Day celebrations, noting that the clamour was "unprecedented." Crew also stated that Diageo is spending €200m (£170m) on a new Guinness factory in Kildare to keep supplies up to the level now required.
tgt_seg: 虽然健力士在那些会在面包店外排队的人群中，可能正面临失去吸引力的风险，但这对其业绩几乎没有影响。它早已超越小众，实际上已大到难以失败。拥有该品牌的饮品巨头帝亚吉欧首席执行官Debra Crew本周对媒体表示，2024年10月和11月对黑啤的需求甚至超过了圣帕特里克节期间的销量，称这种热度“前所未有”。Crew还表示，帝亚吉欧正在基尔代尔投资2亿欧元（1.7亿英镑）新建一家健力士工厂，以满足当前的供应需求。

src_seg: Music to my ears, really - I'm just pleased that while years ago you could walk into a pub and reasonably expect that Guinness wouldn't be served there, these days I can pretty much get my preferred pint anywhere. And, among all of the arguments to explain the surge in approval for the drink, it is important to acknowledge the obvious one: its smooth texture and subtly rich taste do just combine to offer something genuinely delicious, even when you get a mediocre one.
tgt_seg: 对我来说，这无疑是好消息——我很高兴，如今几乎在任何地方都能喝到我喜欢的这杯黑啤，而不是像过去那样走进酒吧还得担心没有健力士。在所有解释这款酒人气飙升的理由中，有一点必须承认：它顺滑的口感和细腻丰富的味道确实能带来真正的美味，即使偶尔喝到一杯中等水平的。

src_seg: Ultimately, I'm more than happy to let the hype move on to a less obvious drink (over the past couple of weeks, I've been in two south-east London pubs that have recently installed the rival stout Murphy's, owing to local demand - go figure). Because as annoying as social media Guinness chat might be, and despite the extent to which the Schooner Scorer's camera angles haunt my nightmares (I mean it, don't Google it), it's like a wise man called Robbie Williams once sang: "You can't argue with popularity. Well you could, but you'd be wrong."
tgt_seg: 归根结底，我非常乐意让热度转移到其他不那么显眼的酒品上（过去几周，我在伦敦东南部的两家酒吧发现它们因本地需求新上了竞争对手Murphy's黑啤——你品，你细品）。因为，尽管社交媒体上关于健力士的讨论令人厌烦，尽管Schooner Scorer的拍摄角度让我噩梦连连（我是认真的，别去搜），但正如一位名叫Robbie Williams的智者曾唱过的：“你无法与流行对抗。你可以试试，但你会错的。”

src_seg: This will be the year that Guinness loses its cool. Cheers to that!
tgt_seg: 今年，吉尼斯将失去冷静。 祝贺！

src_seg: I'm not sure I can remember exactly when I sensed it. Regardless of the precise moment the notion arrived, however, I have felt for a while that we are heading for a change when it comes to the pint du jour. For a few years now, Guinness has been the fashionable choice for millennial and gen Z drinkers, swept up in the aesthetic renaissance of the Good Old-Fashioned Bloody Pub. But I think the tide is turning. This will probably be the year that the Irish stout stops being cool.

src_seg: I'm pretty sure that what will finally usher the Guinness hype train back into the station will be the same thing that came for Aperol spritzes and truffle: overexposure. The Aperol, once a genuinely trendy, vaguely Sex and the City-ish aperitivo-style drink is now a cultural behemoth in its own right - delicious, certainly, but definitely no longer "cool." And truffle, well ... would you like a side of truffle fries for that truffle mac and cheese garnished with truffle oil?

Debra Crew, chief executive of Diageo, the drinks conglomerate that owns the brand, told press this week that demand for the stout in October and November 2024 had surpassed even the amount called for during St Patrick's Day celebrations, noting that the clamour was "unprecedented." Crew also stated that Diageo is spending €200m (£170m) on a new Guinness factory in Kildare to keep supplies up to the level now required.
tgt_seg: 虽然健力士在那些喜欢在面包店外排队的人群中可能面临失去其前卫优势的巨大风险，但这对其利润几乎没有影响。它已经超越了小众追捧的地位，基本上变得“大到不能倒”。拥有该品牌的酒业集团帝亚吉欧（Diageo）的首席执行官黛布拉·克鲁本周告诉媒体，2024年10月和11月对这款黑啤酒的需求甚至超过了圣帕特里克节庆祝活动期间的需求量，并指出这种热潮是“前所未有的”。克鲁还表示，帝亚吉欧正斥资2亿欧元（合1.7亿英镑）在基尔代尔新建一家健力士工厂，以满足当前所需的供应水平。

src_seg: Music to my ears, really - I'm just pleased that while years ago you could walk into a pub and reasonably expect that Guinness wouldn't be served there, these days I can pretty much get my preferred pint anywhere. And, among all of the arguments to explain the surge in approval for the drink, it is important to acknowledge the obvious one: its smooth texture and subtly rich taste do just combine to offer something genuinely delicious, even when you get a mediocre one.
tgt_seg: 这对我来说真是天籁之音——我只是很高兴，几年前你走进一家酒吧，很可能那里不卖健力士，而如今我几乎可以在任何地方喝到我喜欢的品脱。而且，在所有解释这款饮品受欢迎程度激增的论点中，我们必须承认一个显而易见的原因：它顺滑的口感和微妙丰富的味道相结合，确实提供了一种真正美味的体验，即便你喝到的是一杯平庸之作。

src_seg: Ultimately, I'm more than happy to let the hype move on to a less obvious drink (over the past couple of weeks, I've been in two south-east London pubs that have recently installed the rival stout Murphy's, owing to local demand - go figure). Because as annoying as social media Guinness chat might be, and despite the extent to which the Schooner Scorer's camera angles haunt my nightmares (I mean it, don't Google it), it's like a wise man called Robbie Williams once sang: "You can't argue with popularity. Well you could, but you'd be wrong."
tgt_seg: 归根结底，我非常乐意让这股热潮转向一种不那么大众的饮品（在过去几周里，我光顾的两家伦敦东南部的酒吧都因当地需求而新安装了其竞争对手墨菲黑啤的设备——谁能想到呢）。因为，尽管社交媒体上关于健力士的讨论可能很烦人，尽管那些啤酒评分博主的拍摄角度在我的噩梦中挥之不去（我是认真的，别去搜），但正如一位名叫罗比·威廉姆斯的智者曾经唱过的那样：“你无法与流行争辩。好吧，你可以争，但那样你就错了。”

src_seg: This will be the year that Guinness loses its cool. Cheers to that!
tgt_seg: 这将是Guinness失去风头的一年。干杯！

src_seg: I'm not sure I can remember exactly when I sensed it. Maybe it was when some of the more gimmicky London pubs introduced "stamp cards" to ration out Guinness after news of a shortage; maybe it was when I was served the 500th London Guinness rating video by my Instagram algorithm. Regardless of the precise moment the notion arrived, however, I have felt for a while that we are heading for a change when it comes to the pint du jour. For a few years now, Guinness has been the fashionable choice for millennial and gen Z drinkers, swept up in the aesthetic renaissance of the Good Old-Fashioned Bloody Pub. But I think the tide is turning. This will probably be the year that the Irish stout stops being cool.
tgt_seg: 我不确定我什么时候开始感觉到变化，也许是在一些更花哨的伦敦酒吧推出“邮票卡”来限量供应Guinness后，也许是在我的Instagram算法为我播放了第500个伦敦Guinness评分视频时。无论确切的时刻是什么，我都感觉我们正在走向一场关于每日一品脱的变化。几年来，Guinness一直是千禧一代和Z世代饮酒者的时尚选择，被卷入了古老的血腥酒吧的美学复兴。但我认为潮流正在转变。这将可能是Guinness不再时尚的一年。

src_seg: I'm pretty sure that what will finally usher the Guinness hype train back into the station will be the same thing that came for Aperol spritzes and truffle: overexposure. The Aperol, once a genuinely trendy, vaguely Sex and the City-ish aperitivo-style drink is now a cultural behemoth in its own right - delicious, certainly, but definitely no longer "cool." And truffle, well ... would you like a side of truffle fries for that truffle mac and cheese garnished with truffle oil?
tgt_seg: 我很确定最终会将Guinness的热潮带回站台的东西就是过度曝光。Aperol曾经是一款真正时尚的、略带《欲望都市》风格的aperitivo风格饮料，现在已经成为其自身的文化巨头——当然，它确实美味，但绝对不再“酷”。而Truffle，嗯，你想在那个Truffle mac and cheese上加一份Truffle fries吗？用Truffle oil调味的？

src_seg: Overexposure, of course, is the death knell for cool in most cases (or at least self-conscious, trend-following "coolness," as I mean it here). This is particularly true amid the one-upmanship of contemporary food and drink culture which, as defined by social media, is always about being the first to find the undiscovered or most novel thing - the "hidden gem," the bakery and "pasta space" in London's zone 6 or what have you ("Come with me to the pub in Richmond that regularly floods"). And while Guinness's current round of popularity began because it was once viewed among younger pubgoers as a left-field choice - an "if you know, you know" order - it now couldn't be less of a secret.
tgt_seg: 过度曝光当然是大多数情况下“酷”的死穴（或者至少是有意识的、追随潮流的“酷”，我这里指的是）。这在当代食物和饮料文化中尤其如此，它总是关于在社交媒体上成为第一个发现最新的或最独特的东西——“隐藏的瑰宝”，伦敦的zone 6的面包店和“面食空间”，或者什么的（“让我带你去 Richmond 的一家酒吧，那里经常淹水”）。而Guinness的当前流行始于年轻酒吧顾客将其视为另类选择——“如果你知道，你就知道”的订单——它现在已经不再是秘密。

src_seg: Undeniably, Guinness is everywhere. For the 2024-25 season, it shafted Budweiser to become the official beer of the Premier League, and will hold this honour for the next four years. It is the official beer of rugby's Six Nations tournament (meaning that for the next month, it is also the official beer of people called Henry). And a few months ago, news broke that the brand will be opening a Guinness Storehouse attraction, described as a "microbrewery and culture hub," in Covent Garden - despite the fact that London has nothing to do with Guinness or its 250-year-old heritage. Add to this the countless Hinge prompts about "splitting the G," and the impenetrable gaggle of gilets that pretty much always surrounds Soho's Guinness Disneyland, otherwise known as the wildly successful Devonshire pub, and you have to admit that the brand's cool stock is sinking.
tgt_seg: 不可否认，Guinness无处不在。在2024-25赛季，它取代Budweiser成为英超联赛的官方啤酒，并在接下来的四年里保持这一荣誉。它是六国杯橄榄球赛的官方啤酒（这意味着在接下来的一个月里，它也是那些叫Henry的人们的官方啤酒）。几个月前，新闻爆出该品牌将在伦敦的Covent Garden开设一个Guinness Storehouse景点，被描述为“微型酿酒厂和文化中心”——尽管伦敦与Guinness或其250年的历史毫无关系。再加上Hinge提示关于“分杯”的无数提示，以及围绕伦敦的Soho的Guinness迪士尼乐园（即成功的Devonshire酒吧）的难以穿透的围巾，你不得不承认品牌的“酷”正在下降。

src_seg: I don't speak as a Guinness naysayer. On the contrary, I grew up with a Dublin man and former pub landlord for a grandfather, so reverence for the stout is all but in my blood. As such, Guinness is pretty much the only pint I regularly drink, and I'll even admit that I'm One Of Those People who has long-winded opinions about their favourite Guinness in London, and who really does believe that it differs in quality depending on where you order it (it's all in the gas, the installation and the line-cleaning).
tgt_seg: 我不是Guinness的反对者。相反，我长大后有一个爱喝Guinness的都柏林人，他曾是我的祖父，酒馆老板，所以尊敬这款啤酒几乎是我血液中的一部分。因此，Guinness几乎是我唯一经常喝的啤酒，我甚至承认自己是伦敦人，对他们的Guinness有长篇大论的意见，并且真的相信它在不同的地方有不同的质量（这全在于气体、安装和清洁线）。

src_seg: While Guinness may be at significant risk of losing its edge among, say, people who queue outside bakeries, this hardly matters to its bottom line. It has surpassed cult status, and has in essence become too big to fail. Debra Crew, chief executive of Diageo, the drinks conglomerate that owns the brand, told press this week that demand for the stout in October and November 2024 had surpassed even the amount called for during St Patrick's Day celebrations, noting that the clamour was "unprecedented." Crew also stated that Diageo is spending €200m (£170m) on a new Guinness factory in Kildare to keep supplies up to the level now required.
tgt_seg: 虽然Guinness可能面临来自排队等候面包店的人等的显著风险，但这对其底线几乎没有影响。它已经超越了流行文化的地位，本质上已经变得太大而不能失败。Diageo的首席执行官Debra Crew，拥有该品牌的饮料公司，本周告诉媒体，2024年10月和11月的Guinness需求超过了圣帕特里克节庆祝活动期间的需求，并指出这种需求“前所未有”。Crew还表示，Diageo将投资2亿欧元（1.7亿英镑）在Kildare建造一家新的Guinness工厂，以满足目前的需求。

src_seg: Music to my ears, really - I'm just pleased that while years ago you could walk into a pub and reasonably expect that Guinness wouldn't be served there, these days I can pretty much get my preferred pint anywhere. And, among all of the arguments to explain the surge in approval for the drink, it is important to acknowledge the obvious one: its smooth texture and subtly rich taste do just combine to offer something genuinely delicious, even when you get a mediocre one.
tgt_seg: 对我来说，音乐真的很好听，我很高兴看到几年前你可以走进酒吧，合理地期待Guinness不会在那里供应，而现在我几乎可以在任何地方找到我喜欢的啤酒。而且，在所有解释Guinness饮料热潮的论点中，重要的是要承认一个明显的事实：它的顺滑质地和微妙丰富的口感确实结合在一起，提供了一种真正美味的东西，即使你喝到一杯平庸的啤酒。

src_seg: Ultimately, I'm more than happy to let the hype move on to a less obvious drink (over the past couple of weeks, I've been in two south-east London pubs that have recently installed the rival stout Murphy's, owing to local demand - go figure). Because as annoying as social media Guinness chat might be, and despite the extent to which the Schooner Scorer's camera angles haunt my nightmares (I mean it, don't Google it), it's like a wise man called Robbie Williams once sang: "You can't argue with popularity. Well you could, but you'd be wrong."
tgt_seg: 最终，我很高兴让热潮转移到不那么显眼的饮料上（过去几周，我在伦敦东南部的两家酒吧发现最近安装了竞争对手啤酒Murphy's，因为当地需求——去想象一下）。因为正如Robbie Williams曾经唱过的那句话：“你不能和流行作对。你可以，但你会错的。”

src_seg: Pig Heart Boy review - lively staging of Malorie Blackman's stimulating novel
tgt_seg: 《猪心男孩》评介 - 马洛里·布莱克曼原著小说的生动舞台演绎

src_seg: Some set designs instantly make sense. Paul Wills's clever arrangement of television screens and speakers, all linked up by glowing capillary-like tubes, encapsulates Malorie Blackman's 1997 novel about a boy whose pig-heart transplant leads to a media frenzy. Andrew Exeter's lighting switches from blood red to cool blue for scenes when 13-year-old Cameron repeatedly puts himself - and, eventually, his new heart - to the test when diving at his local pool.
tgt_seg: 有些舞台设计一眼就能理解。保罗·威尔斯巧妙地布置了电视屏幕和扬声器，用发光的毛细管状管道将它们连接起来，完美地诠释了马洛里·布莱克曼1997年的小说：一个男孩接受猪心移植后引发媒体狂热。安德鲁·埃克塞特的灯光设计在13岁的卡梅伦反复考验自己——以及最终他的新心脏——在当地游泳池潜水时，从血红色切换到清凉的蓝色。

src_seg: Blackman's novel is itself a deep dive: this "what would you do?" book for young readers considers ethics, animal rights, othering and empathy. Keeping the pre-social media setting, Winsome Pinnock's new adaptation draws upon the heightened poetic style of Blackman's opening chapter. Pinnock retains the narrator's spirited interest in wordplay, boosts the wisdom of Cameron's Nan and makes water more of a unifying theme throughout the story. Her version also takes a thrilling new turn towards the end.
tgt_seg: 布莱克曼的小说本身就是一次深度探索：这本“你会怎么做？”的青少年读物探讨了伦理、动物权利、异化和同理心等主题。温索姆·平诺克的新改编保留了原著的社会媒体出现前的背景，借鉴了布莱克曼开篇章节中高度诗意的风格。平诺克保留了叙述者对文字游戏的热爱，增强了卡梅伦的奶奶的智慧，并使水成为贯穿整个故事的统一主题。她的版本在结尾处也出现了一个令人激动的新转折。

src_seg: Tristan Fynn-Aiduenu's boisterous production has some vivid performances, too, including by Immanuel Yeboah in the main role. But by overplaying the comedy it drowns out some of the story's more reflective episodes. In the novel, Cameron often cracks jokes, even when face to face with the animal named Trudy whose heart he will receive, yet that encounter is hugely moving as the boy is overwhelmed with relief, fear, guilt and hope. On stage, Trudy is played as a disco-queen pig with pink puffer jacket and oversized glasses; discovering Cameron's plans for her heart, she squeals in jokey horror. Elsewhere, animal rights are thinly discussed.
tgt_seg: 特里斯坦·费恩-艾杜埃努的热闹制作也有一些生动的表演，包括伊曼纽尔·耶博阿饰演的主角。但是，由于过分强调喜剧，故事中一些更具反思性的片段被淹没了。在小说中，卡梅伦经常开玩笑，即使在面对那只名叫特鲁迪的动物（他将接受它的心脏移植）时也是如此，但那次相遇非常感人，因为这个男孩充满了如释重负、恐惧、内疚和希望的情绪。在舞台上，特鲁迪被扮成一个迪斯科女王猪，穿着粉色羽绒服，戴着超大号眼镜；当她发现卡梅伦的计划时，她发出开玩笑似的恐惧尖叫。在其他地方，动物权利的讨论很薄弱。

src_seg: The production is more successful at conveying how Cameron is viewed by his classmates both before the operation (when they see his illness as fragility) and after (when he is still considered different to them). The children are played by an adult cast, most doubling up as the grownup characters. The pioneering Dr Bryce (Tré Medley) is amusingly portrayed as a spy-like smooth operator, all dressed in white both in and out of his laboratory, when that set design again works efficiently. Christina Ngoyi as his best friend Marilyn (Marlon in the book) has the right note of compromised loyalty; Christine During's popular Julie has a buoyant ease but her later fear of Cameron again tips into comedy.
tgt_seg: 该制作更成功地传达了卡梅伦在手术前（当时同学们把他的病看作脆弱）和手术后（当时他仍被认为与他们不同）被同学们的看法。孩子们由成年演员扮演，大多数人兼演成年角色。开创性的布莱斯博士（特雷·梅德利饰）被有趣地刻画成一个间谍般的圆滑操作者，无论是在实验室里还是在外面都穿着白色的衣服，这种舞台设计再次有效地发挥了作用。作为卡梅伦最好的朋友玛丽莲（书中是马龙）的克里斯蒂娜·恩戈伊，有一种妥协的忠诚感；克里斯汀·杜林饰演的受欢迎的朱莉，有一种轻快的自在感，但她后来对卡梅伦的恐惧再次陷入了喜剧。

src_seg: Cameron's asides to the audience include a raucous interrogation about who sold his story to the press that is strained and distracts from his inner tumult. The screens on stage could be used more effectively during Cameron's TV interview and for the camcorder footage he records for his brother.
tgt_seg: 卡梅伦对观众的旁白包括对谁把他的故事卖给媒体的喧闹质问，这有些牵强，并分散了人们对他内心动荡的注意力。舞台上的屏幕本可以在卡梅伦的电视访谈和他为弟弟录制的摄像机画面中更有效地使用。

src_seg: The show is aimed at nine to 13-year-olds (probably geared more towards the younger side of that range) and dynamically captures the turbulent world of school thanks in part to DK Fashola's movement direction, especially appealing in an early slo-mo sequence. This staging has plenty of style and flows swiftly, helped by Xana's sound design and compositions - but it never has quite the same direct appeal to head and heart as Blackman's book.
tgt_seg: 这部剧的目标观众是9到13岁（可能更倾向于这个年龄段的较年轻的一端），由于DK法索拉的动作指导，部分归功于动态地捕捉了学校动荡的世界，尤其是在早期的慢动作序列中很有吸引力。这个舞台剧有大量的风格，流畅迅速，Xana的音效设计和作曲也助了一臂之力——但它从来没有像布莱克曼的书那样直接打动头脑和心灵。
