src_seg: When Remaking a Masterpiece Is Worth the Risk
tgt_seg: 当重拍经典之作值得冒险时

src_seg: I've always thought that one of the most insoluble aesthetic problems going is remaking a movie masterpiece. I certainly understand the impulse to passionately re-engage such a work, but if the definition of a masterwork is something peerless at what it sought to accomplish, how do you remake it without simply reiterating it? There's a reason no one has tried second versions of Fellini's "8½" or Coppola's "The Godfather" or Polanski's "Chinatown." In the case of Fellini's achievement, is someone going to produce a more harrowing portrait of the self-deluding toxicity of male narcissism? In the case of Coppola's, of the corrosive effects of power? Or in the case of Polanski's, of the Hey-nothing-personal malevolence of late-model capitalism? (Water itself in that movie turns out to be the commodity that's manipulated for profit.)
tgt_seg: 我一直认为，重拍一部电影杰作是目前最难以解决的美学问题之一。我当然理解重新演绎这样一部作品的冲动，但如果一部杰作的定义是它在所追求的成就上无与伦比，那么如何重拍而不仅仅是重复它呢？费里尼（Fellini）的《八部半》（"8½"）、科波拉（Coppola）的《教父》（"The Godfather"）或波兰斯基（Polanski）的《唐人街》（"Chinatown"）没有人尝试过第二版，是有原因的。以费里尼的作品为例，有人能描绘出比男性自恋的自我欺骗毒性更令人毛骨悚然的肖像吗？以科波拉的作品为例，有人能展现出权力腐蚀性更深刻的影响吗？或者以波兰斯基的作品为例，有人能揭示出后期资本主义那种“与个人无关”的恶意吗？（在这部电影中，水本身成为被操纵以牟利的商品。）

src_seg: When it comes to those who have waded into that kind of deep water, some have tried the Let's-really-shake-things-up solution. There's the lamentable 1962 remake of "The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari," for instance, which not only eliminated the central figure of Cesare the somnambulist but also featured a Caligari who instead of practicing diabolic hypnotism spent his time showing the heroine offensive pictures. Other filmmakers have chosen the even more baffling route of changing almost nothing, such as Gus Van Sant's nearly shot-for-shot 1998 remake of "Psycho." The number of disappointed moviegoers you risk in remaking a masterpiece from 1922 is smaller, for obvious reasons, but even so, the director Robert Eggers has made clear in any number of interviews his understanding that his new "Nosferatu" is re-engaging one of the greatest of the silent movies. (In 2016, when he was first attempting to remake the film, he told an interviewer that it felt "ugly and blasphemous and egomaniacal and disgusting" to take up that project so early into his career.)
tgt_seg: 对于那些敢于涉足此类深水区的人，有些人尝试了“彻底颠覆”的解决方案。例如，1962年令人遗憾的重拍版《卡里加里博士的小屋》（"The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari"），不仅删除了梦游者切萨雷（Cesare）这一核心人物，还让卡里加里（Caligari）不再练习恶魔催眠术，而是花时间向女主角展示冒犯性的图片。其他电影制作人则选择了几乎不变的更令人费解的路线，如格斯·范·桑特（Gus Van Sant）1998年几乎一模一样的重拍版《惊魂记》（"Psycho"）。重拍1922年的经典之作，失望的观众数量较少，原因显而易见，但即使如此，导演罗伯特·埃格斯（Robert Eggers）在多次采访中明确表示，他明白自己的新作《鼻妖》（"Nosferatu"）是在重新演绎一部最伟大的无声电影之一。（2016年，当他首次尝试重拍这部电影时，他告诉一位采访者，在职业生涯的早期接手这个项目感觉“丑陋、亵渎、自大且令人作呕。”）

src_seg: F. W. Murnau's "Nosferatu: A Symphony of Horror" is itself a remake - an unauthorized adaptation of "Dracula," Bram Stoker's compulsively readable fever dream of a novel - and Murnau and the screenwriter Henrik Galeen retained much of what was arresting about the original while slipping in their own major changes: They're responsible, for example, for the now-set-in-stone tradition that sunlight can destroy the vampire, a notion nowhere in Stoker's book. I likely saw "Nosferatu" at too impressionable an age. I was 6, PBS was showing such things and my babysitter was simply glad I wasn't burning down the house. But I would have been flattened by it whenever I saw it. It was like having felt a draft from a grave. (Its effects were so long-lasting that 30-something years later I published a novel inspired by the film and its production.) The whole thing wasn't so much petrifying as insidiously unsettling, and all of that started with the figure of Nosferatu himself. Max Schreck's performance is, 102 years later, still the benchmark for sinister and dignified repulsiveness. Schreck's vampire has the stillness of a figure in a bad dream or a spider on its web, and the world he inhabits is at times equally disconcerting. After our hero Hutter's first frightening night in Nosferatu's castle, he notices in the mirror that something has bitten his neck, and he smiles.
tgt_seg: F.W. 穆瑙（Murnau）的《鼻妖：恐怖交响曲》（"Nosferatu: A Symphony of Horror"）本身就是一部重拍作品——对布拉姆·斯托克（Bram Stoker）那部令人着迷的小说《德古拉》（"Dracula"）的未经授权改编——穆瑙和编剧亨利克·加伦（Henrik Galeen）保留了原作中令人震撼的元素，同时加入了自己的重大改动：例如，他们确立了如今已成为定论的传统，即阳光可以摧毁吸血鬼，而这个概念在斯托克的书中并不存在。我可能在太容易受影响的年纪看了《鼻妖》。我六岁，PBS正在播放这样的内容，我的保姆只是高兴我没有烧掉房子。但无论我何时看到它，都会被它震撼。它就像感受到从坟墓中吹来的寒风。（它的影响持续了很久，三十多年后，我出版了一部受这部电影及其制作启发的小说。）整个作品并不那么令人毛骨悚然，而是悄然令人不安，而这一切都从鼻妖本人开始。马克斯·施雷克（Max Schreck）的表演，102年后，仍是阴险而高贵的厌恶感的基准。施雷克的吸血鬼有着悪梦中人物或蜘蛛在网上般的静止，而他居住的世界有时同样令人不安。在我们的主人公胡特（Hutter）在鼻妖的城堡度过第一个可怕的夜晚后，他在镜子里注意到自己的脖子被咬了，他笑了。

src_seg: But the most destabilizing figure might well be Hutter's wife, Ellen, our heroine, who's again and again shown to be telepathically on the monster's wavelength, even when he's thousands of miles away, so that polarities like good and evil or desire and repulsion seem to just evaporate while we watch. That last aspect alone would seem to land this story in Robert Eggers's wheelhouse. Part of the subversive energy of movies like "The Witch," "The Lighthouse" and "The Northman" derives from what feels like modern takes on historical characters in thrall to dark passions so that the distantly historical is both granted its strangeness and animated by a scrutinizing modern sensibility. At its best, his version both evokes and reconceives Murnau's most brilliant visual ideas. Murnau's masterful use of the opacities of dark archways from which the vampire can emerge and into which he can dissolve is both echoed and made new. Murnau's famously arresting use of shadows to visualize the vampire's defiling reach is reimagined when those shadows in this new version extend themselves in a 360-degree pan that evokes their vertiginous inescapability. And the shadow of the vampire's hand now extends across the entire city, repurposing the most memorable image from Murnau's "Faust."
tgt_seg: 但最令人不安的人物可能是胡特的妻子艾伦（Ellen），我们的女主角，她一次又一次地被展示出与怪物心灵感应，即使他远在千里之外，以至于善恶或欲望与厌恶等对立面似乎在我们观看时蒸发了。仅仅是最后一点，就似乎让这个故事落入了罗伯特·埃格斯的范畴。像《女巫》（"The Witch"）、《灯塔》（"The Lighthouse"）和《北欧人》（"The Northman"）这样的电影，其颠覆性能量的一部分源于对历史人物的现代诠释，这些人物被黑暗的激情所控制，以至于遥远的历史既被赋予其陌生感，又被现代审视的敏锐性所激活。在最佳状态下，他的版本既唤起了又重新构想了穆瑙最 brillante 的视觉创意。穆瑙对黑暗拱门的不透明性的巧妙运用，吸血鬼可以从中出现并溶解其中，既得到了回响又焕然一新。穆瑙著名地运用阴影来视觉化吸血鬼的玷污范围，在这新版本中，这些阴影在360度全景中延伸，唤起了它们令人眩晕的不可逃脱性。而吸血鬼手掌的阴影现在延伸到整个城市，重新利用了穆瑙《浮士德》（"Faust"）中最难忘的图像。

src_seg: When Remaking a Masterpiece Is Worth the Risk
tgt_seg: 重塑杰作何时值得冒险

src_seg: I've always thought that one of the most insoluble aesthetic problems going is remaking a movie masterpiece. I certainly understand the impulse to passionately re-engage such a work, but if the definition of a masterwork is something peerless at what it sought to accomplish, how do you remake it without simply reiterating it? (Water itself in that movie turns out to be the commodity that's manipulated for profit.)

src_seg: When Remaking a Masterpiece Is Worth the Risk
tgt_seg: 值得冒险重拍的经典之作

src_seg: I've always thought that one of the most insoluble aesthetic problems going is remaking a movie masterpiece. I certainly understand the impulse to passionately re-engage such a work, but if the definition of a masterwork is something peerless at what it sought to accomplish, how do you remake it without simply reiterating it? There's a reason no one has tried second versions of Fellini's "8½" or Coppola's "The Godfather" or Polanski's "Chinatown." In the case of Fellini's achievement, is someone going to produce a more harrowing portrait of the self-deluding toxicity of male narcissism? In the case of Coppola's, of the corrosive effects of power? Or in the case of Polanski's, of the Hey-nothing-personal malevolence of late-model capitalism? (Water itself in that movie turns out to be the commodity that's manipulated for profit.)
tgt_seg: 我一直认为，重拍电影经典是解决不了的审美难题之一。我当然理解人们热衷于重新接触这些作品的情绪，但如果经典之作的定义是它所追求的无与伦比的成就，那么如何在不重复其内容的情况下重拍呢？没有人尝试过费内尔利的《8½》或科波拉的《教父》或波加切利的《 Chinatown》 的第二版本，原因就在于此。就费内尔利的成就而言，有人会制作出更令人震惊的肖像，描绘男性自欺欺人的毒性和自恋？就科波拉的成就而言，有人会制作出权力腐蚀性的肖像？或者就波加切利的成就而言，有人会制作出最新资本主义中男性恶意肖像？（那部电影中的水本身就是为了利润而被操纵的商品。）

src_seg: When it comes to those who have waded into that kind of deep water, some have tried the Let's-really-shake-things-up solution. There's the lamentable 1962 remake of "The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari," for instance, which not only eliminated the central figure of Cesare the somnambulist but also featured a Caligari who instead of practicing diabolic hypnotism spent his time showing the heroine offensive pictures. Other filmmakers have chosen the even more baffling route of changing almost nothing, such as Gus Van Sant's nearly shot-for-shot 1998 remake of "Psycho." The number of disappointed moviegoers you risk in remaking a masterpiece from 1922 is smaller, for obvious reasons, but even so, the director Robert Eggers has made clear in any number of interviews his understanding that his new "Nosferatu" is re-engaging one of the greatest of the silent movies. (In 2016, when he was first attempting to remake the film, he told an interviewer that it felt "ugly and blasphemous and egomaniacal and disgusting" to take up that project so early into his career.)
tgt_seg: 对于那些已经深入研究这一领域的人来说，有些人尝试了“让一切真正动起来”的解决方案。例如，1962年的《卡利加里博士的柜台》重拍版，不仅删除了中央人物——睡眠走路者塞萨尔，还让卡利加里花时间展示给女主人公不雅的图片。其他电影制作人选择了更令人困惑的路线，几乎没有改变什么，例如，范圣1998年几乎一镜一镜地重拍了《惊魂记》。出于显而易见的原因，重拍1922年的经典之作，失望的观众会少一些，但即使如此，导演罗伯特·埃格尔斯在无数次采访中都明确表示，他理解他的新《诺泽拉图》是在重新接触一部无声电影中的经典之作。 （2016年，当他第一次尝试重拍这部电影时，他告诉一位采访者，在职业生涯的初期就这样做感觉“丑陋、亵渎、自恋和令人作呕”。）

src_seg: F. W. Murnau's "Nosferatu: A Symphony of Horror" is itself a remake - an unauthorized adaptation of "Dracula," Bram Stoker's compulsively readable fever dream of a novel - and Murnau and the screenwriter Henrik Galeen retained much of what was arresting about the original while slipping in their own major changes: They're responsible, for example, for the now-set-in-stone tradition that sunlight can destroy the vampire, a notion nowhere in Stoker's book. I likely saw "Nosferatu" at too impressionable an age. I was 6, PBS was showing such things and my babysitter was simply glad I wasn't burning down the house. But I would have been flattened by it whenever I saw it. It was like having felt a draft from a grave. (Its effects were so long-lasting that 30-something years later I published a novel inspired by the film and its production.) The whole thing wasn't so much petrifying as insidiously unsettling, and all of that started with the figure of Nosferatu himself. Max Schreck's performance is, 102 years later, still the benchmark for sinister and dignified repulsiveness. Schreck's vampire has the stillness of a figure in a bad dream or a spider on its web, and the world he inhabits is at times equally disconcerting. After our hero Hutter's first frightening night in Nosferatu's castle, he notices in the mirror that something has bitten his neck, and he smiles.
tgt_seg: 《诺泽拉图：恐怖交响曲》本身就是一个重拍——未经授权改编了《德古拉》，这本小说是斯托克尔的强迫性阅读的梦境。 Murnau和编剧Henrik Galeen保留了原版中令人着迷的部分，同时进行了重大更改：例如，他们负责现在已经成为定论的阳光可以毁灭吸血鬼的观念，这在斯托尔的书中并没有提到。我可能在过于感性的年龄看了《诺泽拉图》。我6岁，PBS正在播放这样的东西，我的保姆只是很高兴我没有把房子烧了。但我每次看到它都会被它击倒。这就像从坟墓中感受到一阵寒风。 （它的影响持续了30多年，我在30多年后出版了一本灵感来自这部电影及其制作的小说。）整个事情不仅令人石化，而且令人不安，这一切都始于诺泽拉图本人。102年后，Max Schreck的表演仍然是邪恶和尊严的排斥基准。 Schreck的吸血鬼拥有一个坏梦或蜘蛛网上的静止的形状，他所居住的世界有时同样令人不安。在我们的英雄胡特第一次在诺泽拉图的城堡中度过可怕的夜晚后，他发现镜子中有人咬了他的脖子，他微笑着。

src_seg: But the most destabilizing figure might well be Hutter's wife, Ellen, our heroine, who's again and again shown to be telepathically on the monster's wavelength, even when he's thousands of miles away, so that polarities like good and evil or desire and repulsion seem to just evaporate while we watch. That last aspect alone would seem to land this story in Robert Eggers's wheelhouse. Part of the subversive energy of movies like "The Witch," "The Lighthouse" and "The Northman" derives from what feels like modern takes on historical characters in thrall to dark passions so that the distantly historical is both granted its strangeness and animated by a scrutinizing modern sensibility. At its best, his version both evokes and reconceives Murnau's most brilliant visual ideas. Murnau's masterful use of the opacities of dark archways from which the vampire can emerge and into which he can dissolve is both echoed and made new. Murnau's famously arresting use of shadows to visualize the vampire's defiling reach is reimagined when those shadows in this new version extend themselves in a 360-degree pan that evokes their vertiginous inescapability. And the shadow of the vampire's hand now extends across the entire city, repurposing the most memorable image from Murnau's "Faust."
tgt_seg: 但最令人不安的角色可能是胡特的妻子埃伦，我们的 heroine，即使当他成千上万英里之外时，她也再次被证明是与怪物同频的，因此，在我们观看时，好与坏、欲望与排斥等对照似乎就消失了。仅这一方面似乎就将这个故事归入罗伯特·埃格尔斯的领域。像《女巫》、《灯塔》和《北人》这样的电影中的反叛能量的一部分来自对历史人物的现代解读，这些人物被黑暗的欲望所控制，因此，历史上的人物被赋予了陌生感，并通过现代审慎感被激活。在最好的时候，他的版本既唤起了Murnau最 brilliant视觉想法，又重新构想了它们。Murnau巧妙地利用了黑暗拱门的透明度，吸血鬼可以从中出现，也可以消失，这既被模仿，又被重新创造。Murnau以令人难忘的方式使用阴影来可视化吸血鬼的污染，当这些阴影在这个新版本中扩展到360度平移时，它唤起了它们令人眩晕的无法逃脱感。现在，吸血鬼的手影现在扩展到整个城市，重新利用了Murnau《浮士德》中最令人难忘的图像。

Schreck's vampire has the stillness of a figure in a bad dream or a spider on its web, and the world he inhabits is at times equally disconcerting. After our hero Hutter's first frightening night in Nosferatu's castle, he notices in the mirror that something has bitten his neck, and he smiles.

W. 默纳乌的《诺斯费拉图：恐怖交响曲》本身就是一个翻拍作品——对布拉姆·斯托克的《德古拉》进行未经授权的改编，斯托克的这部小说是令人强烈共鸣的热门读物。默纳乌和编剧亨里克·加勒恩在保留了原作吸引人的元素的同时，也融入了自己的重大改动：例如，他们负责将阳光可以摧毁吸血鬼的这一观念深深植根于人们的观念中，而这一观念在斯托克的书中根本就没有。我可能在一个非常容易受到影响的年龄看了《诺斯费拉图》，我当时只有6岁，PBS正在播放这样的节目，而我的保姆只是很高兴我没有把房子烧了。但每次我看到它，我都会被它击倒。这就像是从坟墓里感受到一股寒意。（其影响持续了很长时间，30多年后，我出版了一部受这部电影及其制作启发的小说。）事情本身并不那么可怕，而是令人不安，而这一切都始于诺斯费拉图这个角色。102年后，马克斯·施雷克的表演仍然是邪恶和高贵的令人厌恶的标准。施雷克的吸血鬼像一个噩梦中的人物或蜘蛛在网上一样安静，而他所居住的世界有时也同样令人不安。在我们的主角胡特第一次在诺斯费拉图的城堡里度过可怕的一夜后，他在镜子中注意到脖子上被咬了一口，然后他微笑了。

src_seg: But the most destabilizing figure might well be Hutter's wife, Ellen, our heroine, who's again and again shown to be telepathically on the monster's wavelength, even when he's thousands of miles away, so that polarities like good and evil or desire and repulsion seem to just evaporate while we watch. That last aspect alone would seem to land this story in Robert Eggers's wheelhouse. Part of the subversive energy of movies like "The Witch," "The Lighthouse" and "The Northman" derives from what feels like modern takes on historical characters in thrall to dark passions so that the distantly historical is both granted its strangeness and animated by a scrutinizing modern sensibility. At its best, his version both evokes and reconceives Murnau's most brilliant visual ideas. Murnau's masterful use of the opacities of dark archways from which the vampire can emerge and into which he can dissolve is both echoed and made new. Murnau's famously arresting use of shadows to visualize the vampire's defiling reach is reimagined when those shadows in this new version extend themselves in a 360-degree pan that evokes their vertiginous inescapability. And the shadow of the vampire's hand now extends across the entire city, repurposing the most memorable image from Murnau's "Faust."
tgt_seg: 但最具破坏性的角色可能是胡特的妻子艾伦，也就是我们的女主角，她一次又一次地表现出与怪物的思维波长一致，即使怪物距离她数千英里，所以在我们观看时，善与恶或欲望与厌恶等极性似乎都消失了。仅凭这一点，这部电影似乎就能进入罗伯特·艾格的领域。像《女巫》、《灯塔》和《北人》这样的电影之所以具有颠覆性，是因为它们让人感觉像是对历史人物的现代解读，这些人物被黑暗的激情所控制，因此，虽然这些历史事件已经发生很久，但它们既保持了其怪异性，又被现代审视的敏感性赋予了生命。在最好的情况下，他的版本既唤起了又重新构想了穆瑙最精彩的视觉构思。穆瑙在黑暗的通道中使用不透明度，让吸血鬼可以出现和消失，这种手法既得到了回声，也得到了新的诠释。穆瑙以令人难忘的方式使用阴影来可视化吸血鬼的玷污触角，在新版本中，这些阴影在360度全景中延伸，令人感到无法逃脱的恐怖。此外，吸血鬼的阴影现在延伸到了整个城市，重新诠释了穆瑙的《浮士德》中最令人难忘的画面。

src_seg: When Remaking a Masterpiece Is Worth the Risk
tgt_seg: 重拍经典电影：是否值得冒这个险？

src_seg: I've always thought that one of the most insoluble aesthetic problems going is remaking a movie masterpiece. I certainly understand the impulse to passionately re-engage such a work, but if the definition of a masterwork is something peerless at what it sought to accomplish, how do you remake it without simply reiterating it? There's a reason no one has tried second versions of Fellini's "8½" or Coppola's "The Godfather" or Polanski's "Chinatown." In the case of Fellini's achievement, is someone going to produce a more harrowing portrait of the self-deluding toxicity of male narcissism? In the case of Coppola's, of the corrosive effects of power? Or in the case of Polanski's, of the Hey-nothing-personal malevolence of late-model capitalism? (Water itself in that movie turns out to be the commodity that's manipulated for profit.)
tgt_seg: 我一直觉得，改拍电影杰作是最难以解决的美学问题。我当然理解重拍此类作品的冲动，但如果杰作的定义是它的成就在同时代中不可复制，那么你又该如何重拍一部杰作，而不至于简单重复原版？这并非没有道理，就没人尝试过重拍费里尼的《8½》、科波拉的《教父》或波朗基尼的《唐人街》。以费里尼的作品为例，你会重拍一部更深刻地刻画男性自负所导致的自我欺骗的电影吗？以科波拉的作品为例，会重拍一部展现权力的腐蚀性效果的电影吗？以波朗基尼的作品为例，会重拍一部展现后现代资本主义的随意恶毒的电影吗？（电影中的水本身就是一种可以用来谋取利益的商品。）

src_seg: When it comes to those who have waded into that kind of deep water, some have tried the Let's-really-shake-things-up solution. There's the lamentable 1962 remake of "The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari," for instance, which not only eliminated the central figure of Cesare the somnambulist but also featured a Caligari who instead of practicing diabolic hypnotism spent his time showing the heroine offensive pictures. Other filmmakers have chosen the even more baffling route of changing almost nothing, such as Gus Van Sant's nearly shot-for-shot 1998 remake of "Psycho." The number of disappointed moviegoers you risk in remaking a masterpiece from 1922 is smaller, for obvious reasons, but even so, the director Robert Eggers has made clear in any number of interviews his understanding that his new "Nosferatu" is re-engaging one of the greatest of the silent movies. (In 2016, when he was first attempting to remake the film, he told an interviewer that it felt "ugly and blasphemous and egomaniacal and disgusting" to take up that project so early into his career.)
tgt_seg: 对于那些深入这类复杂水域的人来说，有的尝试过“彻底改变一切”的方法。例如，不尽人意的 1962 年电影《卡里加里的地下室》翻拍版，不仅将这个故事中梦游者切萨雷这个核心角色删去，还将卡里加里博士这个角色改成了一个拿着冒犯性照片给女主角看的人。而有的电影制作人则采取了更加让人难以理解的做法，比如古斯·范·桑特（Gus Van Sant）于 1998 年几乎逐格翻拍了《惊魂记》（Psycho）。翻拍一部 1922 年的经典之作所冒的失望观众之险相对更小（很显然如此），尽管如此，导演罗伯特·艾格斯（Robert Eggers）仍然在多次访谈中都表达了他对新版《诺斯费拉图》的意见，并表示新版重新演绎了无声电影时代其中一部最伟大的作品。（2016 年，在尝试翻拍这部电影之初，他曾告诉访谈者，自己觉得在电影生涯如此早的阶段就涉足这样一个项目十分“丑陋、亵渎神灵、自私自利而且令人作呕”。）

src_seg: When it comes to those who have waded into that kind of deep water, some have tried the Let's-really-shake-things-up solution. Other filmmakers have chosen the even more baffling route of changing almost nothing, such as Gus Van Sant's nearly shot-for-shot 1998 remake of "Psycho." The number of disappointed moviegoers you risk in remaking a masterpiece from 1922 is smaller, for obvious reasons, but even so, the director Robert Eggers has made clear in any number of interviews his understanding that his new "Nosferatu" is re-engaging one of the greatest of the silent movies. src_seg: F. W. Murnau's "Nosferatu: A Symphony of Horror" is itself a remake - an unauthorized adaptation of "Dracula," Bram Stoker's compulsively readable fever dream of a novel - and Murnau and the screenwriter Henrik Galeen retained much of what was arresting about the original while slipping in their own major changes: They're responsible, for example, for the now-set-in-stone tradition that sunlight can destroy the vampire, a notion nowhere in Stoker's book. I likely saw "Nosferatu" at too impressionable an age. I was 6, PBS was showing such things and my babysitter was simply glad I wasn't burning down the house. But I would have been flattened by it whenever I saw it. It was like having felt a draft from a grave. (Its effects were so long-lasting that 30-something years later I published a novel inspired by the film and its production.) The whole thing wasn't so much petrifying as insidiously unsettling, and all of that started with the figure of Nosferatu himself. Max Schreck's performance is, 102 years later, still the benchmark for sinister and dignified repulsiveness. Schreck's vampire has the stillness of a figure in a bad dream or a spider on its web, and the world he inhabits is at times equally disconcerting. After our hero Hutter's first frightening night in Nosferatu's castle, he notices in the mirror that something has bitten his neck, and he smiles.
tgt_seg: FW 茂瑙的《诺斯费拉图：恐怖交响曲》本身就是翻拍，是未经授权改编自布拉姆·斯托克的小说《德古拉》，这部小说引人入胜，读起来像一部狂热的梦幻小说。茂瑙和编剧亨里克·加林保留了原著的许多吸引人之处，同时又加入了自己的重大改动：例如，他们创造了如今已成定局的传统，即阳光可以摧毁吸血鬼，而斯托克的书中却没有提到这个概念。我可能在太容易受影响的年龄看了《诺斯费拉图》。我当时 6 岁，PBS 正在播放这样的事情，我的保姆很高兴我没有烧毁房子。但每当我看到它，我就会被它击垮。感觉就像是感受到了来自坟墓的阵阵寒风。（它的影响如此持久，以至于 30 多年后，我出版了一本受这部电影及其制作启发的小说。）整个事情并不那么令人恐惧，而是阴险地令人不安，而所有这一切都始于诺斯费拉图本人的形象。102 年后，马克斯·施莱克的表演仍然是阴险而有尊严的令人厌恶的标杆。施莱克笔下的吸血鬼就像噩梦中的人物或蛛网上的蜘蛛一样静止不动，他所居住的世界有时也同样令人不安。我们的英雄胡特在诺斯费拉图的城堡度过了第一个可怕的夜晚后，他在镜子里发现有东西咬了他的脖子，他笑了。

src_seg: But the most destabilizing figure might well be Hutter's wife, Ellen, our heroine, who's again and again shown to be telepathically on the monster's wavelength, even when he's thousands of miles away, so that polarities like good and evil or desire and repulsion seem to just evaporate while we watch. That last aspect alone would seem to land this story in Robert Eggers's wheelhouse. Part of the subversive energy of movies like "The Witch," "The Lighthouse" and "The Northman" derives from what feels like modern takes on historical characters in thrall to dark passions so that the distantly historical is both granted its strangeness and animated by a scrutinizing modern sensibility. At its best, his version both evokes and reconceives Murnau's most brilliant visual ideas. Murnau's masterful use of the opacities of dark archways from which the vampire can emerge and into which he can dissolve is both echoed and made new. Murnau's famously arresting use of shadows to visualize the vampire's defiling reach is reimagined when those shadows in this new version extend themselves in a 360-degree pan that evokes their vertiginous inescapability. W. 穆瑙的《诺斯费拉图：恐怖交响曲》本身就是一部重拍作品——对布拉姆·斯托克那部令人痴迷的小说《德古拉》的未经授权改编。穆瑙和编剧亨利克·加伦保留了原作中许多引人入胜的元素，同时加入了他们自己的重大改动：例如，他们确立了如今已成定论的传统，即阳光可以摧毁吸血鬼，而这个概念在斯托克的书中并不存在。我可能是在太容易受影响的年纪看了《诺斯费拉图》。我六岁的时候，PBS在播放这样的节目，我的保姆只是很高兴我没有把房子烧掉。但无论何时看到它，我都会被它震撼。这就像感受到从坟墓中吹来的一阵寒风。（它的影响非常持久，以至于三十多年后，我出版了一部受这部电影及其制作启发的小说。）整个故事并不那么可怕，而是悄然令人不安，而这一切都始于诺斯费拉图这个人物本身。马克斯·施雷克的表演，在102年后，仍然是邪恶与高贵的厌恶感的标杆。施雷克的吸血鬼有着像噩梦中的人物或蜘蛛在网上一样的静止，而他居住的世界有时同样令人不安。在我们的英雄胡特在诺斯费拉图的城堡度过第一个可怕的夜晚后，他在镜子里注意到自己的脖子被什么东西咬了，他笑了。

src_seg: But the most destabilizing figure might well be Hutter's wife, Ellen, our heroine, who's again and again shown to be telepathically on the monster's wavelength, even when he's thousands of miles away, so that polarities like good and evil or desire and repulsion seem to just evaporate while we watch. That last aspect alone would seem to land this story in Robert Eggers's wheelhouse. Part of the subversive energy of movies like "The Witch," "The Lighthouse" and "The Northman" derives from what feels like modern takes on historical characters in thrall to dark passions so that the distantly historical is both granted its strangeness and animated by a scrutinizing modern sensibility. At its best, his version both evokes and reconceives Murnau's most brilliant visual ideas. Murnau's masterful use of the opacities of dark archways from which the vampire can emerge and into which he can dissolve is both echoed and made new. Murnau's famously arresting use of shadows to visualize the vampire's defiling reach is reimagined when those shadows in this new version extend themselves in a 360-degree pan that evokes their vertiginous inescapability. And the shadow of the vampire's hand now extends across the entire city, repurposing the most memorable image from Murnau's "Faust."
tgt_seg: 但最令人不安的人物可能是胡特的妻子埃伦，我们的主角，她一次又一次地被证明能心灵感应到怪物的波长，即使他距离数千英里之外，以至于善与恶、欲望与厌恶等对立面在我们观看时似乎都蒸发了。仅凭这一点，这个故事似乎就属于罗伯特·埃格斯的领域。像《女巫》、《灯塔》和《北欧人》这样的电影，其颠覆性能量的一部分源于对历史人物的现代诠释，这些人物被黑暗的激情所束缚，以至于遥远的历史既被赋予了陌生感，又被现代审视的敏锐性所激活。在最佳情况下，他的版本既唤起了又重新构想了穆瑙最杰出的视觉创意。穆瑙巧妙地利用了黑暗拱门的不透明性，让吸血鬼可以从中出现并消失，这种手法在新的版本中得到了回响和创新。穆瑙那著名的、引人入胜的阴影运用，将吸血鬼的玷污范围可视化，在新的版本中被重新构想，阴影在360度全景中延伸，唤起了它们令人眩晕的不可逃脱性。而吸血鬼手影的阴影如今延伸到了整个城市，重新利用了穆瑙《浮士德》中最令人难忘的画面。

src_seg: When Remaking a Masterpiece Is Worth the Risk
tgt_seg: 重拍经典之作是否值得冒险

src_seg: I've always thought that one of the most insoluble aesthetic problems going is remaking a movie masterpiece. I certainly understand the impulse to passionately re-engage such a work, but if the definition of a masterwork is something peerless at what it sought to accomplish, how do you remake it without simply reiterating it? There's a reason no one has tried second versions of Fellini's "8½" or Coppola's "The Godfather" or Polanski's "Chinatown." In the case of Fellini's achievement, is someone going to produce a more harrowing portrait of the self-deluding toxicity of male narcissism? In the case of Coppola's, of the corrosive effects of power? Or in the case of Polanski's, of the Hey-nothing-personal malevolence of late-model capitalism? (Water itself in that movie turns out to be the commodity that's manipulated for profit.)
tgt_seg: 我一直认为，最难解决的美学问题之一就是重拍一部电影经典。我完全理解人们对重新投入这样一部作品的冲动，但如果一部杰作的定义是它在追求的目标上无与伦比，那么如何重拍它而不简单地重复它呢？没有人尝试过重拍费里尼的《甜蜜生活》、柯波拉的《教父》或波兰斯基的《大都会》的原因就在于此。《甜蜜生活》的成就，难道有人会制作出更令人痛苦的自我陶醉的男性自恋毒性肖像吗？在柯波拉的作品中，权力腐蚀的影响如何？或者在波兰斯基的作品中，晚期资本主义的“无个人恶意”又如何？（在电影中，水本身变成了被操纵以牟取利润的商品。）

src_seg: When it comes to those who have waded into that kind of deep water, some have tried the Let's-really-shake-things-up solution. There's the lamentable 1962 remake of "The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari," for instance, which not only eliminated the central figure of Cesare the somnambulist but also featured a Caligari who instead of practicing diabolic hypnotism spent his time showing the heroine offensive pictures. Other filmmakers have chosen the even more baffling route of changing almost nothing, such as Gus Van Sant's nearly shot-for-shot 1998 remake of "Psycho." The number of disappointed moviegoers you risk in remaking a masterpiece from 1922 is smaller, for obvious reasons, but even so, the director Robert Eggers has made clear in any number of interviews his understanding that his new "Nosferatu" is re-engaging one of the greatest of the silent movies. (In 2016, when he was first attempting to remake the film, he told an interviewer that it felt "ugly and blasphemous and egomaniacal and disgusting" to take up that project so early into his career.)
tgt_seg: 对于那些涉足这种深水区的人来说，有些人尝试了彻底改变现状的解决方案。例如，1962年的《卡里加里博士的小屋》重拍版不仅取消了中情局催眠术的中心人物，还改编成卡里加里不再进行魔鬼催眠，而是花时间给女主角展示冒犯性图片。其他电影人选择了更令人困惑的路线，几乎不改变任何东西，例如古斯·范·桑特1998年几乎逐帧重拍的《惊魂记》。重拍1922年的经典之作所冒的风险较小，原因显而易见，但即便如此，导演罗伯特·埃格尔斯在无数次采访中都明确表示，他理解他的新版《诺森弗图》是对一部最伟大的无声电影的重新诠释。（2016年，当他首次尝试重拍这部电影时，他告诉一位采访者，在职业生涯初期接受这个项目让他感觉“丑陋、亵渎、自恋和令人作呕”。）

tgt_seg: 我一直认为，重新制作一部电影杰作是当今最难以解决的审美难题之一。我理解人们热衷于重新演绎这些作品的愿望，但如果一部作品被定义为在它所追求的目标上无可匹敌，那么如何能够不只是简单地重复它呢？ 费里尼的《八部半》、科波拉的《教父》以及波兰斯基的《中国城》之所以没有被尝试过重拍，是有原因的。 费里尼的成就，是否有人能呈现出更令人心碎的男性自恋的虚幻毒性？ 科波拉的，是否有人能展现出权力的腐蚀性影响？ 或者波兰斯基的，是否有人能揭示出冷酷的资本主义？（在那个电影中，水本身最终成为了被操纵以获取利润的商品。）

src_seg: When it comes to those who have waded into that kind of deep water, some have tried the Let's-really-shake-things-up solution. There's the lamentable 1962 remake of "The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari," for instance, which not only eliminated the central figure of Cesare the somnambulist but also featured a Caligari who instead of practicing diabolic hypnotism spent his time showing the heroine offensive pictures. Other filmmakers have chosen the even more baffling route of changing almost nothing, such as Gus Van Sant's nearly shot-for-shot 1998 remake of "Psycho." The number of disappointed moviegoers you risk in remaking a masterpiece from 1922 is smaller, for obvious reasons, but even so, the director Robert Eggers has made clear in any number of interviews his understanding that his new "Nosferatu" is re-engaging one of the greatest of the silent movies. (In 2016, when he was first attempting to remake the film, he told an interviewer that it felt "ugly and blasphemous and egomaniacal and disgusting" to take up that project so early into his career.)
tgt_seg: 对于那些试图重塑经典作品的人来说，有些人尝试过大胆的改造方案。例如，令人遗憾的1962年《卡利加里博士的内阁》翻拍版，不仅删除了核心人物失眠者塞萨尔，还塑造了一个卡利加里博士，他不再施展邪恶的催眠术，而是向女主角展示不雅图片。其他电影人则选择了更加令人费解的路径，几乎照搬原版，比如 Gus Van Sant 1998 年翻拍的《惊魂记》。虽然从1922年翻拍杰作所面临的失望观众数量相对较少，但导演罗伯特·埃格斯在多次采访中明确表示，他深知新版《吸血鬼诺斯费拉图》是对一部伟大的无声电影的改编。（早在2016年他最初尝试翻拍这部电影时，就曾对一位采访者表示，在职业生涯早期承担这个项目让他感到丑陋、亵渎、自负和令人厌恶。）

src_seg: F. W. Murnau's "Nosferatu: A Symphony of Horror" is itself a remake - an unauthorized adaptation of "Dracula," Bram Stoker's compulsively readable fever dream of a novel - and Murnau and the screenwriter Henrik Galeen retained much of what was arresting about the original while slipping in their own major changes: They're responsible, for example, for the now-set-in-stone tradition that sunlight can destroy the vampire, a notion nowhere in Stoker's book. I likely saw "Nosferatu" at too impressionable an age. I was 6, PBS was showing such things and my babysitter was simply glad I wasn't burning down the house. But I would have been flattened by it whenever I saw it. It was like having felt a draft from a grave. (Its effects were so long-lasting that 30-something years later I published a novel inspired by the film and its production.) The whole thing wasn't so much petrifying as insidiously unsettling, and all of that started with the figure of Nosferatu himself. Max Schreck's performance is, 102 years later, still the benchmark for sinister and dignified repulsiveness. Schreck's vampire has the stillness of a figure in a bad dream or a spider on its web, and the world he inhabits is at times equally disconcerting. After our hero Hutter's first frightening night in Nosferatu's castle, he notices in the mirror that something has bitten his neck, and he smiles.
tgt_seg: 弗里茨·朗（F. W. Murnau）的《吸血鬼：恐怖之交响》本身也是一部改编作品——这是一部未经授权的对布莱姆·斯托克（Bram Stoker）引人入胜的小说《德古拉》的改编——朗和编剧亨利克·加林（Henrik Galeen）保留了原作中许多精彩之处，同时又加入了一些重要的改变。例如，他们负责了现在已经成为普遍认知的传统，即阳光可以消灭吸血鬼，而这个概念在斯托克的小说中并未提及。我可能在过于年轻的年龄就看到了《吸血鬼》，当时我只有六岁，美国公共广播公司（PBS，美国公共电视网）正在播放这类影片，我的保姆只是很高兴我没有把房子烧了。但无论我什么时候看到它，都会被它深深震撼。它就像感受到了从坟墓中吹来的寒意。（它的影响如此深远，以至于三十多年后，我出版了一部受到这部电影及其制作启发的长篇小说。）整部影片并非是令人石化的恐惧，而是潜移默化的不安，而这一切都始于吸血鬼诺斯费拉图（Nosferatu）这个形象。102年过去了，马克斯·施瑞克（Max Schreck）的表演仍然是阴险而令人敬畏的恶的标杆。施瑞克的吸血鬼像噩梦中的人物或蛛网上的蜘蛛一样静止不动，而他所处的世界有时也同样令人不安。在我们的英雄胡特（Hutter）第一次在诺斯费拉图的城堡里度过可怕的夜晚后，他注意到脖子上被什么东西咬了一口，然后他露出了笑容。

src_seg: But the most destabilizing figure might well be Hutter's wife, Ellen, our heroine, who's again and again shown to be telepathically on the monster's wavelength, even when he's thousands of miles away, so that polarities like good and evil or desire and repulsion seem to just evaporate while we watch. That last aspect alone would seem to land this story in Robert Eggers's wheelhouse. Part of the subversive energy of movies like "The Witch," "The Lighthouse" and "The Northman" derives from what feels like modern takes on historical characters in thrall to dark passions so that the distantly historical is both granted its strangeness and animated by a scrutinizing modern sensibility. At its best, his version both evokes and reconceives Murnau's most brilliant visual ideas. Murnau's masterful use of the opacities of dark archways from which the vampire can emerge and into which he can dissolve is both echoed and made new. Murnau's famously arresting use of shadows to visualize the vampire's defiling reach is reimagined when those shadows in this new version extend themselves in a 360-degree pan that evokes their vertiginous inescapability. And the shadow of the vampire's hand now extends across the entire city, repurposing the most memorable image from Murnau's "Faust."
tgt_seg: 但或许最具破坏性的人物是胡特的妻子艾伦，我们的女主角，她一次又一次地展现出与怪物心灵感应的能力，即使相隔数千英里，也能够感知到它的存在，以至于善恶、渴望与厌恶等对立的概念在我们观看时似乎都烟消云散。仅就这一点而言，这个故事似乎非常适合罗伯特·艾格斯导演的风格。像《女巫》、《灯塔》和《北方人》等电影的反叛能量，部分源于对历史人物及其黑暗欲望的现代视角，使得遥远的历史既保留了其奇异之处，又被一种审视的现代视角所赋予活力。在最佳状态下，他的作品既唤起了又重新构想了谋瑙最杰出的视觉创意。谋瑙对黑暗拱门，即吸血鬼可以从中出现和消失的遮蔽空间，运用高超的技巧，在这部新作品中得到了回响和创新。谋瑙以其标志性的手法，利用阴影来可视化吸血鬼的侵蚀力量，在这一新版本中被重新想象，那些阴影以360度全景旋转的方式延伸，营造出一种令人不安的压迫感。而吸血鬼之手的阴影如今已笼罩整个城市，借鉴了谋瑙的《浮士德》中最具代表性的画面。

tgt_seg: F·W·茂瑙的《诺斯费拉图：恐怖交响曲》本身就是一部未经授权的改编作品，改编自布拉姆·斯托克那部引人入胜的小说《德古拉》。茂瑙与编剧亨里克·加伦既保留了原著中的许多引人注目的元素，又巧妙地加入了他们自己的重大改动：例如，如今已成为定论的“阳光可以摧毁吸血鬼”的设定，其实并不出现在斯托克的原著中。我当时可能年纪太小，还不具备抵抗这种强烈视觉冲击的能力。那时我只有6岁，公共广播公司（PBS）正在播放这类影片，而我的保姆则只关心我是否会在家里惹事。但无论何时观看这部电影，都会被它深深震撼。那种感觉就像从坟墓中吹来的冷风一样。（这种影响如此深远，以至于三十多年后，我还出版了一部受该片及其制作过程启发的小说。）整部影片与其说是令人恐惧，不如说是让人感到隐隐不安，而这一切都始于诺斯费拉图这个角色本身。即使在102年后的今天，马克斯·施雷克的表演依然堪称经典：他饰演的吸血鬼就像噩梦中的怪兽或像蛛网上的蜘蛛般静止不动，而他所生活的世界则同样令人不安。在主人公胡特在诺斯费拉图的城堡度过了那个恐怖的夜晚后，他竟然在镜子中发现了自己脖子上的咬痕，随后竟露出了笑容。

src_seg: But the most destabilizing figure might well be Hutter's wife, Ellen, our heroine, who's again and again shown to be telepathically on the monster's wavelength, even when he's thousands of miles away, so that polarities like good and evil or desire and repulsion seem to just evaporate while we watch. That last aspect alone would seem to land this story in Robert Eggers's wheelhouse. Part of the subversive energy of movies like "The Witch," "The Lighthouse" and "The Northman" derives from what feels like modern takes on historical characters in thrall to dark passions so that the distantly historical is both granted its strangeness and animated by a scrutinizing modern sensibility. At its best, his version both evokes and reconceives Murnau's most brilliant visual ideas. Murnau's masterful use of the opacities of dark archways from which the vampire can emerge and into which he can dissolve is both echoed and made new. Murnau's famously arresting use of shadows to visualize the vampire's defiling reach is reimagined when those shadows in this new version extend themselves in a 360-degree pan that evokes their vertiginous inescapability. And the shadow of the vampire's hand now extends across the entire city, repurposing the most memorable image from Murnau's "Faust."
tgt_seg: 但最令人不安的角色，或许正是胡特的妻子艾伦——我们的女主角。她一次又一次展现出与那个怪物之间的心灵感应，即便他们相隔千里；在观影过程中，善与恶、欲望与厌恶等对立概念似乎都逐渐消融。仅凭这一点，这个故事就显然属于罗伯特·艾格斯的擅长领域。从《女巫》《灯塔》到《北欧人》，艾格斯作品的颠覆性力量部分源于其对那些被黑暗激情所支配的历史人物的现代诠释：这些遥远历史中的角色既保留了其固有的怪异感，又被现代视角重新审视。在艾格斯的版本中，他既继承了穆尔瑙最具创意的视觉手法，又对其进行了重新诠释。穆尔瑙巧妙地运用那些幽暗、不透明的拱门，让吸血鬼得以从中现身或消失；这一手法在艾格斯的电影中得到了呼应并被赋予了新意。穆尔瑙以阴影来象征吸血鬼的邪恶力量，这一经典视觉手法在艾格斯的版本中被重新演绎：那些阴影在360度全景镜头中蔓延开来，营造出一种令人眩晕、无处可逃的压迫感。而吸血鬼手掌的阴影如今笼罩着整座城市，这一画面实则是对穆尔瑙《浮士德》中最令人难忘的影像的再利用。

src_seg: When Remaking a Masterpiece Is Worth the Risk
tgt_seg: 重制经典，何时才值得冒险

src_seg: I've always thought that one of the most insoluble aesthetic problems going is remaking a movie masterpiece. I certainly understand the impulse to passionately re-engage such a work, but if the definition of a masterwork is something peerless at what it sought to accomplish, how do you remake it without simply reiterating it? There's a reason no one has tried second versions of Fellini's "8½" or Coppola's "The Godfather" or Polanski's "Chinatown." In the case of Fellini's achievement, is someone going to produce a more harrowing portrait of the self-deluding toxicity of male narcissism? In the case of Coppola's, of the corrosive effects of power? Or in the case of Polanski's, of the Hey-nothing-personal malevolence of late-model capitalism? (Water itself in that movie turns out to be the commodity that's manipulated for profit.)
tgt_seg: 我一直认为，当今最难解的审美难题之一便是翻拍电影杰作。我当然理解那种想要热情地重新诠释这类作品的冲动，但如果杰作的定义是在其追求的目标上无与伦比，你又该如何在不简单复述它的前提下进行翻拍呢？没人尝试过费里尼的《八部半》、科波拉的《教父》或波兰斯基的《唐人街》的第二版，这是有原因的。就费里尼的成就而言，难道会有人能对男性自恋中自欺欺人的毒性，进行更令人痛彻心扉的刻画吗？就科波拉的成就而言，有人能更好地描绘权力的腐蚀性影响吗？或者就波兰斯基的成就而言，有人能更好地展现晚期资本主义那种“嘿，无涉个人恩怨”式的恶意吗？（在那部电影里，水本身就是被操纵以牟利的商品。）

src_seg: When it comes to those who have waded into that kind of deep water, some have tried the Let's-really-shake-things-up solution. There's the lamentable 1962 remake of "The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari," for instance, which not only eliminated the central figure of Cesare the somnambulist but also featured a Caligari who instead of practicing diabolic hypnotism spent his time showing the heroine offensive pictures. Other filmmakers have chosen the even more baffling route of changing almost nothing, such as Gus Van Sant's nearly shot-for-shot 1998 remake of "Psycho." The number of disappointed moviegoers you risk in remaking a masterpiece from 1922 is smaller, for obvious reasons, but even so, the director Robert Eggers has made clear in any number of interviews his understanding that his new "Nosferatu" is re-engaging one of the greatest of the silent movies. (In 2016, when he was first attempting to remake the film, he told an interviewer that it felt "ugly and blasphemous and egomaniacal and disgusting" to take up that project so early into his career.)
tgt_seg: 在那些涉足此等深水区的人中，一些人尝试了“让我们彻底颠覆一番”的解决方案。例如，1962年对《卡里加里博士的小屋》那部可悲的翻拍版，不仅删除了核心人物——梦游者凯撒，而且片中的卡里加里也不再施行恶魔般的催眠术，而是把时间花在给女主角看不雅的照片上。其他电影制作人则选择了更令人费解的路线——几乎未作任何改动，例如格斯·范·桑特1998年几乎逐镜头翻拍的《惊魂记》。翻拍一部1922年的杰作，所冒的令影迷失望的风险，出于显而易见的原因会更小，但即便如此，导演罗伯特·艾格斯已在多次采访中明确表示，他清楚自己的新版《诺斯费拉图》是在重新诠释一部最伟大的默片。（2016年，当他首次尝试翻拍该片时，他告诉一位采访者，在自己职业生涯如此早期就接手这个项目，感觉“丑陋、亵渎、自大和恶心”。）

src_seg: F. W. Murnau's "Nosferatu: A Symphony of Horror" is itself a remake - an unauthorized adaptation of "Dracula," Bram Stoker's compulsively readable fever dream of a novel - and Murnau and the screenwriter Henrik Galeen retained much of what was arresting about the original while slipping in their own major changes: They're responsible, for example, for the now-set-in-stone tradition that sunlight can destroy the vampire, a notion nowhere in Stoker's book. I likely saw "Nosferatu" at too impressionable an age. I was 6, PBS was showing such things and my babysitter was simply glad I wasn't burning down the house. But I would have been flattened by it whenever I saw it. It was like having felt a draft from a grave. (Its effects were so long-lasting that 30-something years later I published a novel inspired by the film and its production.) The whole thing wasn't so much petrifying as insidiously unsettling, and all of that started with the figure of Nosferatu himself. Max Schreck's performance is, 102 years later, still the benchmark for sinister and dignified repulsiveness. Schreck's vampire has the stillness of a figure in a bad dream or a spider on its web, and the world he inhabits is at times equally disconcerting. After our hero Hutter's first frightening night in Nosferatu's castle, he notices in the mirror that something has bitten his neck, and he smiles.

That last aspect alone would seem to land this story in Robert Eggers's wheelhouse. Part of the subversive energy of movies like "The Witch," "The Lighthouse" and "The Northman" derives from what feels like modern takes on historical characters in thrall to dark passions so that the distantly historical is both granted its strangeness and animated by a scrutinizing modern sensibility. tgt_seg: 但最具颠覆性的角色很可能是胡特的妻子、我们的女主角艾伦，她被一再展现出在心灵感应上与怪物同频，即便他远在千里之外。于是，善与恶、欲望与排斥这样的两极对立似乎就在我们眼前消散了。仅这最后一点，似乎就让这个故事正中罗伯特·艾格斯的下怀。像《女巫》、《灯塔》和《北方人》这类电影的部分颠覆性能量，正源于其对受黑暗激情支配的历史人物的现代诠释，从而使遥远的历史既被赋予了其应有的陌生感，又被一种审视性的现代感性所激活。在他的版本中，最好的部分既唤起了茂瑙最卓越的视觉创意，又对其进行了重新构思。茂瑙对黑暗拱门的晦暗不明之处（吸血鬼可从中出现或隐没）的精湛运用，既得到了呼应，又被赋予了新意。茂瑙利用影子来将吸血鬼的玷污之手视觉化的震撼手法，在新版中被重新想象——那些影子通过一个360度的摇镜扩展开来，唤起了它们令人眩晕的无处可逃之感。并且，吸血鬼手的影子如今延伸至整座城市，这是对茂瑙《浮士德》中最令人难忘的影像的再利用。

tgt_seg:
重制经典：风险与回报
在电影史上，有许多经典影片被重制过，但并非所有重制都能成功。重制经典的风险在于，观众可能会对原版有着深深的感情，难以接受新的解读。然而，成功的重制也可能带来新的视角和更广泛的受众。
重制经典的动机有很多。有些导演可能希望将自己的视角和创意融入经典作品中，给观众带来新的体验。有些制片人可能希望通过重制来吸引新的观众群，增加票房收入。有些演员可能希望通过重制来展示自己的演技和才华。
然而，重制经典也存在着挑战。首先，观众可能会对原版有着强烈的忠诚感，难以接受新的解读。其次，重制经典的成本可能会很高，尤其是当涉及到大-budget电影时。最后，重制经典的成功也取决于导演和演员的表现。
那么，重制经典是否值得冒险呢？答案取决于具体情况。有些重制可能会带来新的视角和更广泛的受众，值得冒险。然而，其他重制可能会失去原版的魅力，甚至会被观众所唾弃。
在电影史上，有许多经典影片被重制过，但并非所有重制都能成功。例如，2019年的《猫王》重制版虽然获得了好评，但票房收入却不如预期。相反，2013年的《美女与野兽》重制版却获得了巨大的成功，票房收入超过了1亿美元。
因此，重制经典是否值得冒险，取决于具体情况。有些重制可能会带来新的视角和更广泛的受众，值得冒险。然而，其他重制可能会失去原版的魅力，甚至会被观众所唾弃。

That last aspect alone would seem to land this story in Robert Eggers's wheelhouse. Part of the subversive energy of movies like "The Witch," "The Lighthouse" and "The Northman" derives from what feels like modern takes on historical characters in thrall to dark passions so that the distantly historical is both granted its strangeness and animated by a scrutinizing modern sensibility. At its best, his version both evokes and reconceives Murnau's most brilliant visual ideas. Murnau's masterful use of the opacities of dark archways from which the vampire can emerge and into which he can dissolve is both echoed and made new. Murnau's famously arresting use of shadows to visualize the vampire's defiling reach is reimagined when those shadows in this new version extend themselves in a 360-degree pan that evokes their vertiginous inescapability. And the shadow of the vampire's hand now extends across the entire city, repurposing the most memorable image from Murnau's "Faust."
tgt_seg: 但最具破坏性的人物可能是胡特尔的妻子艾伦，她又一次又一次地表现出与怪物共振，甚至当他身处数千英里之外时，她也能感受到。因此，像善恶或欲望和排斥这样的极性似乎在我们眼前就消失了。仅凭这一点，这个故事似乎就适合罗伯特·埃格斯的风格。像《女巫》、《灯塔》和《北方人》这样的电影的颠覆性力量部分来自对历史人物的现代解读，他们被黑暗情绪所控制。这样一来，历史的陌生感就被赋予了现代的审视力。他的最佳版本既能唤起又能重新诠释穆纳乌的最出色的视觉想法。穆纳乌对黑暗拱门的不透明性使用得炉火纯青，从而使吸血鬼可以出现和消失。这个想法在新版本中被重复和重新创造。穆纳乌对阴影的著名使用使吸血鬼的玷污范围变得清晰可见。在这个新版本中，阴影在360度的全景中延伸，表现出他们的深渊般的不可避免性。吸血鬼的手影现在延伸到整个城市，重新利用了穆纳乌《法斯特》的最令人难忘的镜头。

src_seg: When Remaking a Masterpiece Is Worth the Risk
tgt_seg: 重拍经典之作何时值得冒险

src_seg: I've always thought that one of the most insoluble aesthetic problems going is remaking a movie masterpiece. I certainly understand the impulse to passionately re-engage such a work, but if the definition of a masterwork is something peerless at what it sought to accomplish, how do you remake it without simply reiterating it? There's a reason no one has tried second versions of Fellini's "8½" or Coppola's "The Godfather" or Polanski's "Chinatown." In the case of Fellini's achievement, is someone going to produce a more harrowing portrait of the self-deluding toxicity of male narcissism? In the case of Coppola's, of the corrosive effects of power? Or in the case of Polanski's, of the Hey-nothing-personal malevolence of late-model capitalism? (Water itself in that movie turns out to be the commodity that's manipulated for profit.)
tgt_seg: 我一直认为，最难解决的美学问题之一就是重拍一部电影杰作。我当然理解人们对重新投入这样一部作品的冲动，但如果杰作的定义是指在所追求的目标上无与伦比的作品，那么如何重拍它而不简单地重复它呢？没有人尝试过重拍费里尼的《甜蜜生活》、科波拉的《教父》或波兰斯基的《唐人街》是有原因的。就费里尼的成就而言，有人会制作一部更令人心碎的关于男性自恋的自我欺骗毒性的肖像吗？就科波拉而言，关于权力的腐蚀性？或者就波兰斯基而言，关于晚期资本主义的无个人恶意？（在电影中，水本身被证明是为利润而操纵的商品。）

src_seg: When it comes to those who have waded into that kind of deep water, some have tried the Let's-really-shake-things-up solution. There's the lamentable 1962 remake of "The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari," for instance, which not only eliminated the central figure of Cesare the somnambulist but also featured a Caligari who instead of practicing diabolic hypnotism spent his time showing the heroine offensive pictures. Other filmmakers have chosen the even more baffling route of changing almost nothing, such as Gus Van Sant's nearly shot-for-shot 1998 remake of "Psycho." The number of disappointed moviegoers you risk in remaking a masterpiece from 1922 is smaller, for obvious reasons, but even so, the director Robert Eggers has made clear in any number of interviews his understanding that his new "Nosferatu" is re-engaging one of the greatest of the silent movies. (In 2016, when he was first attempting to remake the film, he told an interviewer that it felt "ugly and blasphemous and egomaniacal and disgusting" to take up that project so early into his career.)
tgt_seg: 对于那些涉足这种深水区的人来说，有些人尝试了彻底改变现状的解决方案。例如，令人遗憾的是，1962 年的《卡利加里博士的小屋》重拍版不仅取消了卡里加里博士的中心人物塞萨雷，还改编成卡里加里博士不再进行魔鬼般的催眠，而是花时间给女主角展示令人反感的图片。其他电影制片人则选择了几乎不改变任何东西的更令人困惑的路线，例如古斯·范·桑特的 1998 年《惊魂记》几乎逐镜头重拍版。出于显而易见的原因，重拍 1922 年的杰作所冒的让观众失望的风险较小，但即便如此，导演罗伯特·埃格尔斯在无数次采访中都明确表示，他明白他的新《诺森弗图》正在重新演绎一部最伟大的无声电影。 (2016 年，当他首次尝试重拍这部电影时，他告诉一位采访者，在他职业生涯的早期接受这个项目感觉“丑陋、亵渎、自恋和令人作呕”。)

src_seg: F. W. Murnau's "Nosferatu: A Symphony of Horror" is itself a remake - an unauthorized adaptation of "Dracula," Bram Stoker's compulsively readable fever dream of a novel - and Murnau and the screenwriter Henrik Galeen retained much of what was arresting about the original while slipping in their own major changes: They're responsible, for example, for the now-set-in-stone tradition that sunlight can destroy the vampire, a notion nowhere in Stoker's book. I likely saw "Nosferatu" at too impressionable an age. I was 6, PBS was showing such things and my babysitter was simply glad I wasn't burning down the house. But I would have been flattened by it whenever I saw it. It was like having felt a draft from a grave. (Its effects were so long-lasting that 30-something years later I published a novel inspired by the film and its production.) The whole thing wasn't so much petrifying as insidiously unsettling, and all of that started with the figure of Nosferatu himself. Max Schreck's performance is, 102 years later, still the benchmark for sinister and dignified repulsiveness. Schreck's vampire has the stillness of a figure in a bad dream or a spider on its web, and the world he inhabits is at times equally disconcerting. After our hero Hutter's first frightening night in Nosferatu's castle, he notices in the mirror that something has bitten his neck, and he smiles.

At its best, his version both evokes and reconceives Murnau's most brilliant visual ideas. tgt_seg: 我一直认为，重拍电影杰作是最难以解决的美学难题之一。我当然能理解人们想要激情重温这样一部作品的冲动，但如果说杰作的定义在于其在所追求目标上的无与伦比，那么你如何在重拍时不只是简单重复？这也是为什么没有人尝试过重拍费里尼的《八部半》、科波拉的《教父》或波兰斯基的《唐人街》。以费里尼的成就为例，谁能创作出比原作更令人不安的男性自恋毒性自我欺骗画像？以科波拉为例，谁能更深刻地展现权力的腐蚀性影响？又或者以波兰斯基为例，谁能更犀利地揭示晚期资本主义那种“别往心里去”的恶意？（在那部电影中，水本身最终成为被操纵以牟利的商品。）

src_seg: When it comes to those who have waded into that kind of deep water, some have tried the Let's-really-shake-things-up solution. There's the lamentable 1962 remake of "The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari," for instance, which not only eliminated the central figure of Cesare the somnambulist but also featured a Caligari who instead of practicing diabolic hypnotism spent his time showing the heroine offensive pictures. Other filmmakers have chosen the even more baffling route of changing almost nothing, such as Gus Van Sant's nearly shot-for-shot 1998 remake of "Psycho." The number of disappointed moviegoers you risk in remaking a masterpiece from 1922 is smaller, for obvious reasons, but even so, the director Robert Eggers has made clear in any number of interviews his understanding that his new "Nosferatu" is re-engaging one of the greatest of the silent movies. (In 2016, when he was first attempting to remake the film, he told an interviewer that it felt "ugly and blasphemous and egomaniacal and disgusting" to take up that project so early into his career.)
tgt_seg: 对于那些涉足这类深水区的人来说，有些人尝试了“让我们彻底颠覆一切”的方案。例如，1962年令人遗憾的《卡里加里博士的小屋》重拍版，不仅删去了核心人物恍惚者凯撒，还让卡里加里博士不再施展恶魔般的催眠术，而是花时间给女主角看令人反感的图片。还有一些电影人选择了更令人费解的方式——几乎不做任何改变，比如格斯·范·桑特1998年几乎一镜不差的《惊魂记》重拍。重拍1922年杰作所面临的失望观众数量较少，原因显而易见，但即便如此，导演罗伯特·艾格斯在多次采访中都明确表示，他深知自己的新作《诺斯费拉图》是在重新诠释无声电影史上最伟大的作品之一。（2016年，当他首次尝试重拍该片时，他曾对一位采访者表示，自己在职业生涯如此早期就接手这个项目，感觉“丑陋、亵渎、自大且令人作呕”。）

src_seg: F. W. Murnau's "Nosferatu: A Symphony of Horror" is itself a remake - an unauthorized adaptation of "Dracula," Bram Stoker's compulsively readable fever dream of a novel - and Murnau and the screenwriter Henrik Galeen retained much of what was arresting about the original while slipping in their own major changes: They're responsible, for example, for the now-set-in-stone tradition that sunlight can destroy the vampire, a notion nowhere in Stoker's book. I likely saw "Nosferatu" at too impressionable an age. I was 6, PBS was showing such things and my babysitter was simply glad I wasn't burning down the house. But I would have been flattened by it whenever I saw it. It was like having felt a draft from a grave. (Its effects were so long-lasting that 30-something years later I published a novel inspired by the film and its production.) The whole thing wasn't so much petrifying as insidiously unsettling, and all of that started with the figure of Nosferatu himself. Max Schreck's performance is, 102 years later, still the benchmark for sinister and dignified repulsiveness. Schreck's vampire has the stillness of a figure in a bad dream or a spider on its web, and the world he inhabits is at times equally disconcerting. After our hero Hutter's first frightening night in Nosferatu's castle, he notices in the mirror that something has bitten his neck, and he smiles.
tgt_seg: F·W·茂瑙的《诺斯费拉图：恐怖交响曲》本身就是一部重拍——它是对布拉姆·斯托克那部令人欲罢不能、如同热病般的小说《德古拉》的未经授权改编——茂瑙和编剧亨里克·加林在保留原作诸多引人入胜之处的同时，也加入了自己的重大改动：例如，正是他们确立了如今已成定律的传统——阳光可以毁灭吸血鬼，这一设定在斯托克的原著中并不存在。我大概是在过于年幼的年纪看到了《诺斯费拉图》。那时我6岁，PBS正在播放这类影片，而我的保姆只要我不把房子点着就很高兴。但无论我何时看到它，都会被它震撼。那种感觉就像是从坟墓里吹来的一阵冷风。（它的影响如此持久，以至于三十多年后我出版了一部受该片及其制作过程启发的小说。）整部影片与其说是令人惊恐，不如说是阴险地令人不安，而这一切都始于诺斯费拉图本人的形象。马克斯·施雷克的表演，时隔102年，依然是阴森与庄严令人厌恶的标杆。施雷克饰演的吸血鬼如同噩梦中的人物或蛛网上的蜘蛛般静止，而他所处的世界有时同样令人不安。在我们的主人公胡特在诺斯费拉图城堡度过第一个恐怖之夜后，他在镜中发现脖子上被咬了，却露出了微笑。

src_seg: But the most destabilizing figure might well be Hutter's wife, Ellen, our heroine, who's again and again shown to be telepathically on the monster's wavelength, even when he's thousands of miles away, so that polarities like good and evil or desire and repulsion seem to just evaporate while we watch. That last aspect alone would seem to land this story in Robert Eggers's wheelhouse. Part of the subversive energy of movies like "The Witch," "The Lighthouse" and "The Northman" derives from what feels like modern takes on historical characters in thrall to dark passions so that the distantly historical is both granted its strangeness and animated by a scrutinizing modern sensibility. At its best, his version both evokes and reconceives Murnau's most brilliant visual ideas. Murnau's masterful use of the opacities of dark archways from which the vampire can emerge and into which he can dissolve is both echoed and made new. Murnau's famously arresting use of shadows to visualize the vampire's defiling reach is reimagined when those shadows in this new version extend themselves in a 360-degree pan that evokes their vertiginous inescapability. And the shadow of the vampire's hand now extends across the entire city, repurposing the most memorable image from Murnau's "Faust."
tgt_seg: 但最具颠覆性的角色或许是胡特的妻子艾伦，我们的女主角。她一次次被展现为与怪物心灵感应，即使他远在千里之外，善恶、欲望与厌恶等对立面在观众眼前似乎都消解了。仅这一点就足以让这个故事落入罗伯特·艾格斯的擅长领域。他的《女巫》《灯塔》和《北方人》等影片的颠覆性力量部分源于对历史人物被黑暗激情支配的现代解读，使遥远的历史既保留了其陌生感，又被现代审视的敏锐目光所激活。在最佳状态下，他的版本既唤起又重构了茂瑙最精彩的视觉创意。茂瑙对黑暗拱门不透明感的巧妙运用，使吸血鬼可以从中现身或消失，这一手法在新作中既被呼应又焕然一新。茂瑙著名的用影子表现吸血鬼玷污之手的视觉冲击，在新版本中被重新想象——那些影子在360度的全景镜头中延展，令人眩晕地无法逃脱。而吸血鬼手的影子如今横跨整座城市，重新诠释了茂瑙《浮士德》中最令人难忘的画面。

tgt_seg: 弗·W·茂瑙的《诺斯费拉图：恐怖交响曲》本身就是一部翻拍片——它未经授权改编自布莱姆·斯托克的《德古拉》，那是一本令人欲罢不能的噩梦小说——茂瑙和编剧亨里克·加林保留了许多原作的惊人之处，同时又加入了他们自己的重大改动：例如，阳光可以消灭吸血鬼的这个如今已成定论的传统便是他们确立的，这一概念在斯托克的书中根本没有。我可能是在一个过于易受影响的年龄看到了《诺斯费拉图》。我那时才6岁，公共广播公司（PBS）正在播放这类东西，而我的保姆只求我别把房子烧了就算不错了。但无论我何时看到它，它都会让我彻底折服。那就像感受到了来自坟墓的阴风。（其影响如此深远，以至于三十多年后，我发表了一本受这部电影及其制作过程启发的小说。）整部电影与其说是恐怖，不如说是阴险地令人不安，而这一切都始于诺斯费拉图这个角色本身。102年后，马克斯·史瑞克的表演仍然是那种既阴险又不失尊严的骇人形象的标杆。史瑞克的吸血鬼就像噩梦中的人物或网上的一只蜘蛛般静止不动，而他所处的世界有时同样令人不安。在我们的英雄胡特在诺斯费拉图的城堡里度过了第一个恐怖之夜后，他在镜子里注意到自己的脖子上有东西咬了下去，然后他笑了。

src_seg: But the most destabilizing figure might well be Hutter's wife, Ellen, our heroine, who's again and again shown to be telepathically on the monster's wavelength, even when he's thousands of miles away, so that polarities like good and evil or desire and repulsion seem to just evaporate while we watch. That last aspect alone would seem to land this story in Robert Eggers's wheelhouse. Part of the subversive energy of movies like "The Witch," "The Lighthouse" and "The Northman" derives from what feels like modern takes on historical characters in thrall to dark passions so that the distantly historical is both granted its strangeness and animated by a scrutinizing modern sensibility. At its best, his version both evokes and reconceives Murnau's most brilliant visual ideas. Murnau's masterful use of the opacities of dark archways from which the vampire can emerge and into which he can dissolve is both echoed and made new. Murnau's famously arresting use of shadows to visualize the vampire's defiling reach is reimagined when those shadows in this new version extend themselves in a 360-degree pan that evokes their vertiginous inescapability. And the shadow of the vampire's hand now extends across the entire city, repurposing the most memorable image from Murnau's "Faust."
tgt_seg: 但最具颠覆性的角色很可能是哈特的妻子艾伦，我们的女主角，她一次又一次地被表现得能与怪物心灵感应，即便他远在千里之外，以至于当我们看着时，善与恶或欲望与排斥之类的两极对立似乎都消失了。仅这最后一点，似乎就让这个故事成了罗伯特·艾格斯的拿手好菜。像《女巫》、《灯塔》和《北方人》这类电影的部分颠覆性能量，正是源于其对受黑暗激情支配的历史人物的现代诠释，从而使遥远的历史既被赋予了其应有的陌生感，又被一种审视的现代感性所激活。在他的版本中，最出色之处既唤起了茂瑙最卓越的视觉创意，又对其进行了重新构思。茂瑙对黑暗拱门的晦暗不明之处（吸血鬼可从中出现或隐没）的精湛运用，既得到了呼应，又被赋予了新意。茂瑙利用影子来将吸血鬼的玷污之手可视化的震撼手法，在新版中被重新想象——那些影子通过360度的摇镜扩展开来，唤起了它们令人眩晕的无所逃遁之感。而且吸血鬼的手影现在延伸横跨整个城市，重新利用了茂瑙在《浮士德》中最令人难忘的影像。

src_seg: When Remaking a Masterpiece Is Worth the Risk
tgt_seg: 当重拍电影杰作值得冒险时

src_seg: I've always thought that one of the most insoluble aesthetic problems going is remaking a movie masterpiece. I certainly understand the impulse to passionately re-engage such a work, but if the definition of a masterwork is something peerless at what it sought to accomplish, how do you remake it without simply reiterating it? There's a reason no one has tried second versions of Fellini's "8½" or Coppola's "The Godfather" or Polanski's "Chinatown." In the case of Fellini's achievement, is someone going to produce a more harrowing portrait of the self-deluding toxicity of male narcissism? In the case of Coppola's, of the corrosive effects of power? Or in the case of Polanski's, of the Hey-nothing-personal malevolence of late-model capitalism? (Water itself in that movie turns out to be the commodity that's manipulated for profit.)
tgt_seg: 我一直认为重拍电影杰作是其中一个最难以解决的美学问题。我当然理解重拍作品的冲动，但如果杰作的定义是它追求的成就中无与伦比的，那么你如何重拍它而不只是重复它？没有人尝试过“Fellini的《8½》”或“Coppola的《教父》”或“Polanski的《唐人街》》的第二版。在Fellini的成就中，有人会制作一个对男性自欺欺人的毒性更令人痛心的自欺欺人的形象吗？在Coppola的成就中，腐蚀性权力效应是什么？或者在Polanski的成就中，晚期资本主义的无个人恶意是什么？（在那部电影中，水本身就是被操纵以获取利润的商品。）

src_seg: When it comes to those who have waded into that kind of deep water, some have tried the Let's-really-shake-things-up solution. There's the lamentable 1962 remake of "The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari," for instance, which not only eliminated the central figure of Cesare the somnambulist but also featured a Caligari who instead of practicing diabolic hypnotism spent his time showing the heroine offensive pictures. Other filmmakers have chosen the even more baffling route of changing almost nothing, such as Gus Van Sant's nearly shot-for-shot 1998 remake of "Psycho." The number of disappointed moviegoers you risk in remaking a masterpiece from 1922 is smaller, for obvious reasons, but even so, the director Robert Eggers has made clear in any number of interviews his understanding that his new "Nosferatu" is re-engaging one of the greatest of the silent movies. (In 2016, when he was first attempting to remake the film, he told an interviewer that it felt "ugly and blasphemous and egomaniacal and disgusting" to take up that project so early into his career.)
tgt_seg: 当那些已经涉足那种深水时，有些人选择了“让我们重新搅动一切”的解决方案。例如，1962年的《卡里加里博士的诊室》的令人遗憾的重拍版，不仅消除了中心人物Cesare the somnambulist，而且还让Caligari花时间给女主角展示令人反感的图片。其他电影制作人选择了更令人困惑的路线，几乎没有改变，例如Gus Van Sant的1998年重拍版的“Psycho”。重拍1922年的杰作的失望的电影观众的风险较小，原因显而易见，但即使如此，导演Robert Eggers在任何一次采访中都清楚地表明，他的新“Nosferatu”正在重新吸引最伟大的默片之一。（在2016年，当他首次尝试重拍这部电影时，他告诉采访者，在他职业生涯早期就开始这个项目，感觉“丑陋、亵渎、自恋和令人作呕”）

src_seg: F. W. Murnau's "Nosferatu: A Symphony of Horror" is itself a remake - an unauthorized adaptation of "Dracula," Bram Stoker's compulsively readable fever dream of a novel - and Murnau and the screenwriter Henrik Galeen retained much of what was arresting about the original while slipping in their own major changes: They're responsible, for example, for the now-set-in-stone tradition that sunlight can destroy the vampire, a notion nowhere in Stoker's book. I likely saw "Nosferatu" at too impressionable an age. I was 6, PBS was showing such things and my babysitter was simply glad I wasn't burning down the house. But I would have been flattened by it whenever I saw it. It was like having felt a draft from a grave. (Its effects were so long-lasting that 30-something years later I published a novel inspired by the film and its production.) The whole thing wasn't so much petrifying as insidiously unsettling, and all of that started with the figure of Nosferatu himself. Max Schreck's performance is, 102 years later, still the benchmark for sinister and dignified repulsiveness. Schreck's vampire has the stillness of a figure in a bad dream or a spider on its web, and the world he inhabits is at times equally disconcerting. After our hero Hutter's first frightening night in Nosferatu's castle, he notices in the mirror that something has bitten his neck, and he smiles.
tgt_seg: F. W. Murnau的《Nosferatu：恐怖交响曲》本身就是重拍版 - 对Bram Stoker的《Dracula》的未经授权改编，这是一本充满阅读的热闹的梦想小说 - 并且Murnau和编剧Henrik Galeen保留了原始作品中令人惊讶的东西，同时也进行了自己的重大改动：例如，他们负责了现在已经成为定石的传统，即阳光可以摧毁吸血鬼，这种想法在Stoker的书中根本不存在。我可能在太早的年龄看了《Nosferatu》，我6岁，PBS正在播放这样的东西，我的保姆只是很高兴我没有烧掉房子。但每次我看到它，我都会被它压扁。这就像从坟墓里感受到一阵风。（它的效果持续了30多年，我出版了一部受这部电影和其制作启发的小说。）整部电影不仅令人恐惧，而且令人不安，而这一切都始于Nosferatu的形象。Max Schreck的表演在102年后仍然是令人毛骨悚然和高贵的厌恶的基准。Schreck的吸血鬼的静止状态就像一个在噩梦中出现的形象或蜘蛛在网上一样，而他居住的世界有时同样令人不安。在Hutter的第一场可怕的夜晚，他在Nosferatu的城堡中，他注意到镜子中有人咬了他的脖子，然后他微笑。

src_seg: But the most destabilizing figure might well be Hutter's wife, Ellen, our heroine, who's again and again shown to be telepathically on the monster's wavelength, even when he's thousands of miles away, so that polarities like good and evil or desire and repulsion seem to just evaporate while we watch. That last aspect alone would seem to land this story in Robert Eggers's wheelhouse. Part of the subversive energy of movies like "The Witch," "The Lighthouse" and "The Northman" derives from what feels like modern takes on historical characters in thrall to dark passions so that the distantly historical is both granted its strangeness and animated by a scrutinizing modern sensibility. At its best, his version both evokes and reconceives Murnau's most brilliant visual ideas. Murnau's masterful use of the opacities of dark archways from which the vampire can emerge and into which he can dissolve is both echoed and made new. Murnau's famously arresting use of shadows to visualize the vampire's defiling reach is reimagined when those shadows in this new version extend themselves in a 360-degree pan that evokes their vertiginous inescapability. And the shadow of the vampire's hand now extends across the entire city, repurposing the most memorable image from Murnau's "Faust."
tgt_seg: 但最具破坏性的角色可能是Hutter的妻子Ellen，我们的女英雄，她一次又一次地被证明是与怪物同步的心灵感应，即使它在成千上万英里之外，这样就使得善与恶或欲望与厌恶似乎在我们观看时就消失了。这个故事的最后一个方面似乎落在了Robert Eggers的手中。像“The Witch”、“The Lighthouse”和“The Northman”这样的电影的部分颠覆性能量来自于对历史人物的现代看法，这些人物被黑暗欲望所困，因此远古的历史既被赋予了其怪异性，又被现代审慎的敏感性所激活。在其最佳状态下，他的版本既唤起了Murnau最精彩的视觉想法，也重新构想了它们。Murnau对暗巷的透明度使用，吸血鬼可以从那里出现，并消失，既被回声，也被赋予了新的生命。Murnau以其令人惊叹的使用阴影来可视化吸血鬼的玷污影响而闻名，在这个新版本中，那些阴影在360度旋转中延伸，唤起了它们无法逃脱的令人不安的性质。吸血鬼的手影现在延伸到整个城市，重新利用了Murnau的《Faust》中最令人难忘的形象。

src_seg: How the "Manosphere" Became Mainstream Entertainment
tgt_seg: “男人圈”如何成为主流娱乐

src_seg: Whenever Bill Belichick, the 72-year-old former head coach of the New England Patriots, goes out in public with his girlfriend, Jordon Hudson, who is exactly one-third his age, they tend to draw attention. It was no different at the 2025 N.F.L. Honors earlier this month. Everything about the red-carpet photos accentuates their Evel Knievel-size age gap: Belichick looks sedately pleased in a maroon blazer, like a car dealer at a Shriners banquet; Hudson beams in a sparkly Cirque du Soleil-style number that covers approximately 12 percent of her torso. That's what most people seemed to notice about the pictures.
tgt_seg: 每当72岁的美国爱国者队前主教练比尔·贝利奇克与他的女友，年龄是他三分之一的乔丹·哈德森一起出现在公众场合时，他们总会吸引人们的注意力。本月早些时候在2025年NFL荣誉颁奖典礼上，他们也未能免俗。红毯上的照片无一例外地突出了他们巨大的年龄差距：贝利奇克身穿深红色西装，看起来心满意足，就像慈善晚宴上的汽车销售员一样；而哈德森则身穿闪闪发光的太阳马戏团风格的礼服，礼服覆盖了她躯干的大约12%的面积。这就是大多数人似乎对这些照片的关注点。

src_seg: But not Dave Portnoy. The founder and owner of Barstool Sports - the Utne Reader for the light-domestic-swilling, backslapping, Zyn-packing, parlay-chasing American male - Portnoy has long been treated as an avatar for everything that elite media is not. Barstool might be considered the outermost ring of the so-called manosphere, the vast realm of male-oriented alternative media that has been credited with the rightward drift of the young male vote. Portnoy - a Trump supporter with a long history of misogynistic comments and bullying, who has been accused of nonconsensually filming women during uncomfortably rough sex - doesn't exactly run away from that label. (He has denied the claims about sexual misconduct and filed a suit against the outlet that published them; it was dismissed.) And what he noticed about the photos of Belichick and Hudson was the clutch Hudson wore, which was shaped like a little football: "Very cool purse from BB's girlfriend," he posted on X. "Football girlfriend purse."
tgt_seg: 但戴夫·波特诺伊却不同。作为Barstool Sports的创始人和所有者——这是一家迎合轻度饮酒、喜欢拍肩膀、嚼Zyn尼古丁袋、热衷于体育投注的美国男性的媒体，被视为精英媒体的对立面。Barstool可以被视为所谓的“男人圈”的最外层，这个男性导向的另类媒体领域被认为导致了年轻男性选民向右翼漂移。波特诺伊是特朗普的支持者，长期发表厌女言论和欺凌他人，并被指控在性行为中未经同意拍摄女性（他否认了关于性行为不检的指控，并对发表这些指控的媒体提起诉讼，但被驳回）。他并不避讳这个标签。对于贝利奇克和哈德森的照片，波特诺伊关注的是哈德森戴的手袋，它被设计成一个小橄榄球的形状：“BB的女朋友的手袋很酷，”他在X平台上发帖说。“橄榄球女友手袋。”

src_seg: It's certainly possible that Portnoy, a die-hard Patriots fan, was being ironic, conveying something like, "I refuse to see anything unusual here." But I would bet that he genuinely did like the purse. I would make that bet because I have spent many hours watching Portnoy's most fascinating nonsports media product, his "One Bite" pizza reviews, and I know about his softer side. He has been doing these reviews for 12 years, though I first encountered them during the pandemic. I was, at that point, ambiently aware of Portnoy, but only for all the stuff people hated about his website: the "Smokeshow of the Day" photos, the army of online "Stoolies" who mobbed his many critics. But if you watch the pizza videos, you're reminded that most of the stuff these controversial media figures do is entirely normal. A lot of the time, it's downright amusing.
tgt_seg: 波特诺伊是爱国者队的铁杆粉丝，他很可能是在表达一种讽刺，就像他在说“我拒绝看到这里有什么不寻常的地方”。但我敢打赌，他真的喜欢这个手袋。我敢这么说，是因为我花了很多时间观看波特诺伊最吸引人的非体育类媒体产品——他的“One Bite”披萨评论，我了解他的温柔的一面。他已经做了12年的披萨评论了，尽管我是在疫情期间才第一次接触到它们。那时，我对波特诺伊已经有所耳闻，但只是因为人们讨厌他的网站的一些内容，比如“每日辣妹”照片，以及他在网上网罗的一群“stoolie”，他们会围攻他的批评者。但如果你观看披萨视频，你会想起这些争议媒体人物所做的大部分事情其实是完全正常的。很多时候，甚至相当有趣。

src_seg: Each episode of "One Bite" begins with Portnoy's walking out the door of the business under consideration, then executing the entirety of his review right out front, sometimes practically blocking foot traffic, often with the proprietor looking on anxiously. Given all this, the concept seems almost cruel: He buys an entire pie but reviews the pizza based on one bite. "One bite," goes the motto. "Everybody knows the rules." The reason for this, Portnoy explained in an early video, is that the response has to be immediate, beneath the level of consciousness, like a "Rotchbloch" test. But Portnoy can never limit himself to one bite, typically finishing about half a slice of molten pizza, blowing big cheekfuls of air on it the way you would for a toddler, balancing the rest of the pie in his other hand as he tries to sort out where it belongs on his 10-point scale.
tgt_seg: 每一集“One Bite”都以波特诺伊走出正在评测的店铺开始，然后在店铺门前完成整个评论，有时几乎挡住了人行道，店主往往焦虑地看着他。鉴于此，这个概念看起来几乎有些残忍：他买了一个完整的披萨，但只根据一口的味道来评论。“一口，”口号是这么说的。“每个人都知道规则。”波特诺伊在早期的视频中解释说，这种反应必须是即刻的，在意识层面之下，就像一种“Rotchbloch”测试。但波特诺伊永远无法限制自己只咬一口，通常会吃掉半片熔化的披萨，用脸颊鼓起一大团空气，就像对一个幼儿一样，同时用另一只手平衡着剩下的披萨，试图在他的10分制评分标准中给它定位。

src_seg: It's certainly possible that Portnoy, a die-hard Patriots fan, was being ironic, conveying something like, "I refuse to see anything unusual here." But I would bet that he genuinely did like the purse. I would make that bet because I have spent many hours watching Portnoy's most fascinating nonsports media product, his "One Bite" pizza reviews, and I know about his softer side. He has been doing these reviews for 12 years, though I first encountered them during the pandemic. I was, at that point, ambiently aware of Portnoy, but only for all the stuff people hated about his website: the "Smokeshow of the Day" photos, the army of online "Stoolies" who mobbed his many critics. But if you watch the pizza videos, you're reminded that most of the stuff these controversial media figures do is entirely normal. A lot of the time, it's downright amusing.
tgt_seg: 当然，波特诺伊作为一名狂热的爱国者球迷，可能是故意讽刺，表达了类似“我拒绝看到这里有任何不寻常之处”的意味。但我敢打赌，他确实喜欢那只手袋。我之所以敢打赌，是因为我花了很多时间观看波特诺伊最引人入胜的非体育媒体产品——他的“One Bite”披萨评论，我了解了他那柔软的一面。他已经做了12年的披萨评论，尽管我是在疫情期间首次接触到他的。那时，我只是对他的网站感到一知半解，但我知道人们讨厌他的网站上的“Smokeshow of the Day”照片，以及他的许多批评者被他的“Stoolies”军团围攻。但如果你看看披萨视频，你会发现这些有争议的媒体人物做的大部分事情都是完全正常的。很多时候，这些事情甚至非常有趣。

src_seg: Each episode of "One Bite" begins with Portnoy's walking out the door of the business under consideration, then executing the entirety of his review right out front, sometimes practically blocking foot traffic, often with the proprietor looking on anxiously. Given all this, the concept seems almost cruel: He buys an entire pie but reviews the pizza based on one bite. "One bite," goes the motto. "Everybody knows the rules." The reason for this, Portnoy explained in an early video, is that the response has to be immediate, beneath the level of consciousness, like a "Rotchbloch" test. But Portnoy can never limit himself to one bite, typically finishing about half a slice of molten pizza, blowing big cheekfuls of air on it the way you would for a toddler, balancing the rest of the pie in his other hand as he tries to sort out where it belongs on his 10-point scale.
tgt_seg: 每一集“One Bite”都以波特诺伊从正在评论的店铺走出开始，然后在门外执行整个评论，有时几乎会阻挡行人，店主常常焦虑地看着。考虑到这一点，这个概念似乎几乎残忍：他买了一整个披萨，但只根据一口来评论。“一口”是他的口头禅。“大家都知道规则。”波特诺伊在早期的一段视频中解释说，这样做是为了让反应立即发生，在无意识的层面，就像“Rotchbloch”测试一样。但波特诺伊从来不能仅仅满足于一口，通常会吃掉半片半熟的披萨，像对待幼儿一样吹满脸颊的空气，同时用另一只手试图弄清楚它在他10分的评分体系中属于哪个位置。

Everything about the red-carpet photos accentuates their Evel Knievel-size age gap: Belichick looks sedately pleased in a maroon blazer, like a car dealer at a Shriners banquet; Hudson beams in a sparkly Cirque du Soleil-style number that covers approximately 12 percent of her torso. That's what most people seemed to notice about the pictures.
tgt_seg: 每当72岁的比尔·贝利奇克（Bill Belichick），前新英格兰爱国者队主教练，与比他小整整三分之一岁的女友乔丹·哈德森（Jordon Hudson）公开露面时，他们总会吸引人们的注意。本月初的2025年NFL荣誉颁奖典礼也不例外。红毯照片上的每一处细节都突显了他们之间巨大的年龄差距：贝利奇克穿着maroonblazer，看起来像是在Shriners宴会上的汽车经销商；而哈德森则身穿闪亮的太阳马戏团风格服装，遮盖了大约12%的躯干。这就是大多数人从照片中注意到的。

src_seg: But not Dave Portnoy. The founder and owner of Barstool Sports - the Utne Reader for the light-domestic-swilling, backslapping, Zyn-packing, parlay-chasing American male - Portnoy has long been treated as an avatar for everything that elite media is not. Barstool might be considered the outermost ring of the so-called manosphere, the vast realm of male-oriented alternative media that has been credited with the rightward drift of the young male vote. Portnoy - a Trump supporter with a long history of misogynistic comments and bullying, who has been accused of nonconsensually filming women during uncomfortably rough sex - doesn't exactly run away from that label. (He has denied the claims about sexual misconduct and filed a suit against the outlet that published them; it was dismissed.) And what he noticed about the photos of Belichick and Hudson was the clutch Hudson wore, which was shaped like a little football: "Very cool purse from BB's girlfriend," he posted on X. "Football girlfriend purse."
tgt_seg: 但戴夫·波特诺伊（Dave Portnoy）却不是这样。作为Barstool Sports的创始人兼所有者——这家公司是为那些喜欢轻度饮酒、拍拍后背、携带Zyn口香糖、追求大奖的美国男性服务的Utne Reader——波特诺伊长期以来一直被视为精英媒体的化身。Barstool可以被认为是所谓的“男性世界观”的最外层，这是一个以男性为导向的替代媒体领域，被认为是年轻男性选民向右倾斜的原因。波特诺伊——一个特朗普支持者，有着长期的厌女症言论和欺凌行为，被指控在性爱过程中非自愿拍摄女性——并不回避这个标签。 (他否认了关于性行为不端的指控，并对发布这些指控的媒体提起诉讼；该诉讼已被驳回。)而他在照片中注意到的是哈德森佩戴的手链，形状像一个小足球：“BB的女朋友的非常酷的手链，”他在X上发帖说。“足球女友手链。”

src_seg: It's certainly possible that Portnoy, a die-hard Patriots fan, was being ironic, conveying something like, "I refuse to see anything unusual here." But I would bet that he genuinely did like the purse. I would make that bet because I have spent many hours watching Portnoy's most fascinating nonsports media product, his "One Bite" pizza reviews, and I know about his softer side. He has been doing these reviews for 12 years, though I first encountered them during the pandemic. I was, at that point, ambiently aware of Portnoy, but only for all the stuff people hated about his website: the "Smokeshow of the Day" photos, the army of online "Stoolies" who mobbed his many critics. But if you watch the pizza videos, you're reminded that most of the stuff these controversial media figures do is entirely normal. A lot of the time, it's downright amusing.
tgt_seg: 波特诺伊，作为一名死忠的爱国者队球迷，很可能是出于讽刺，表达了一种“我拒绝在这里看到任何不寻常之处”的态度。但我敢打赌，他真的喜欢这个手链。我敢打赌，因为我花了许多时间观看波特诺伊最有趣的非体育媒体产品，他的“一口咬定”披萨评论，我知道他的温柔一面。他已经做了12年的这些评论，虽然我在疫情期间第一次遇到它们。当时，我对波特诺伊只是有所耳闻，但只是因为人们讨厌他网站上的所有内容：当天的“Smokeshow”照片，一群在线“Stoolies”骚扰他的许多批评者。但如果你看了披萨视频，你会想起这些有争议的媒体人物所做的大部分事情都是完全正常的。很多时候，这简直很有趣。

src_seg: Each episode of "One Bite" begins with Portnoy's walking out the door of the business under consideration, then executing the entirety of his review right out front, sometimes practically blocking foot traffic, often with the proprietor looking on anxiously. Given all this, the concept seems almost cruel: He buys an entire pie but reviews the pizza based on one bite. "One bite," goes the motto. "Everybody knows the rules." The reason for this, Portnoy explained in an early video, is that the response has to be immediate, beneath the level of consciousness, like a "Rotchbloch" test. But Portnoy can never limit himself to one bite, typically finishing about half a slice of molten pizza, blowing big cheekfuls of air on it the way you would for a toddler, balancing the rest of the pie in his other hand as he tries to sort out where it belongs on his 10-point scale.

Everything about the red-carpet photos accentuates their Evel Knievel-size age gap: Belichick looks sedately pleased in a maroon blazer, like a car dealer at a Shriners banquet; Hudson beams in a sparkly Cirque du Soleil-style number that covers approximately 12 percent of her torso. That's what most people seemed to notice about the pictures.
tgt_seg: 当新英格兰爱国者队前主教练比尔·贝利奇（72岁）和年龄正好是他的三分之一的女友乔登·汉得斯德（Jordon Hudson）在公众中露面时，他们往往会引起人们的注意。 这一月早些时候的 2025 N.F.L. 荣誉也不例外。 关于红地毯照片的一切都凸显了他们的埃维尔·克尼维尔（Evel Knievel）大小的年龄差距：贝利奇穿着棕褐色夹克，看起来像在 shriners 宴会上的汽车经销商；哈德逊穿着闪闪发光的太阳戏团风格服装，覆盖着约 12% 的身体。 这似乎是大多数人注意到的照片的原因。

src_seg: But not Dave Portnoy. The founder and owner of Barstool Sports - the Utne Reader for the light-domestic-swilling, backslapping, Zyn-packing, parlay-chasing American male - Portnoy has long been treated as an avatar for everything that elite media is not. Barstool might be considered the outermost ring of the so-called manosphere, the vast realm of male-oriented alternative media that has been credited with the rightward drift of the young male vote. Portnoy - a Trump supporter with a long history of misogynistic comments and bullying, who has been accused of nonconsensually filming women during uncomfortably rough sex - doesn't exactly run away from that label. (He has denied the claims about sexual misconduct and filed a suit against the outlet that published them; it was dismissed.) And what he noticed about the photos of Belichick and Hudson was the clutch Hudson wore, which was shaped like a little football: "Very cool purse from BB's girlfriend," he posted on X. "Football girlfriend purse."
tgt_seg: 但这并不适用于戴夫·波特诺伊。Barstool Sports 的创办人兼所有者 — — 《Utne Reader》的男性读者 — — 波特诺伊长期以来被视为精英媒体不具备的一切的化身。 Barstool 可能被认为是所谓的“男人圈”的最外层，这是以男性为导向的另类媒体的巨大领域，它被归咎于年轻人投票偏右倾向。 波特诺伊 — — 特朗普支持者、长期发表反女性言论和欺凌行为，曾被指控在尴尬的性交过程中未经同意地拍摄女性 — — 并没有完全逃避这一标签。 (他否认了有关性行为不端的指控，并针对发布这些指控的媒体提起诉讼；该诉讼被驳回) 他注意到贝利奇克和哈德森的照片上，哈德森戴着一个形状像小橄榄球一样的手包：他在 X 上写道：“来自BB女朋友的非常酷的皮包。”“足球女友皮包。

src_seg: It's certainly possible that Portnoy, a die-hard Patriots fan, was being ironic, conveying something like, "I refuse to see anything unusual here." But I would bet that he genuinely did like the purse. I would make that bet because I have spent many hours watching Portnoy's most fascinating nonsports media product, his "One Bite" pizza reviews, and I know about his softer side. He has been doing these reviews for 12 years, though I first encountered them during the pandemic. I was, at that point, ambiently aware of Portnoy, but only for all the stuff people hated about his website: the "Smokeshow of the Day" photos, the army of online "Stoolies" who mobbed his many critics. But if you watch the pizza videos, you're reminded that most of the stuff these controversial media figures do is entirely normal. A lot of the time, it's downright amusing.
tgt_seg: 显然波特诺伊是一位忠实的爱国者队粉丝，他的讽刺意味“我拒绝看到任何不寻常的东西”。 但我敢打赌，他真的喜欢这个钱包。 我愿意打赌，因为我已经花了很多时间观看波特诺伊最迷人的非体育媒体产品，“ One Bite” 的披萨评论，而且我知道他的柔软的一面。 他做了 12 年的评论，尽管我在疫情期间第一次遇到过这些评论。 当时，我对波特诺伊有所认识，但只是因为他网站上的那些人们讨厌的东西：“每日吸烟秀”照片、在线“ Stoolies” 军队，他们袭击了他的许多批评者。 但如果你看披萨视频，就会想起这些有争议的媒体人物做的大部分事情是完全正常的。 很多时候，这简直太有趣了。

src_seg: Each episode of "One Bite" begins with Portnoy's walking out the door of the business under consideration, then executing the entirety of his review right out front, sometimes practically blocking foot traffic, often with the proprietor looking on anxiously. Given all this, the concept seems almost cruel: He buys an entire pie but reviews the pizza based on one bite. "One bite," goes the motto. "Everybody knows the rules." The reason for this, Portnoy explained in an early video, is that the response has to be immediate, beneath the level of consciousness, like a "Rotchbloch" test. But Portnoy can never limit himself to one bite, typically finishing about half a slice of molten pizza, blowing big cheekfuls of air on it the way you would for a toddler, balancing the rest of the pie in his other hand as he tries to sort out where it belongs on his 10-point scale.
tgt_seg: 每集“一口一咬”开始时，波特诺伊从所考虑的商店门口走出去，然后就在前面进行完整的评论，有时几乎挡住了人行道，经常让店主焦虑不已。 鉴于这一切，这个概念似乎几乎是残忍的：他买了一整块馅饼，但只根据一口一咬对披萨进行评价。 “一口一咬”就是它的口号。 “每个人都知道规则。”波特诺伊在一部早期的视频中解释称，原因在于反应必须立即发生，在意识水平之下，就像“Rotchbloch”测试一样。 但波特诺伊永远不能局限于一口一咬，通常会吃完大约一半片熔化过的披萨，像喂婴儿一样吹气，用另一只手平衡剩下的馅饼，试图弄清楚它在 10 分等级表中属于哪个位置。

Another fine evening (ok not really, it's wet and drizzly, but →) to continue exploring my stash of #Rum from #Japan 
Cor Cor again - this time the "Industrial" (アンデユストリエル) red version - which is the one they make from the molasses byproduct of sugar making (as opposed to the previous 'green' agricole that's directly from fermenting the cane juice). 
Just got a small bottle. Quite thick, heavy sugar nose (almost probitas like), but not too sweet. Dreamy daiquiri if you ask me.
tgt_seg:
又是一个美好的夜晚（好吧，其实不是，是个阴雨天，但是→）继续探索我的来自#日本的#朗姆酒收藏
再次品尝Cor Cor - 这次是“Industrial”（アンデユストリエル）红标版本 - 这款是用制糖过程中产生的糖蜜副产品制成的（与之前直接用甘蔗汁发酵的“绿色”农业朗姆酒不同）。 
刚刚买了一小瓶。闻起来有浓厚的糖味（几乎像朗姆酒的原型），但不至于太甜。如果你问我，这是一款梦幻般的代基里鸡尾酒。

src_seg:
Adding to this thread on my #Japanese #Okinawa #Rum exploration
Opened this OneRum bottle intending to daiquiri, but the fragrance or lack prompted me to pull out and get nosy. Smells a bit like Indian palm toddy. Uses sugar just from Ie island. Tempted to say Clairin like but no it's more spirit, vodka or sochu like - thin, smooth with a touch of heat (48%) just a late hint it's sugar distillate. Sochu, awamori sensibilities in making it for sure. (Mizuho Distillery)
1/3
tgt_seg:
继续更新这个关于我的#日本 #冲绳 #朗姆酒探索的帖子
打开这瓶OneRum时，我本打算调制代基里，但它的香气（或者说缺乏香气）促使我拿出来细闻。闻起来有点像印度棕榈酒。使用的是来自伊江岛的糖。想说它像Clairin，但又不完全是 - 它更像白酒或泡盛酒 - 单薄、顺滑，带有一丝辛辣（48%），最后才有一丝糖蒸馏的味道。肯定是在酿造过程中融入了泡盛酒的风格。（Mizuho Distillery）
1/3

Opened this OneRum bottle intending to daiquiri, but the fragrance or lack prompted me to pull out and get nosy. Smells a bit like Indian palm toddy. Uses sugar just from Ie island. Tempted to say Clairin like but no it's more spirit, vodka or sochu like - thin, smooth with a touch of heat (48%) just a late hint it's sugar distillate. Sochu, awamori sensibilities in making it for sure. (Mizuho Distillery)
1/3
tgt_seg:
继续在我的#日本#桔岛#奶狮探索的话题上发帖
打算用这瓶 OneRum 烤 daiquiri，但是香气或者缺乏的提示让我拔出来仔细品味。有点像印度的椰子酒的香气。只使用椐岛的糖。有点想说像克拉林一样，但是实际上更像是精酿、 vodka 或者 sochu 一样 - 细腻，滑滑的，有一点温度（48%），只是稍后有一点甜蜜的提示，这是糖蒸汽蒸馏的产物。精酿、 awamori 的感觉肯定在制造过程中。（Mizuho Distillery）
1/3

src_seg:
3/3
Ok so I did make that #Daiquiri  
2 oz #rum
1 oz fresh squeezed lime juice [wish I had shikuwasa]
¾ oz rich simple syrup
Oh dear f$expletive deleted me - in a well chilled coupe, took a sip and this is exquisite. Close my eyes and aware of the back of my neck calming. 
Didn't expect that. 180⁰ from a more upfront sugary rum.
tgt_seg:
3/3
好吧，我确实做了那个 daiquiri
2 oz #奶狮
1 oz 新鲜榨汁的柠檬汁 [愿望自有石川柠檬]
¾ oz 富糖简单酱
哇哦，真的，在一个好好冷的杯子中喝下去，这是非常精美的。闭上眼睛，感觉后颈部的寒意消失。
没有预期到这一点。与更前面的甜蜜的奶狮相比，完全是 180 度的变化。

src_seg:
Another fine evening (ok not really, it's wet and drizzly, but →) to continue exploring my stash of #Rum from #Japan 
Cor Cor again - this time the "Industrial" (アンデユストリエル) red version - which is the one they make from the molasses byproduct of sugar making (as opposed to the previous 'green' agricole that's directly from fermenting the cane juice). 
Just got a small bottle. Quite thick, heavy sugar nose (almost probitas like), but not too sweet. Dreamy daiquiri if you ask me.
tgt_seg:
又一个美好的夜晚（其实不然，天气潮湿且毛毛雨，但→）继续探索我从#日本带来的#朗姆酒藏酒
再次选择Cor Cor——这次是“工业”（アンデユストリエル）红色版本，这款酒是用制糖过程中的糖蜜副产品制成（与之前直接发酵甘蔗汁的“绿色”农业朗姆酒不同）。
刚刚买了一小瓶。酒体相当浓稠，浓重的糖香（几乎像probitas），但不过于甜腻。在我看来，这是一款梦幻般的达基里。

tgt_seg:

贝尔公司旧网保留了一个用于拨打长途电话的快捷按键！所以，如果一个城市的电话区号以字母“ABC”开头，用户就会被自动拨入长途电话网络，而费用非常高昂。这就是电话区号分开的原因。

src_seg:
So here we go at Bell again, the English alphabethas 26 letters, we have 8 keys. That is 3 and something per key… 
Which letters do we drop. We need to drop two!
Z was the last letter to enter the company thus first to go!
The letter after that is Y… now that is a popular letter in place names, new York anyone? We cannot fire a letter with a perfect track record!
tgt_seg:
我们又来到了贝尔公司，英文字母有26个，键盘上有8个按键。也就是每个按键可以输入3个字母……
我们要删除哪个字母呢？我们需要删除两个！
Z 是最后一位被公司录用的员工，也是第一个被辞退的员工！
下一个字母是“Y”，这个字母在地名中相当常见，就像纽约这个城市。可是我们不能开除有着完美表现记录的字母！

src_seg:
Language experts were hired to eliminate one more letter from the alphabet.
Q (sorry Q not personal) is a special letter, every French person knows Q cannot live without U. So either one had to go. 
Q in the English language has less to do than U, and Q was dropped from the Bell exchange name scheme!
And this kids is why you won’t find it on old telephones.
tgt_seg:
为了从字母表中删除另一个字母，他们还请来了一名语言学专家。
Q（对不起，Q 并非指个人）是一个特别的字母，每一个法国人都知道 Q 不能没有 U。所以，只能去掉其中一个字母。
在英文中，字母 Q 的用处不如字母 U，因此贝尔交换局的命名方案中就不再使用这个字母了！
这也就是为什么你不会在旧式电话上找到这个功能的原因。

Why is even on the iPhone 1 an empty key? Why did USA get +1?
The old Bell network had 1 reserved as a shortcut to the long distance network! So if a town started with the letters ABC you’d… yes automatically get onto the long distance network, at a heavy charge. Thus this separation!
